abstract: 1. Background and Rationale The integration of Artificial Intelligence in Operational Technology (OT) demands strict adherence to safety interlocks and deterministic latency. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer advanced semantic reasoning, their cloud dependence and non-deterministic nature pose risks in safety-critical industrial environments, such as mining and heavy manufacturing. This systematic literature review investigates the deployment of Small Language Models (SLMs) and Agentic Frameworks at the extreme edge. The primary goal is to map how current literature transitions from descriptive AI applications to prescriptive, safety-aware control mechanisms that prevent modal collapse and hallucinations in offline edge hardware. 2. PICOC Framework Population: Edge computing devices (Extreme Edge / Far Edge) deployed in Operational Technology (OT) networks. Intervention: Deployment of Small Language Models (SLMs), Large Language Models (LLMs), or Agentic Frameworks for semantic reasoning and decision-making. Comparison: Cloud-based inference, purely reactive/heuristic control systems, or zero-shot inference without guardrails. Outcomes: Decision accuracy, inference latency, resilience against modal collapse, and adherence to deterministic safety interlocks. Context: Safety-critical industrial environments (e.g., mining, heavy manufacturing) with restricted or non-existent connectivity. 3. Research Questions (RQs) RQ1: What are the predominant architectures for deploying language models (LLMs/SLMs) at the operational edge in safety-critical environments? RQ2: How does the current literature resolve the trade-off between the semantic reasoning capabilities of SLMs and the need for deterministic latency in industrial OT networks? RQ3: Which guardrail mechanisms or admissibility filters are utilized to prevent hallucinations and modal collapse in generative AI-based decision-making at the process control level? 4. Search Strategy The review will cover peer-reviewed literature indexed in major engineering and computing databases, specifically Scopus and IEEE Xplore. The following search string will be applied to Title, Abstract, and Keywords: ("Edge Computing" OR "Edge AI" OR "Extreme Edge" OR "Far Edge") AND ("Language Model*" OR "LLM*" OR "SLM*" OR "Agent*") AND ("Safety-critical" OR "Operational Technology" OR "Industrial" OR "Mining") 5. Eligibility Criteria Inclusion Criteria (IC): IC1: Published between 2021 and 2026. IC2: Peer-reviewed studies (journals or highly ranked conference proceedings). IC3: Studies proposing, implementing, or evaluating generative AI/agentic models on resource-constrained hardware (Edge). Exclusion Criteria (EC): EC1: Review articles, surveys, or secondary studies. EC2: Studies focused exclusively on cloud-based LLM execution with no edge component. EC3: Applications outside the industrial/OT context (e.g., healthcare, finance, education). EC4: Non-peer-reviewed pre-prints (e.g., arXiv) to ensure theoretical rigor. 6. Screening and Data Extraction Strategy The PRISMA workflow will be applied. Following duplicate removal, an initial screening of titles and abstracts will be conducted to exclude irrelevant records based on the ECs. The remaining articles will undergo full-text screening. Data extraction will be performed systematically to address the proposed RQs.
title: Prescriptive Edge AI in Safety-Critical Operational Technology: A Systematic Literature Review Protocol

abstract: Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) process development generates an enormous body of technical information across a multi-stage, knowledge-intensive continuum from drug discovery to commercial manufacturing. This knowledge is traditionally fragmented across functions and heterogeneous formats, causing traceability gaps and significant knowledge-management costs during technology transfer and regulatory filing. We present a modular agentic-AI platform that converts a heterogeneous corpus of process-development documents into a queryable, dual-layer knowledge graph. A base knowledge layer builds a lexical graph with a Document-Section-Chunk hierarchy through lossless ingestion of digital, scanned, handwritten, and multilingual documents, while an intelligence layer extracts ontology-aligned entities and bridges cross-document concepts through a provenance-anchored domain graph. LLM agents operate across both layers, selecting the retrieval path best suited to each question. We evaluate the lexical layer with a novel three-tier protocol measuring the deployment-fidelity of a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system on proprietary data, demonstrated on 505 questions curated from 38 development reports of a Sanofi small-molecule program. Tier-1 multiple-choice accuracy of 95% signals strong platform reliability; the stricter Tier-2 LLM-judge pass rate of 85%, which degrades on comparative and corpus-wide questions, reveals a failure taxonomy that Tier-1 accuracy alone fails to capture. A router agent selects between layers according to question type. We anticipate this protocol will enable future designers of agentic platforms to assess their systems against nonpublic databases, and that graph-based architectures will see broader adoption in pharma as a means of transforming fragmented document repositories into structured process intelligence.
title: From Document Silos to Process Intelligence: A Multi-Layer Knowledge Graph for CMC Process Development

abstract: Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) is being rapidly adopted in U.S. industries across various sectors. While practitioners and academics recognize many benefits of adopting MBSE, industries also report challenges such as limited tool expertise and a shortage of skilled personnel. Highlighting the difficulties in industry adoption of MBSE, prior research by the authors identified challenges such as tool limitations, knowledge gaps, cultural and political barriers, costs, and the level of customer understanding and acceptance of MBSE practices. Additionally, another study by the authors points out a gap between industry demands for MBSE skills in new hires and the current academic training programs. To further assess the MBSE industry’s workforce needs, this paper introduces a two-phase method for the Structured Extraction of MBSE competencies using large language models based on current workforce demands from LinkedIn job postings. Phase 1 involved extracting 1960 job descriptions from LinkedIn using the term “model-based systems engineer.” In phase 2, large language models (LLMs) employing deep transformer architectures were used to transform unstructured text into structured data. An AI agent was used as an autonomous software layer to manage every interaction between the raw dataset from Phase 1 and the LLM. Supported by the analyzed data, a competency framework is proposed that summarizes the tools, technical skills, and soft skills expected of a model-based systems engineer by the industry. The framework is designed to include core competencies shared across all MBSE roles, with specific competencies tailored for aerospace & defense, manufacturing and automotive, and software and IT sectors.
title: Industry-Driven Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) Workforce Competencies—An AI-Based Competency Extraction Framework

abstract: The design of power electronic converters is a multi-physics optimization challenge that has traditionally resisted the high levels of automation seen in digital VLSI. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising interface for capturing high-level design intent, they inherently lack the domain understanding required to generate manufacturing-ready hardware, often resulting in hallucinations and invalid netlists. This paper presents a novel, autonomous multi-agent framework that orchestrates the end-to-end design of power electronic circuits from natural language specifications to clean Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) without fine-tuning the underlying LLMs. The proposed methodology utilizes a constrained environment to bridge the stochastic gap between generative AI and rigid Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. The logical validity of the circuit is ensured by deploying specialized agents for device specification, component selection, SKiDL-based netlist generation, and layout completion. The framework is validated through the autonomous generation of a 400V 3-phase converter for a variable frequency drive. Results demonstrate that while the system achieves 100% logical connectivity and automated routing, transitioning from logical correctness to physics-aware layout optimization and adhering to creepage and clearance requirements remains a critical frontier. The study concludes that pairing LLM agents with deterministic auto routers solves the connectivity problem but requires further integration of physics-based feedback loops to meet the requirements of commutation loop inductance, thermal management, creepage, and clearance requirements. Additionally, it also details the placement limitations within the schematic and flags any components that have not been included.
title: Power Circuit AI: Designing Power Electronic Circuits for Motor Drives with Generative Artificial Intelligence

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and formal verification and validation (V&V) are two of the most consequential areas in safety-critical systems engineering, and they interact in a dual way: AI is increasingly used to support V&V, while V&V is increasingly applied to certify AI components whose high-dimensional and emergent behaviors resist classical methods. This study provides one of the first comprehensive bibliometric and science-mapping analyses of AI-assisted V&V for safety-critical systems over 2016–2026, combining, for the first time, Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection into a single PRISMA 2020-compliant corpus of 425 documents. Descriptive bibliometrics, keyword co-occurrence and thematic mapping, trend-topic detection, and logistic lifecycle modelling reveal a field growing at 21.8% annually, mobilizing 1249 authors across 54 countries and organized into four thematic communities, formal verification with machine learning, model checking with agentic AI and large language models, and AI-driven runtime monitoring of cyber-physical systems, with large language models, theorem proving, and AI-systems verification as the youngest themes. Findings are situated against emerging AI-governance regimes, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, the United States NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and ISO/IEC 42001. Beyond mapping, the study contributes the AI-Verification Assurance Framework (AVAF), a three-layer instrument that codes each study by verification direction, method, and property, grades the assurance it demonstrates on an A0–A4 scale, and maps it to certification regimes; AVAF is calibrated and pilot-tested on a stratified, subsample (intra-coder test–retest Cohen’s κ = 0.84). Its application reveals a certifiability gap: assurance concentrates in bounded-formal and statistical tiers, and no study in the coded calibration subsample attains a complete formal guarantee over a realistic model or certifiable, tool-qualified evidence (A4). The paper closes with a six-point research agenda on the certification, scalability, and multi-domain transfer of AI-assisted verification.
title: Artificial Intelligence for Verification and Validation of Safety-Critical Systems: A Bibliometric Science-Mapping Study and an Assurance-Level Framework (AVAF) (2016–2026)
Credibility-Aware Demand Response Continuation and Regime-Switching Market Operation in Multi-Energy Microgrids under Hybrid Cyber Threats and Dynamic Uncertainty

abstract: This paper examines how intelligent technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, autonomous systems, robotics, digital twins, the Internet of Things, edge and cloud computing, knowledge graphs, large language models, decision intelligence, agentic AI, and cyber-physical systems, are changing the foundations of competitive strategy. Classical strategy theories, including the resource-based view, Porter's positioning framework, transaction cost economics, and dynamic capabilities, were built for environments in which human judgment, physical assets, and comparatively stable industry structures determined firm performance. Those assumptions hold less well once intelligent technologies become embedded in decision-making, learning, innovation, and value creation across the firm. Drawing on strategic management, information systems, and organizational theory research, this paper argues that classical frameworks remain partly valid but need conceptual extension rather than outright replacement. It develops an original model, the Intelligent Strategy Capability Framework (ISCF), which explains how lasting advantage arises from the interaction of strategic intelligence, human judgment, AI-augmented decision capability, organizational learning, digital resource orchestration, adaptive innovation, knowledge integration, platform and ecosystem strategy, trust and responsible AI, strategic agility, institutional adaptability, and governance capability. The paper discusses managerial and policy implications and sets out directions for future research on strategy in technology-intensive organizations. The central claim is that competitive advantage in an AI-enabled economy depends less on owning intelligent technology and more on the organizational capacity to combine machine intelligence with human judgment under conditions of fast diffusion and rising institutional scrutiny.
title: Rethinking Competitive Strategy for a World Driven by Intelligent Technologies
venue: Scholedge International Journal of Business Policy & Governance

abstract: Abstract Data-driven techniques such as large language models have proved astonishingly powerful, yet progress with cyber-physical systems such as robots has been slower. The usual explanation is insufficient training data. This paper considers a more fundamental possibility: knowledge acquired through observation differs from knowledge acquired through embodied interaction. Using Shannon information theory, I distinguish the information observed about a physical object from the information contained in that object. Under continuum models of physics, an exact physical state cannot be represented by any finite sequence of bits, while every noisy measurement reveals only finitely many bits. It is therefore a mistake to infer from the digital representability of observations that physical reality itself is digital. Interaction does not eliminate this limitation, but it enables an agent to correlate its actions with their consequences and thereby construct a causal model of itself in the world. This may explain why some capabilities cannot be learned from observational data alone: learning to ride a bicycle may require getting on one, even for a robot. Cyber-physical systems, which embed computational processes into physical ones, are therefore fundamentally richer than computational processes alone.
title: Is Information Digital? A Defense of Reality

abstract: Recent advances in foundation models, multimodal learning, reasoning-oriented large language models, agenticworkflows, and edge AI have expanded the capabilities of artificial intelligence systems. However, practical decision-makingremains brittle because many systems optimize prediction quality while under-modeling intervention effects, uncertainty,safety constraints, latency budgets, and human accountability. This paper introduces AEGIS-DM, an adaptive, edge-aware,governed, interventional, and safe decision-making framework designed for AI systems deployed across emerging technologysettings including agentic assistants, cyber-physical systems, healthcare decision support, and enterprise automation. Theframework combines five layers: multimodal state representation, predictive scoring, causal effect estimation, simulator- orplanner-based long-horizon optimization, and a governance layer for calibration, fairness, policy checks, logging, and humanoverride. We further propose a cross-domain evaluation protocol using public resources such as Adult, D4RL, WebShop,ALFWorld, MIMIC-IV Demo, NASA CMAPSS, and M5, together with open-source tooling including OpenAI Evals,Responsible AI Toolbox, OpenSpiel, RecSim NG, Stable-Baselines3, and RLlib. Because this manuscript is a methods-andbenchmark contribution, the quantitative section reports deterministic scenario-based simulation results under the statedprotocol rather than production deployment measurements. Under the reference protocol, the proposed hybrid approach isexpected to outperform rule-based, supervised-only, offline-RL-only, and prompt-only agent baselines in composite decisionquality and robustness while maintaining substantially better latency and cost than cloud-only frontier-model pipelines.
title: Decision Intelligence for AI and Emerging Technologies: The AEGIS-DM Framework for Trustworthy, CostAware, and Low-Latency Decision Making
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: The increasing integration of distributed energy resources (DERs) and modern communication technologies is transforming residential energy systems into dynamic cyber–physical networks. While DERs enable flexible and decentralized energy generation, they also introduce variability and uncertainty in supply. In addition, dynamic electricity pricing, diverse user behaviors, and emerging peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading mechanisms increase the complexity of residential energy management. The deployment of advanced communication infrastructures further exposes these systems to cyber-physical threats such as false data injection (FDI) attacks. This thesis develops an actor-critic reinforcement learning (RL)-based framework for intelligent, adaptive, and secure residential energy systems. The proposed framework integrates three interconnected layers: smart home energy management, decentralized P2P energy trading, and cybersecurity protection against FDI attacks. First, a multi-agent fuzzy actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed for smart home energy management systems (HEMS). In this framework, smart appliances and subsystems are modeled as autonomous agents that learn optimal energy usage policies under dynamic electricity prices and uncertain environmental conditions. The proposed approach jointly minimizes electricity cost and maximizes occupant comfort while maintaining scalability. Fuzzy logic is incorporated to effectively handle continuous state and action spaces and to capture uncertainties in user preferences and consumption patterns. Second, smart homes are enabled to participate in continuous double-auction P2P energy trading markets using a hierarchical actor-critic reinforcement learning framework. The lower-level policy manages household energy consumption and storage operations, while the higher-level policy allows buyer and seller agents to learn strategic bidding behaviors in decentralized markets. This hierarchical structure captures cooperative–competitive interactions among participants while preserving privacy. Third, to protect system integrity, reinforcement-learning-based anomaly detection mechanisms are developed to identify FDI attacks in both HEMS and P2P energy trading environments. The proposed label-free detection approach integrates multi-head self-attention mechanisms, adaptive threshold learning, and knowledge distillation techniques. By leveraging graph-based representation learning and large language model (LLM) reasoning for reward shaping, the framework enables scalable, decentralized, and adaptive detection of evolving cyberattacks without requiring historical attack labels.
title: Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning-Based Secure Energy Management and Trading for Smart Homes

abstract: This standards position paper presents Execution Governance (EG) as a complementary pre-execution authorization layer for AI-enabled actions, autonomous systems, agentic AI, cyber-physical systems, and high-consequence digital workflows. It explains how EG addresses the structural question of whether a specific proposed action may be authorized to produce a governed effect before that effect materializes. The paper positions EG alongside existing AI governance, risk management, ethical design, and agent-related frameworks, including ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, IEEE 7000, and W3C agent-related community discussions. It argues that these frameworks are necessary but do not, by themselves, define a distinct execution-time authorization boundary for individual proposed actions. EG is therefore presented as a complementary structural layer, not as a replacement for existing standards or governance frameworks. This document is part of the Execution Governance v1.0.1 Public Release Series. It is a conceptual standards position paper for public discussion and pre-standardization research. It is not an ISO, IEC, IEEE, NIST, or W3C standard, specification, certification scheme, conformance model, or implementation guide, and it is not endorsed by those organizations.
title: Execution Governance as a Pre-Execution Authorization Layer v1.0.1
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Modern communication networks are experiencing a rapid transformation driven by the exponential growth of data traffic, the growing number of latency-sensitive applications, and the integration of heterogeneous computing and communication resources. Applications such as Large-Language Models (LLMs), real-time video analytics, extended reality (XR), industrial automation, and connected vehicles impose strict requirements on latency, reliability, scalability, and security. At the same time, computation and intelligence are increasingly moving from centralized cloud infrastructures toward the network edge, bringing new challenges for resource management, network control, and system security. Emerging communication technologies such as reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and terahertz communication, together with the integration of AI and machine learning into network operations, further increase the complexity of future 6G networks. This thesis follows a holistic approach that combines mathematical modeling, data-driven optimization, reinforcement learning, security and resilience analysis, and intent-based automation, with the goal of enabling autonomous and adaptive control in edge to cloud infrastructures. First, the thesis develops mathematical models for analyzing and optimizing emerging networking technologies. These include optimization frameworks for the placement of deep neural network models in edge-computing environments, analytical models for frequency hopping optimization in LoRa networks, and data-driven channel estimation methods for terahertz communication systems. In addition, reliability-aware resource allocation and path selection models are introduced for RIS-assisted wireless networks. Second, the thesis investigates learning-based mechanisms for optimizing distributed edge networks. The proposed approaches include traffic prediction, topology change detection, and reinforcement learning methods for automated serverless scaling and machine learning model lifecycle management in edge-to-cloud systems. Third, the thesis advances traditional security mechanisms toward resilience and antifragility in future 6G networks. It introduces physical-layer vulnerability models for optical networks under jamming attacks, learning-based detection and mitigation schemes for WDM systems, and reliability analysis for RIS-assisted wireless links under hardware failures and environmental blockages. Finally, the thesis investigates Intent-Based Networking (IBN) as a key paradigm for automated network control and extends it toward learning-driven and agentic AI orchestration. It introduces mechanisms for intent translation, benchmarking ML workloads on heterogeneous hardware, intent drift detection, and intent security assurance. Thus, a multi-agent orchestration architecture is proposed in which specialized agents collaboratively interpret intents, monitor infrastructure, plan actions, and execute orchestration decisions. Finally, this thesis provides an integrated framework for modeling, optimizing, securing, and automating next-generation communication networks, contributing to the development of autonomous, intelligent, and secure 6G networking systems capable of supporting complex edge-to-cloud infrastructures.
title: Performance Analysis and Optimization of Data-Driven AI Methods in Next Generation Networking

abstract: Abstract The United States defense and critical manufacturing industrial base currently faces a systemic "Capital-Efficiency Gap," where the rigid, deterministic logic of legacy Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems fails to align financial liquidity with the velocity of stochastic geopolitical signals. This operational misalignment creates profound vulnerabilities in supply chains for high-value, long-lead assets essential to national security. This Technical Report introduces the "Readiness Protocol," a decentralized multi-agent framework designed as a non-invasive intelligent overlay for legacy IT infrastructure. Synergizing Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) with Large Language Model (LLM) semantic processing, the architecture utilizes three autonomous agents—Inventory, Credit, and Strategic Procurement—to optimize the order-to-cash cycle under uncertainty. Monte Carlo simulations (N=1000) demonstrate that the protocol achieves a 98.9% Service Level and reduces average backorder duration by 48% compared to standard policies. Furthermore, the system demonstrates a Capital Utilization Efficiency of 5.15x, offering Small and Medium-sized Manufacturers (SMMs) a data-driven pathway to finance resilience without depleting operating cash. Source code and simulation data available at: https://github.com/trahulkumar/GovSignal-Connect
title: The Readiness Protocol: Autonomous Capital Synchronization for Critical Infrastructure Supply Chains
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: A Survey on Collision Avoidance Algorithms for Multi-robot Systems
venue: International Journal of Control Automation and Systems

abstract: The Deterministic Autonomous Infrastructure Governance System (DAIGS) architecture was originally designed to govern massive, safety-critical industrial environments—from nuclear fusion reactors to uncrewed aerospace platforms. However, the rapid proliferation of consumer-facing Large Language Models (LLMs) and local agentic ecosystems introduces a structurally different class of adversarial threats: prompt injection, toxic content generation, unauthorized data exfiltration, and hallucination-driven corruption of Personally Identifiable Information (PII). I present Lume-Omni, a consumer and edge-focused adaptation of the DAIGS architecture that proves deterministic governance invariants can be mathematically and efficiently enforced within browser sandboxes, WebAssembly (WASM) modules, and constrained mobile endpoints. By framing the consumer application state—including DOM boundaries, prompt envelopes, and data-access layers—as a bounded control surface governed by Lume’s deterministic engine, I establish mathematically provable immunity against prompt-driven exploitation. The architecture introduces six consumer-specific state layers, eleven deterministic invariants, edge-executed Ed25519 runtime certificates, PII exfiltration envelopes, and faceted personality synchronization that safely bridges micro-consumer instances to the broader macroeconomic Trust Layer graph. Lume-Omni bridges the mathematical rigor of industrial cyber-physical safety with the high-throughput, low-latency requirements of everyday web interaction, proving that deterministic governance is not merely an industrial luxury but a mathematical necessity for the consumer internet.
title: Lume-Omni: Deterministic Autonomous Infrastructure Governance for Consumer and Edge Ecosystems
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: We consider economic theory from the perspective of a total automation economy, one with no human involvement in production either in manufacturing or in management. One can naturally ask whether a total automation economy is fundamentally a centrally planned economy or, alternatively, whether efficiency demands decentralization into local decisions by competing agents -- agentic production. A soviet economist, Leonid Kantorovich, developed linear programming as a method companies or governments can use to optimize production. Ironically, he is also generally credited with showing that the most efficient production is achieved through decentralization -- a free market economy with competing agents. Here we review Kantorovich's dualization in detail. We take the objective of the economy to be maximizing production weighted by (human) market price. A fundamental issue is whether an automated pursuit of this objective might have alignment vulnerabilities as the economy evolves. Another question is whether dualization provides insight into the utility of agentic AI systems (multi-agent AI systems) generally.
title: Alignment of a Total Automation Economy

abstract: The Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System (JCIDS) was created as a means to overhaul military procurement processes. Ideally, the requirements development process is meant to take a total of 2-4 years from concept to manufacturing. However the actual length of concept development is much longer. As a result, technologies that are conceptualized through the analytical process often enter the acquisition too late to need for the warrior. To reduce the lengthy timeline in requirements development, we used Large Language Models (LLMs) to conduct the necessary research and synthesize documents that abide by strict JCIDS guidelines. Prompt engineering can achieve these results as a proof of concept. However, the output responses lack the content length and depth necessary to pass through the requirements validation process. Therefore, a combination of agentic workflows, prompt engineering, and sufficient context is needed to achieve the desired outcomes. This project utilizes a novel framework to derive Capabilities Based Assessments (CBAs) at an approximate 80 percent readiness level requiring the final steps of validation and verification by subject matter experts.
title: RAIMOND Requirements AI for Military Operational Needs Development

abstract: In the face of volatile oil prices and an accelerating global energy transition, Kuwait's energy sector stands at a crossroads where effective knowledge management (KM) has become essential to competitive and sustainable industrial operations. This review examines the role of KM in fostering innovation, efficiency and informed decision-making within energy organisations, and the tools and technologies that support it. It gives particular attention to how generative AI (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs), through techniques such as retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs and AI agents, are reshaping KM practice. Drawing on Kuwait's national energy initiatives, the paper sets out the principal opportunities and challenges for KM in the country. To our knowledge, it is the first review to connect GenAI-enabled KM with Kuwait's energy sector and Vision 2035; it proposes an integrative framework mapping GenAI techniques to the knowledge management cycle, grounds the framework in evidence from manufacturing deployments, sets out how it should be evaluated, and outlines a research agenda for the continued, technology-enabled growth of the sector.
title: Knowledge management in the age of generative AI : opportunities and challenges for Kuwait’s energy sector
venue: Strathprints: The University of Strathclyde institutional repository (University of Strathclyde)

abstract: In modern manufacturing processes, product quality and productivity often depend on skilled operators who use their undocumented experience to finetune process parameters in real time. This form of intuitive knowledge is rarely captured or formalized and exists mainly as personal intuition. As these skilled operators retire, the loss of tacit expertise in factory operation widens the gap in process optimization and leads to inefficiencies. This paper presents an AI-driven, integrated framework that captures, stores, and leverages tacit domain knowledge to enable adaptive process optimization. The AI system consists of agentic Large Language Models (LLMs) and a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to form a graph-based AI reasoning framework. The agentic LLM extracts information from unstructured sources (operator notes, machine configuration logs, manuals) and serves as a knowledge-capture and analysis system that continuously interacts with users to structure, contextualize, and store domain knowledge for downstream process optimization. Next, the GNN model learns the latent interdependencies among process parameters, after which an optimization process is built on top of the GNN to estimate changes for an optimized configuration. To validate the proposed AI framework, we demonstrated a finetuning process for a press-brake operation at Cincinnati Incorporated, a manufacturer of metal fabrication equipment. The results from the case study demonstrate the AI system’s ability to capture expert domain-specific knowledge and provide interpretable feedback for adjusting machine configuration. It also shows a significant reduction in setup time and fewer trial-and-error operations for the press brake machine.
title: Tacit Domain Knowledge Extraction and AI-Driven Learning Framework for Optimization of Factory Operations

abstract: We present PICasso, an AI-assisted framework for automated synthesis, verification, and optimization of photonic integrated circuits (PICs) from natural-language specifications. PICasso couples a structured NL -> YAML -> GDS generation pipeline with PDK aware knowledge injection, automated placement and routing, DRC/LVS validation, and SAX-based photonic simulation. To systematically evaluate AI-driven photonic design, we introduce PIC-Set, a benchmark of 36 parameterized PIC design tasks spanning core photonic primitives and multi-component circuits. Using PIC-Set, we benchmark several state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs) under a unified evaluation protocol, including new metrics such as structural and functional $Spec@k$, optimization efficiency, and robustness under perturbations. Across the benchmark, PICasso significantly improves end-to-end specification satisfaction compared to vanilla LLM generation. Structural $Spec@3$ reaches up to 92.7% and functional $Spec@3$ up to 52% on high-complexity circuits. In addition, PICasso consistently reduces circuit insertion loss, lowering the mean loss from 4.98 dB to 3.25 dB (1.74 dB improvement) through simulation-guided optimization. These results demonstrate that structured domain constraints, physical verification, and simulation feedback transform LLMs from brittle netlist generators into practical PIC design agents capable of producing manufacturable layouts with competitive runtimes relative to manual GUI-based workflows.
title: PICasso: An AI-Enabled Design Framework for Autonomous Optimization of Silicon Photonic Devices

abstract: Data science plays a critical role in transforming complex data into actionable insights across numerous domains. Recent developments in large language models (LLMs) and artificial intelligence (AI) agents have significantly automated data science workflow. However, it remains unclear to what extent AI agents can match the performance of human experts on domain-specific data science tasks, and in which aspects human expertise continues to provide advantages. We introduce AgentDS, a benchmark and competition designed to evaluate both AI agents and human-AI collaboration performance in domain-specific data science. AgentDS consists of 17 challenges across six industries: commerce, food production, healthcare, insurance, manufacturing, and retail banking. We conducted an open competition involving 29 teams and 80 participants, enabling systematic comparison between human-AI collaborative approaches and AI-only baselines. Our results show that current AI agents struggle with domain-specific reasoning. AI-only baselines perform below the top quartile of competition participants, while the strongest solutions arise from human-AI collaboration. These findings challenge the narrative of complete automation by AI and underscore the enduring importance of human expertise in data science, while illuminating directions for the next generation of AI. Visit the AgentDS website here: https://agentds.org/ and open source datasets here: https://huggingface.co/datasets/lainmn/AgentDS .
title: AgentDS Technical Report: Benchmarking the Future of Human-AI Collaboration in Domain-Specific Data Science
Trust-Conditioned Bounded Continuation for Resilient Demand Response in Renewable-Integrated Multi-Energy Microgrids with Heterogeneous Energy Storage

abstract: The rapid diffusion of data‑driven automation and agentic AI systems is reshaping the foundations of work, decision‑making, and human–technology interaction. As organizations move toward Society 5.0— Japan’s vision for a human-centered “super smart” society in which cyber-physical intelligence augments human capability across economic and social systems—there is an urgent need for operational architectures that are not only technologically capable but also fundamentally human‑centric. This paper presents an applied model using Intelligent Operations framework that integrates agentic AI, enterprise data fabric, human‑in‑the‑loop governance, and secure multi‑system orchestration, and enterprise digital twins that simulate processes and operational states for context-aware decision support. The result is an adaptive socio‑technical system that enhances human decision‑making rather than replacing it, while simultaneously enabling automation at operational scale.The research builds on fieldwork across finance, supply chain, HR, and complex asset‑intensive environments, where organizational processes are distributed across heterogeneous platforms such as ERP, HCM, workflow systems, enterprise data lakes, RPA tools, and emerging AI orchestration layers. Traditional human‑computer interaction models are insufficient in these environments because workers face fragmented data landscapes, inconsistent process execution, and increasing cognitive load. The proposed Intelligent Operations framework addresses these pain points by introducing an orchestration layer that harmonizes data, interprets context (including real-time insights from digital twin models), and deploys agentic AI workers capable of completing multi‑step tasks across systems.A key contribution of this work is the definition of agentic AI in enterprise socio‑technical ecosystems—AI agents equipped not only with language models and planning capability but also with secure access to enterprise systems through structured patterns such as passthrough APIs, workflow orchestration, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and agent‑to‑agent (A2A) collaboration. Rather than relying on brittle rule‑based workflows, the agents dynamically interpret goals, assess context, and plan actionable sequences while maintaining traceability, decision lineage, and auditability. This supports a new form of “digital labor” that works alongside human employees to augment cognitive, administrative, and analytical tasks. However, the framework insists on human‑in‑the‑loop governance, recognizing that human oversight remains essential for ethical, safe, and responsible AI deployment. The DMO acts as a security and compliance boundary—enforcing identity controls, audit trails, approval checkpoints, policy enforcement, and anomaly detection throughout the agentic automation lifecycle. This hybrid model ensures that automation amplifies human capability without bypassing institutional safeguards or creating new forms of risk.The paper also discusses the human‑centric business implications: reduced cognitive load for knowledge workers, increased transparency of decision processes, improvements in cross‑functional collaboration, and the redefinition of roles as humans transition from transactional executors to supervisors, interpreters, and strategic actors. Proposed framework becomes the backbone for Society 5.0 organizational design—linking people, processes, data, and intelligent systems through a unified operational fabric.This research demonstrates that when designed with ergonomics, human values, and socio‑technical principles at the center, agentic AI become powerful enablers of human‑centric, resilient, and adaptive enterprises.
title: Deliver cross-process automation across Finance, HR, Procurement by orchestrating actions across diverse systems -powered by AI & governed workflows
AI Enhanced Quality Assurance Reporting of Surface Deviation Data in Optical 3D Inspection
venue: IFIP advances in information and communication technology

title: Use of AI-Powered Technologies for Review of Environmental Regulations
Embodied Intelligence

abstract: Does the amount of relevant context in a language model's window act as a knob on the novelty of its output, and is there an optimal input-to-window ratio? Using a controlled ideation task with embedding-based novelty and multi-judge groundedness metrics across four models (gemma2:9b through a frontier model), we find: (1) relevant context injected as neutral reference — with no instruction to be original — reliably moves ideation off the mainstream answer, replicating across every family (+49% to +147%), with an isolation design ruling out the implicit-instruction confound; (2) the effect is a saturating switch, not a tunable dial — there is no optimal ratio, novelty saturating within a few hundred tokens of relevant context; and (3) this absolute threshold is scale-invariant, if anything earlier on the stronger model (~300 vs ~800 tokens). A three-judge groundedness protocol (fast LLM, strong LLM, then a blinded human tiebreaker) finds groundedness flat across load (no coherence cost) and, as a second contribution, that automated LLM groundedness judges correlate near zero with a human rater and systematically over-rate on speculative ideation — manufacturing a spurious high-load 'erosion' that only the human pass caught. A cautionary result for LLM-as-judge evaluation. Scope: all evaluation rests on automated proxies plus a single generalist human rater; authoritative judgment of the ideas' quality, originality, and field-specific soundness would require domain experts in each area (a sleep scientist; product and business practitioners), flagged as the essential next step. Our metrics establish the load-response shape, not expert-graded creative value. Authorship: Cristian Ruvalcaba and the Saluca Agentic AI Research Team (Saluca LLC). Code and data: https://github.com/saluca-labs/context-load-novelty . Not peer-reviewed. AI disclosure. This work was produced with an agentic AI research apparatus operated by Saluca Labs. The apparatus drafted, searched and analysed under direction, and is credited as a contributor. Cristian Ruvalcaba is the human author and is accountable for the content. No AI system is listed as an author, because authorship entails accountability that a model cannot hold.
title: Relevant Context-Load as a Saturating Novelty Knob in Language Models: A Cross-Family Study
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) have rapidly evolved from stand-alone text-only large language models (LLMs) into multi-capable agents with integrated reasoning, tool use, and multimodal abilities (e.g., GPT-4, Grok, Google Gemini). These advanced systems promise to tackle complex real-world tasks, but evaluating their performance in practical industrial scenarios remains challenging. Existing benchmarks such as GAIA [1], BFCL [2], and MageBench [3] each focus on a subset of required skills (general question-answering, function calling, or multimodal reasoning) and do not reflect the integrated challenges of industrial applications. To address this gap, we present the PracticalAI Benchmark, a comprehensive evaluation suite for AI systems in realistic industrial environments. PracticalAI tasks demand a combination of capabilities: multi-step logical reasoning for problem-solving, tool usage via API calls to interact with simulated sensors and actuators, processing of image and video inputs, and web search integration to verify real-time technical data. Unlike traditional evaluations that emphasize response correctness, PracticalAI prioritizes execution accuracy – measuring whether an AI agent can autonomously execute the correct sequence of tool calls to accomplish each task. All tasks run in high-fidelity simulated industrial environments, ensuring safe yet realistic testing of an agent’s ability to plan and act autonomously. Although developed for industrial engineering use cases (e.g., manufacturing processes), the PracticalAI framework is broadly applicable to other domains requiring autonomous agents, including IT operations, software system management, and logistics.Artificial intelligence (AI) have rapidly evolved from stand-alone text-only large language models (LLMs) into multi-capable agents with integrated reasoning, tool use, and multimodal abilities (e.g., GPT-4, Grok, Google Gemini). abstract: Recent breakthroughs in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and emerging world models have dramatically advanced Embodied AI. Yet, while agents can now perform complex autonomous tasks in controlled settings, deploying them in unstructured, dynamic, and human-centric environments requires a fundamental leap in how they perceive and interact with the world and human. To operate alongside humans, in applications like elderly care, co-working in warehouses and industrial automation, agents must master multimodal interaction beyond perception. The Tutorial on Human-centric Embodied Multimodal Interaction(HEMI) focuses on three core pillars regarding embodied multimodal interaction: i) Multimodal Perception & Reasoning: how agents fuse multimodal sensory inputs (visual, spatial, linguistic) to comprehend the physical world, identifying critical uncertainty and confusion, ensuring their actions are executable, effective, and safe; ii) Proactive Multimodal Interaction: To resolve ambiguous human intents and prevent physical risks, agents must proactively interact with users, leveraging both verbal and non-verbal cues to clarify goals; iii) Personalized Multimodal Interaction: interpreting situated contexts to adapt agent behaviors, actions, and communication styles according to individual user preferences. By bridging vision-language representation, advanced multimodal human-agent interaction, and the social sciences, the HEMI tutorial establishes an interdisciplinary foundation for researchers with scientific and technical basis required to build intelligent, collaborative, and trustworthy embodied agents in the shared physical world. Dedicated website: hemi-tutorial.github.io
title: Tutorial on Human-centric Embodied Multimodal Interaction (HEMI) in conjunction with ICMI’26

abstract: The rapid proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs), rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems, and battery energy storage has catalyzed a paradigm shift from traditional centralized power distribution toward decentralized, prosumerdriven peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading.This paper presents a comprehensive framework for an AI-Optimized Smart Local Grid (AI-SLG) designed to facilitate efficient, secure, and costeffective P2P energy trading.The proposed system integrates multiple artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies-including reinforcement learning, fuzzy Q-learning, agentic AI, and ensemble machine learning-with blockchain-based smart contracts, Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure, and real-time demand response mechanisms.A layered architecture is introduced comprising a physical grid layer, a cyber-physical control layer, and a decentralized virtual market layer.The pricing mechanism is governed by dynamic supply-demand ratios, while market clearing is achieved through double auction mechanisms implemented as Ethereum smart contracts.Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AI-SLG framework achieves up to 40% reduction in energy trading costs, 21% reduction in operational expenditure (OPEX), and significant improvements in renewable energy utilization and grid stability.The integration of fog computing, LoRaWAN-based IoT cluster zooming, and agentic AI enables autonomous, scalable virtual microgrid formation without altering the physical grid topology.This work addresses critical challenges in P2P trading including privacy preservation, voltage regulation, fault management, and network charge identification, thereby advancing the state-of-the-art toward fully autonomous, resilient, and sustainable smart energy communities.
authors: Vikas K S Vikas K S
title: AI-Optimized Smart Local Grid for Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading System
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT

abstract: To manage their exposure to emerging risks and opportunities, organisations monitor external developments, such as new regulations, market shifts, and technological innovations. This activity, known as environmental scanning, presents several challenges for analysts performing it while also proving difficult to automate due to its judgment-intensive nature. The study investigates how analysts perceive the value and limitations of agentic AI, meaning AI that can independently execute multi-step tasks, in automating this type of judgment-intensive business process. The empirical case explored in the study focuses on the automation of regulatory environmental scanning within the sustainability function of a global heavy manufacturing company. Data is collected from 18 interviews, the development of five AI prototypes, and four workshops where analysts tested AI-supported versions of scanning tasks. The study finds that value varies across process steps, being strongest for information processing tasks but still requiring significant human oversight for tasks needing accountability or depending on interpersonal relationships. Secondly, the study finds that, in addition to increasing productivity, agentic AI created value through mechanisms such as process formalisation and reduced dependencies. The implication is that much value is realised through process transformation rather than the technology itself. Finally, the study finds that agentic AI may fall short when the underlying process bottleneck is misunderstood, when users do not trust the system, or when the agent lacks sufficient internal context or customisation. This suggests that successful implementation requires early end-user involvement and gradual adoption with meaningful human control.
title: Omvärldsbevakning med Agentisk AI : En fallstudie av upplevt värde och begränsningar i omdömeskrävande arbete

abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) continue to advance, the demand for standardized mechanisms that enable seamless, scalable, and context-aware integration of these models in a secure manner is increasing. To meet these requirements, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) has come into existence as an open interoperability standard that offers a common language for linking AI models with tools, resources, and external systems. The survey provides a complete overview of the architectural foundations, communication paradigm, client–server model, transport mechanisms, design principles, and primary application areas of MCP, such as enterprise systems, software engineering, healthcare, manufacturing, education, finance, and multi-agent systems. It also reviews the state of the art and research advances, outlining security issues and their mitigation, and evaluates the status of MCP-based implementations. MCP is shown to be a significant factor in improving interoperability, context-aware reasoning, workflow orchestration, and modular integration of AI, while also minimizing the need for proprietary interfaces. Moreover, it pinpoints key areas of research that are needed in the future, such as scalability, security, standardized benchmarking, interoperability, and long-term context management, offering researchers and practitioners working on the creation of next-generation AI systems significant directions for future research.
title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI Systems: A Survey of Architectures and Applications

abstract: This chapter examines the transformative impact of natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs) on materials science, focusing on challenges and future advancements. Key obstacles include enhancing numerical understanding, quantitative prediction, and scientific reasoning. Numerical proficiency is improved through high-quality datasets and domain-specific fine-tuning. Quantitative prediction is advanced by integrating language encoders with property-prediction networks and deploying AI agents for computational resource integration. Efficiency is optimized via knowledge distillation, balancing model size and performance. Scientific reasoning is augmented through retrieval-augmented generation and advanced training protocols like reinforcement learning, as demonstrated by the DeepSeek-R1 model. Current applications in materials design have shown promise in predicting properties and suggesting compositions, particularly in alloy and polymer engineering. Future advancements are expected to refine these capabilities and integrate language models with computational and experimental tools for real-time insights. The evolution of AI is set to revolutionize materials science by enabling autonomous experimentation, cross-disciplinary synergy, and the development of a hybrid workforce skilled in both AI and materials engineering, ultimately driving sustainable and intelligent manufacturing.
title: Challenges and Future Developments

abstract: This article proposes a conceptual and formal model of intelligent monitoring (IM) of information systems (ISs) in the context of architectural evolution, contextual dependence, and decision-making (DM) uncertainty. IM is studied as an information technology (IT) in which the monitoring process combines observation, interpretation, prediction, and selection of a response strategy. A formalization of the IS as a dynamic directed graph is developed, where the vertices represent functional components, and the edges represent structural, informational, or control connections between them. A description of the functional state (FS) of the system as a region in the multidimensional space of metrics, risk parameters, context, and agent-level is proposed, which allows consideration of both internal configuration changes and the effects of the external environment. The research indicates that a change in the topology of connections, the context of functioning, or the degree of autonomy of components leads to the system transitioning to a new FS, which, in turn, changes the requirements for monitoring architecture, observation, and monitoring mode. A single conceptual model has been developed that links the FS of the ISs, monitoring requirements, and the strategy selection mechanism within the adaptive DM cycle. The study suggests that the proposed concept can serve as a basis for building adaptive, scalable, and resilient monitoring architectures for complex software, cyber-physical, and multi-agent systems. The study extends the conceptual understanding of monitoring as an active element of decision support rather than merely a means of data collection and visualization. Methodologically, the study is positioned as a conceptual-formal work that synthesizes existing monitoring paradigms and develops a formal model intended for further scenario-based, simulation-based, and implementation-oriented validation. Scenario-based synthetic validation and comparative analysis of hierarchical, federated, and hybrid monitoring regimes further demonstrate the practical interpretability of the model and its applicability to context-sensitive design of evolving, LLM-driven, and cyber-physical systems. Prospects for further research include experimental validation of the model and the integration of knowledge-based and LLM-driven mechanisms into the strategy selection problem.
title: INTELLIGENT MONITORING AS AN INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY FOR CONTEXT-AWARE DECISION-MAKING STRATEGY SELECTION

abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated transformative potential in creative and technical fields, yet its application to engineering design remains underdeveloped. Unlike domains where AI outputs can be directly consumed, engineering design demands integration across heterogeneous tools, multimodal data, and highly structured workflows. This thesis develops and evaluates AI-driven approaches for enabling copilot-style systems that assist engineers throughout the early stages of design, where decisions have the greatest impact on cost and performance. We identify and address three central challenges: the need for user control over abstract generative processes, the scarcity of high-quality engineering datasets, and the complexity of integrating AI into diverse design toolchains. Our first contribution is Sketch2Prototype, a multi-stage framework that transforms conceptual sketches into text, images, and manufacturable 3D meshes. Evaluated on a dataset of 1,087 sketches, the system produces more diverse and manufacturable prototypes than direct sketch-to-3D methods, while enabling iterative refinement through a controllable intermediate text stage. Our second contribution is VideoCAD, a synthetic dataset of over 41,000 annotated CAD modeling videos—up to twenty times longer in action horizon than prior UI agent datasets—capturing pixel-precise, long-horizon interactions in a professional CAD environment. We benchmark state-of-the-art behavior cloning models and large language models on VideoCAD, and introduce VideoCADFORMER, a transformer-based architecture that achieves superior performance on long-horizon CAD action prediction. Finally, we present VisionCAD, a fine-tuned Large Language Model (LLM) that constructs CAD Generation code from point cloud and image data, trained with a dataset of over two million image, point cloud, and CADQuery triplets. Together, these contributions demonstrate that generative AI, multimodal learning, and large-scale dataset generation can be combined to accelerate design exploration, improve manufacturability, and integrate seamlessly into engineering workflows. By addressing both the data and workflow bottlenecks, this work lays the foundation for AI copilots that enhance productivity, creativity, and precision in engineering design.
title: From Sketch to CAD Code: Multimodal AI for Controllable Design Generation

abstract: The Cabinet Office of Japan has advocated for Society 5.0, while the European Commission has promoted Industry 5.0, both aiming to establish a human-centered society as a common, overarching goal.Addressing social challenges associated with shifts in population demographics and environmental changes requires the provision of suitable services that meet human needs and resolve related issues.However, given the vast number of services available and the diversity of needs based on factors such as age, region, and language, delivering services that precisely match individual needs is challenging.Therefore, it is essential to develop technology that accurately captures user demands and provides appropriate services to as many individuals as possible.This study aims to create a method for efficiently developing services that satisfy the individual needs of end-users within a cyber-physical space.The core idea is to automate and streamline the specialized processes of requirement gathering and software design and development through agent-based dialogue and service computing technologies.This paper outlines four challenges in service personalization from two perspectives: needs observation and the construction of personalized services.The first challenge is the automatic extraction of individual user needs.We define a needs data model using the 6W1H structure to accurately represent needs and apply natural language processing with large language models (LLM) to extract needs from dialogues with users.Through agent interaction, user requests are refined, and the extracted needs are evaluated for accuracy.Experiments demonstrate that needs could be accurately extracted in a short time without expert intervention.The second challenge involves enabling personalized services through the integration of existing services.We define an application-neutral rule data model and suc-iii cessfully represent the interactions between various services using a data structure based on the 6W1H framework.A platform is built to automatically assess events occurring in the cyber-physical space to facilitate service integration, and further, we succeed in realizing a method to efficiently construct new integrated services in a low-code manner.Development experiments show that this approach enables the construction of personalized services more effectively than conventional methods.The third challenge addresses the creation of new services to meet personalized needs.We propose a systematic approach to the software upcycle process by building a collective intelligence database of development knowledge, enabling the assetization and reuse of valuable existing knowledge.By including not only source code but also the purpose and outcomes of development, the system allows for efficient development tailored to needs-or seeds-based goals.Experiments demonstrate that collective intelligence-based development could produce high-quality software within shorter timeframes.The fourth challenge is implementing a development methodology for new personalized services based on user needs.We successfully create a development ecosystem that incorporates both a needs extraction system and an upcycle-based collective intelligence database.Triggered by user-agent dialogues, this system automatically identifies the needs, services to be developed, and development methods required for personalized service creation.Experiments confirm that this development ecosystem supports the efficient creation of personalized services.

abstract: Mechanical drawing audits are essential to product design and manufacturing but remain labor-intensive and error-prone, particularly when checking tolerances, surface roughness, materials, treatments and assembly requirements. Although computer vision, document understanding, large language models (LLMs), knowledge representation and multi-agent systems (MAS) can support individual tasks, existing efforts remain fragmented. This paper proposes an engineering-oriented approach to AI-assisted mechanical drawing auditing and a three-layer Perception – Cognition – Collaboration (P – C – C) pre-validation reference architecture. Perception transforms carrier-specific evidence into provenance-bearing entities and relations. Cognition aligns them with a versioned Standards-and-Requirements Knowledge Graph and applies approved deterministic numerical and logical rules outside the LLM. Collaboration coordinates audit tasks, preserves conflicts, and routes critical or uncertain findings to authorized engineers. An audit of the Merge_places Computer Vision Dataset reveals limitations in schema consistency, lineage, class semantics and clause grounding. De-identified drawing regions illustrate clearance calculation, detection of a controlled tolerance mismatch, and the routing of GD&T and bill-of-materials (BOM) requests when evidence is incomplete. These bounded cases clarify interface behavior and define validation requirements for provenance, deterministic checking, interoperability, uncertainty, cybersecurity and human governance before engineering deployment. The framework integrates heterogeneous evidence, executable rules and accountable human decisions within a traceable and selectively automated audit workflow.
title: AI-assisted auditing review of mechanical engineering drawings: a Perception–Cognition–Collaboration reference architecture and its implementation Perspectives
venue: International Journal of Computer Integrated Manufacturing

abstract: This public definition package provides the canonical definition of Execution Governance (EG) as an independent structural governance research framework focused on governed effects. It defines the core EG concepts, including governed effect, proposed action, pre-execution authorization, execution authorization, live-context integrity, verified mandate, valid constraints, accountability, reviewability, and sufficient verifiable proof. The package establishes the six concurrent conditions under which a proposed action may be authorized to produce a governed effect: verified mandate, valid constraints, live-context integrity, accountability, reviewability, and sufficient verifiable proof. It is intended as a public reference for researchers, standards contributors, AI governance practitioners, autonomous systems developers, policy communities, and organizations exploring execution-level governance for AI-enabled actions, autonomous systems, agentic AI, cyber-physical systems, and high-consequence digital workflows. This document is part of the Execution Governance v1.0.1 Public Release Series. It is a conceptual and definitional research document. It is not an ISO, IEC, IEEE, NIST, or W3C standard, specification, certification scheme, conformance model, or implementation guide, and it is not endorsed by those organizations.
title: Execution Governance Canonical Definition Package v1.0.1

abstract: This research aims to enhance the efficiency of the corrective maintenance process in the air conditioning manufacturing industry, focusing on reducing waste in the diagnostic phase (Mean Time to Diagnose: MTTD). Based on a case study of the MC-01 machine, which experienced a maximum accumulated downtime of 362.81 hours per year, root cause analysis revealed that 36.58% of the total repair time delay was attributed to limitations in retrieving historical repair data from the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS). The existing system lacked a standardized structure, making data difficult to reuse. This research developed an intelligent maintenance assistant system via the LINE Official Account application by integrating an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Agent with the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technique and a Large Language Model (LLM) through the n8n automation system, acting as a mobile knowledge base for on-site technicians. The performance evaluation demonstrated that the system accurately supports decision-making and provides precise repair guidelines, resulting in a statistically significant reduction in MTTD by 46.77% at a 0.05 significance level. Furthermore, this system serves as a crucial tool that enables maintenance technicians of all levels to perform their tasks rapidly and efficiently in accordance with established standards.

abstract: Operational Technology (OT) is experiencing one of the most remarkable shifts in its history as increased OT and Information Technology (IT) systems converge to form unified, intelligent systems. The aim of this review article is to look at the most important technology trends that are currently changing the OT landscape and consider the impact of these on architecture, operation, and security for industrial environments. The review combines insights from published research from peer-reviewed journals, industry whitepapers, and standards documents to form eight interdependent themes edge computing and Edge AI, industrial and agentic AI, digital twins and predictive maintenance, Zero Trust OT cybersecurity, industrial DataOps, advanced wireless connectivity (5G and private 5G), low-code/no-code platforms, and virtual PLCs based on containerization. The results show that these technologies are not standalone but instead are a highly integrated stack that together supports real-time decision making and resilient operations with the help of intelligence, contextualized data pipelines, and software-defined control. Meanwhile, the review also highlights the ongoing challenges of cybersecurity vulnerabilities associated with increased attack surface, underdeveloped data governance and data quality, talent gaps, and lack of interoperability of vendor ecosystems. The article concludes that the future of OT will be adaptive, autonomous, and securely connected industrial systems, but this will only happen when standards, governance processes, and human–machine collaboration are coordinated. Future research recommendations are made for research on the deployment of agentic AI, empirical benchmarks for Zero Trust OT architectures and unified evaluation frameworks for DataOps maturity in the industrial sector.
title: The Convergence of Intelligence and Infrastructure: A Review of Emerging Technology Trends Reshaping Modern Operational Technology (OT) Ecosystems

abstract: SC-CAIS v0.3.2 — Zenodo Release Notes Release title SC-CAIS v0.3.2: Controlled Agentic AI for Resilient Supply Chains with Runtime Assurance Version v0.3.2 Release summary SC-CAIS is a research-oriented Python framework for evaluating Controlled Agentic AI Systems (CAIS) in multi-echelon supply-chain environments subject to operational, cyber, and compound disruptions. Version 0.3.2 is the frozen experimental release used for the reproducibility campaign supporting the manuscript: "Controlled Agentic AI for Resilient Supply Chains: Runtime Assurance under Operational and Cyber-Physical Disruptions" The framework separates autonomous decision generation from runtime execution control. Agentic policies propose supply-chain actions, while the assurance layer evaluates them against operational, resilience, cyber-data, and governance constraints before execution. The core control logic follows: approve → repair → fallback where feasible actions are approved, violating actions are minimally modified whenever possible, and fallback behavior is used only when no admissible repair can be identified. Main capabilities Multi-echelon supply-chain simulation: suppliers, plants, warehouses, distribution hubs, customers. Explicit separation of true environment state and agent observation state. Operational disruption scenarios, including supplier failure, hub closure, demand surge, transport delay, and capacity degradation. Cyber and data-integrity scenarios, including false inventory signals, telemetry loss, route-status spoofing, and corrupted observations. Compound and cyber-physical disruption scenarios. Policy-agnostic agent interface. Decision baselines including rule-based control, cost-aware optimization, rolling-horizon MILP, and agentic AI. Runtime assurance modes: no assurance / monitor-only, reject-only, SC-CAIS runtime assurance with action repair. Minimal-deviation action repair preserving agent intent whenever possible. Trust-aware route/source substitution. Resilience and assurance metrics. Full trajectory logging. Severity × uncertainty robustness experiments. Paired statistical analysis with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and paired effect size (d_z). Automated generation of article-ready CSV tables and figures. Reproducibility manifest with SHA-256 hashes. Reproducibility campaign The final manuscript campaign executed with SC-CAIS v0.3.2 contains: 10 random seeds, 36 simulation steps per run, 10 principal disruption scenarios, 600 main benchmark runs, 10,800 trajectory records, 1,920 severity × uncertainty robustness runs. The final independent reproduction run was executed on macOS ARM64 using Python 3.13 and reproduced the scientific outputs of the reference campaign. Small numerical differences were observed only for the rolling-horizon MILP baseline due to solver/platform differences and did not affect the scientific conclusions. Key experimental findings Across the final campaign, SC-CAIS reduced the mean residual constraint violation rate of the agentic policy from approximately: 0.6906 without runtime assurance to 0.0000 with SC-CAIS while preserving nearly all of the resilience performance: 0.8969 mean resilience without assurance, 0.8897 mean resilience with SC-CAIS. In the compound disruption scenario, residual violations decreased from approximately 0.8358 to 0.0000, with only a limited reduction in resilience. The repair-vs-reject ablation demonstrated that minimal-deviation action repair substantially outperformed fallback-only control. In the compound scenario, repair recovered approximately +0.69 resilience, reduced cumulative cost by approximately 42.7k model units, and shortened recovery by approximately 13 simulation steps relative to reject-only control. These results support the central design principle of SC-CAIS: autonomous decisions should be constrained at runtime without unnecessarily suppressing adaptive behavior. Quality assurance Version 0.3.2 was validated using: automated unit tests, Ruff static linting, mypy static type checking, repository verification script, smoke benchmark execution, full reproducibility campaign. The release passed the complete verification pipeline before the final manuscript experiment. Changes in v0.3.2 Version 0.3.2 is a maintenance and reproducibility release. Changes relative to v0.3.1 include: final static typing correction for Matplotlib Figure | SubFigure inference, completion of the strict mypy quality gate, no changes to simulation logic, agent policies, assurance rules, disruption definitions, random seeds, benchmark configuration, experimental hypotheses, or scientific outputs. Therefore, v0.3.2 is scientifically equivalent to v0.3.1 and represents the frozen codebase used for the official manuscript run. Software requirements Python 3.13+ NumPy pandas SciPy NetworkX Matplotlib Typer PyYAML Development and verification dependencies include Ruff, mypy, and pytest. Repository Source-code repository: [REPOSITORY Citation If you use SC-CAIS in research, please cite the software release and the associated manuscript. Authors Tymoteusz I. Miller Irmina Durlik Notes This release is intended to provide a transparent and reproducible implementation of the experimental framework described in the associated manuscript. The repository, benchmark configuration, and archived experimental outputs should be preserved unchanged for reproducibility purposes.
title: TyMill/SC-CAIS: SC-CAIS v0.3.2
