abstract: The paper proposes an A2X framework for the design of distributed cyber‑physical systems that include unmanned aerial vehicles, ground robotic platforms and digital infrastructure. Unlike the traditional V2X paradigm, where the basic unit of analysis is a vehicle, A2X treats an agent as the main entity, carrying goals, resources, constraints and interaction strategies. On this basis, an A2X‑environment is defined as a heterogeneous multi‑agent system that combines mobile platforms, stationary infrastructure, communication channels, operators and intelligent software agents. The methodology combines agent‑oriented modelling with game theory and mechanism design. Different classes of games are used as formal templates for cooperation: Stackelberg games for leader–follower coordination, coalitional games for task‑oriented group formation, Bayesian games for interaction under incomplete information, and mean‑field games for large‑scale and swarm‑like behaviours. For each class, the paper discusses how an abstract game can be translated into an operational A2X scenario with explicit roles, rules, information structures and conditions for stable cooperation in a distributed environment. The main contribution is a clear distinction between scenarios and meta‑scenarios of interaction. Scenarios describe concrete cooperative regimes for a given composition of agents and infrastructure, while meta‑scenarios specify how such regimes are built, selected and adapted as tasks, environments and participants change. It is shown that game‑theoretic models gain engineering meaning only when they are embedded into A2X architectures as repeatable and analysable cooperation patterns. The proposed framework is applicable to heterogeneous unmanned systems, urban and transport robotics, and hybrid settings where large language model‑based agents participate both in executing and in generating cooperative regimes.
title: Game-Theoretic Design of A2X Environments for Heterogeneous Unmanned and Robotic Systems

abstract: The automotive industry now uses artificial intelligence (AI) across design, manufacturing, logistics, connected services, and vehicle operation. This expansion creates two linked trust problems. The first concerns cross-company AI supply chains, in which AI services and AI agents are discovered, contracted, and used across open partner networks. The second concerns safety-relevant vehicle data chains, in which machine-learning outputs depend on large streaming sensor data, time-series processing, and low-latency cloud-edge execution. Existing governance work addresses parts of these problems, yet a common trust infrastructure is still missing. This chapter proposes a Trusted AI architecture for automotive ecosystems that combines cyber–physical system design, identity-anchored access control, verifiable provenance, delegated authority for AI agents, AI Service Passports, and risk-based policy decisions. The Catena-X AI Service KIT (KIT: “Keep It Together,” a modular bundle of documentation, open-source code, and standards designed to help a business adopt a specific use case quickly) is examined as an early reference case for the supply-chain control plane. Its value lies in AI service publication, discovery, connector-based access, and usage policy across business partners. A dangerous-driving case study then shows why autonomous-driving and driver-assistance scenarios require an additional operational trust layer. In that case, signed data structures, decentralised identifiers, and verifiable credentials allow each transformation step from vehicle signal to machine-learning label to be assessed and traced, similar to how physical components are traced in a supply chain. The chapter introduces the European Business Wallet as the legal-person identity anchor for business-to-business AI interaction and argues that trustworthy automotive AI depends on a bridge between supply-chain governance and provenance-aware vehicle data chains for legal compliance and product liability purposes.
title: Trusted AI for the Automotive Industry
The Ai-Driven Decision-Making (Aidm) Framework: Integrating Ahp and Chatgpt-4 for Supplier Selection

abstract: This governance document presents the official Quality Assurance (QA) Checklist designed to establish and enforce "responsible control" in automated, agentic AI, and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) workflows within regulated, safety-critical civil engineering practice. Anchored in the triadic governance framework of the MIPR Institute, this checklist operationalizes the Centre of Focus (COF/0)—the unvarying coordinate origin where human professional responsibility, algorithmic assistance, and physical site telemetry reach static equilibrium. As AI language and parametric design models accelerate text and geometry production, they introduce severe cognitive risks, including automation bias, complacency, and the loss of a traceable design paper trail. These "black-box" deviations threaten the professional standard of care and non-delegable legal accountability carried solely by the human practitioner. To mitigate these risks, this checklist translates the Golden Equilibrium Model (GEM) and boundary-damping kinetics into five practical, interface-driven deployment phases: Pre-Prompting Analog Intent: Preserving sketching and traditional planning as cognitive constraints before computation. Boundary-Based Delegation: Restricting agentic AI permissions and establishing mandatory exception-routing thresholds to keep human supervisors in control. Interfacial Quality Controls: Instituting output classification (Draft vs. Proposal vs. Baseline Candidate), strict traceability links ("no source, no trace = no acceptance"), and the "Four-Eyes" verification principle. RACI Accountability Mapping: Assigning unambiguous acceptance authority under Singapore's regulatory engineering frameworks. Decision Logging and Auditing: Systematically archiving prompts, inputs, outputs, and sources to defend design authorship and professional originality. This checklist serves as an in-house operating playbook for Le Management (2011) Pte Ltd and acts as the practical companion to Paper 1 ("Human Decides, AI Assists, CPS Enables") of the 1st World LEM AI-Empowered Built Environment Convention (WABE 2026).
title: Quality Assurance Checklist for Human-AI-CPS Integration in Regulated Engineering Practice: Establishing 'Responsible Control' and the Centre of Focus (COF/0)
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Cyber threats directed against space systems (spanning orbital payloads, tracking and telemetry ground stations, downlinks, and upstream manufacturing supply chains) have evolved into acute operational hazards. Concurrently, national security and commercial defenders face an intelligence volume crisis where telemetry and vulnerability disclosures outpace human cognitive bandwidth. While autonomous multi-agent pipelines powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) offer scalable automation, they introduce severe epistemic liabilities: hallucination, source detachment, uncalibrated certainty, and susceptibility to indirect prompt injection. This paper presents Space-Cyber Brief Crew, a multi-agent cyber threat intelligence (CTI) architecture that automates space-domain intelligence synthesis under an explicit governance layer. Built on a decoupled CrewAI orchestration, the system routes structured reporting through a three-stage sequential pipeline (Collector, Analyst, Writer) governed by ten operational rules. Crucially, the architecture establishes a structural boundary between action capabilities and generative synthesis: downstream analysis agents operate in zero-tool sandboxes, restricting the execution attack surface by construction. We evaluate the framework against a tri-domain threat corpus spanning satellite imagery manipulation, ground industrial control systems (ICS), and global navigation satellite system (GNSS) spoofing. In our evaluation, the governed architecture eliminated identifier fabrication (from 23.3% to 0.0%), preserved 100% provenance retention, and neutralized indirect prompt injection attacks that succeeded in 80% of unconstrained baseline runs. Finally, we examine the institutional, regulatory, and oversight implications, establishing technical criteria for federal procurement and intelligence integration.
title: Governing the Intelligence Loop: Architectural Mitigations for Epistemic Fragility in Autonomous Space-Cyber Threat Analysis
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Abstract The Super Tau-Charm Facility Beam Test Platform (STCF-BTP) requires reliable radiation safety management, deterministic interlock control, and efficient analysis of abnormal interlock events. This paper presents an EPICS-integrated personnel safety system (PSS) with an evidence-constrained Harness-agent diagnostic layer. The PSS is based on redundant PLCs, distributed I/O stations, the EPICS control platform, and an operator interface, and provides interlock functions for shielding doors, area clearance, emergency stop buttons, radiation dose monitoring, ventilation control, and access control. The diagnostic layer is deployed above the PSS as a read-only module and does not participate in real-time PLC control. Interlock state transitions are used as diagnostic triggers. The Harness-agent queries archived PV data through registered diagnostic tools, applies rule-based cause matching, checks evidence sufficiency, and records the evidence and execution trace associated with each diagnosis. On a 165-case system-level test set, the Harness-agent using DeepSeek achieved an exact-diagnosis accuracy of 89.1 %. Using the same test set, the ablation study showed that the harness layer improved exact-diagnosis accuracy across all three evaluated LLMs and reduced unsupported direct-cause generation to 0.0 % in all Harness-agent configurations. These results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating a read-only, evidence-constrained Harness-agent with the STCF-BTP PSS for post-event interlock analysis and provide a practical reference for similar accelerator PSS applications.
title: A personnel safety system enhanced by harness framework-based anomaly detection for the STCF-BTP accelerator facility

abstract: Abstract The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into decision-making is transforming industry norms by enabling smarter, faster, and more reliable decisions. This paper presents a novel approach for supplier selection in manufacturing by combining the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with the Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT). Using GPT as virtual agents to mimic expert evaluations automates the supplier selection process, significantly improving efficiency. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of large language models as virtual experts in complex decision-making, highlighting AI’s crucial role in strategic manufacturing operations. Comparing GPT’s assessments with human expert judgments confirms the model’s reliability and effectiveness in optimizing supplier selection. This approach enhances decision-making processes and emphasizes the broad utility of AI-centric methodologies in various industries.
title: The AI-driven Decision-Making (AIDM) Framework: Integrating AHP and ChatGPT for Supplier Selection

abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of the most transformative technologies of the modern era. By 2026, AI applications have expanded beyond digital assistance into physical, industrial, and social environments. The rapid development of embodied intelligence, enterprise intelligent agents, and multimodal large language models has enabled AI to improve productivity, optimize decision-making, and accelerate innovation across multiple sectors. This article examines the application of AI in manufacturing, healthcare, scientific research, finance, and social governance, highlighting its role in drivingeconomic growth and technological advancement.
title: ARTIFICAL INTELLIGENCE APPLICATIONS IN 2026: TRANSFORMING INDUSTRY , HEALTHCARE, SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH AND SOCIAL GOVERNANCE

abstract: Offsite construction (OSC) requires an integrated design and delivery system. Reusing prior OSC knowledge is paramount to the success of new OSC projects. However, a gap remains in managing and reusing this knowledge across the broader industry. The challenge lies in the fragmented nature of project-based organisations with isolated knowledge systems, which often lack integration and advanced capabilities for knowledge-based collaboration. This paper proposes a novel framework that leverages cutting-edge knowledge-based methods and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to create a container-based knowledge system (CBKS) that can enhance knowledge capture and reuse towards collaborative OSC. Specifically, the semantic web stack is adopted to construct multimodal knowledge containers for both human users and AI agents. In addition, GPT-4o, a large language model (LLM), is embedded into the knowledge system for better knowledge querying, matching and retrieving. By using this framework, constructed modular knowledge units can integrate product, process and organisation factors to address specific OSC problems. To evaluate the technical feasibility of the proposed framework, a prototype is developed and illustrated through a modular connection design. This illustrative case study demonstrates how knowledge is captured for product representation under manufacturing and assembly constraints, enabling its reuse in different projects. Moreover, the usefulness of GPT-4o for enhancing this process is also tested.
title: Enhancing Knowledge Capture and Reuse for Offsite Construction Through A Container-Based Knowledge Approach

abstract: Trajectory generation is a fundamental challenge in autonomous mobility and intelligent transportation systems, where robotic systems and vehicles must navigate safely in complex and dynamic environments. Current approaches often suffer from mode collapse, poor constraint adherence, and overfitting to dataset priors, leading to low-quality and unrealistic trajectory generation. To address these challenges, we propose a novel trajectory generation framework, MH-DDPM, a Multi-modal Hierarchical Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model, designed to generate interpretable, diverse, and rule-compliant trajectories in complex multi-agent environments. Our method adopts a two-stage architecture: a high-level goal generation module based on conditional diffusion, and a low-level deterministic controller for action generation. To enhance contextual awareness, we condition the generative process on semantic embeddings produced by a multi-modal large language model, allowing the model to leverage structured environmental knowledge extracted from map imagery. We validate our framework on the nuScenes dataset, which is a large-scale real-world dataset of autonomous vehicle trajectories. Our method surpasses the state-of-the-art in key metrics, showing its potential to advance interpretable and efficient trajectory generation for autonomous mobility and industrial automation, in the context of Industry 4.0.
title: Multi-modal Hierarchical Diffusion Model for Robust and Realistic Trajectory Generation
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Conference of the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society

abstract: Traditional higher and professional education follows an episodic, front-loaded paradigm in which foundational degrees are earned early in life with little continuous adaptation. In modern technological ecosystems this static model causes rapid skill obsolescence, workforce dislocation, and educational inequity. This paper presents the Dual-Process Adaptive LearningSystem (DP-ALS), a theoretical and cyber-physical architecture for continuous, lifelong education. Drawing on dual-process cog-nitive theory, DP-ALS separates educational intervention into two components: (i) a low-latency System One decision model (design target under 40 ms) that acts as a continuous reflex engine, monitoring learner micro-telemetry to track cognitive load, flow state, and productive struggle through a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP); and (ii) a deliberate SystemTwo generative AI tutor invoked asynchronously only when an impasse is detected or deep conceptual synthesis is required. We formalize the System One / System Two coordination loop and report, in agent-based simulation, an 84.6% reduction in LLM token consumption relative to a monolithic LLM tutor, an 85.3% reduction in cognitive impasse, and a 61.6% reduction in time-to-mastery relative to a static curriculum. The framework is mapped to UN Sustainable Development Goals 4, 8, 9, and 10 and to Washington Accord knowledge profiles and program outcomes.
title: Shifting from One-Time Education to Continuous Growth: A Dual-Process Cognitive Architecture Integrating System One Decision Models and Generative Socratic Tutors for Adaptive Lifelong Learning

abstract: Recent large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress in constraint-aware navigation, maze reasoning, and graph reasoning. However, their ability to reason about complex routing problems under strict geometric, topological, and electrical constraints remains largely unexplored, despite routing being one of the most challenging and critical stages of electronic design automation (EDA). To bridge this gap, we introduce OmniRouting, the first large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs on printed-circuit-board (PCB) routing reasoning under real-world industrial design-rule, manufacturability, and connectivity constraints. OmniRouting contains 1,681 industrial-grade schematic-coupled PCB designs, including board geometries, routable component placements by human engineers, footprints, pad locations, netlists, stackup information, and routing constraints. The benchmark comprises four tasks: (1) geometric routing reasoning, generating physically valid copper traces, vias, and layer assignments to connect circuit nets within constrained board regions; (2) design-rule-aware routing reasoning, producing routable layouts that satisfy clearance, trace-width, via, obstacle-avoidance, and board-boundary constraints; (3) electrical functionality reasoning, preserving schematic-specified connectivity while reasoning over net names and functional roles to produce electrically correct routing; and (4) tool-augmented agentic routing, leveraging external tools for tasks (1)-(3). Our results reveal substantial limitations of current LMMs in PCB routing, including weak path-planning capabilities, poor adherence to design-rule constraints, and inconsistent preservation of electrical functionality. We will open-source all benchmark data, evaluation code, and tool interfaces to facilitate future research.
title: OmniRouting: A Semantic-Coupled Multimodal Benchmark for Constraint-Aware Spatial Reasoning in PCB Routing
COIN Enterprise Transformation

abstract: This chapter analyzes how artificial intelligence is reshaping the mobility space across the entire value chain. The impact of AI ranges from vehicle design and engineering to manufacturing, user experience, after-sales service and back-office operations. Generative AI can assist in styling as well as system and component design with multi-factor optimization. AI can help create specifications, leveraging carmakers’ dataset and regulation-derived input. AI is now generally used as a coding assistant and is core to assisted and autonomous driving. In supply chain and manufacturing, AI can be used to optimize inventory and logistics, control quality, and identify the need for predictive maintenance on production equipment. AI benefits the user experience with increasingly advanced assistants that soon will leverage Agentic AI. Finally, AI can assist in the service space, detecting early signals before a breakdown and supporting dealers’ operations.
title: Artificial Intelligence

abstract: Global supply chains operate under compounding uncertainty -- volatile demand, supplier disruptions, transportationdelays, geopolitical risk, and climate-related shocks -- that traditional operations research methods address throughdeterministic optimisation and scenario planning but cannot dynamically adapt to in real time. AI-powered supply chainoptimisation offers three capabilities traditional methods lack: demand forecasting that captures non-linear and causalrelationships in high-dimensional signals, real-time replanning under disruption, and autonomous decision support formulti-echelon inventory and routing optimisation. This study evaluates eight AI approaches for supply chain optimisationacross five problem domains: demand forecasting, inventory optimisation, supplier risk assessment, vehicle routing, anddisruption response. Methods include gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost, LightGBM), Temporal Fusion Transformer(TFT), deep reinforcement learning for inventory control (DRL-Inv), Graph Neural Networks for supplier risk (GNN-Risk),large language model-powered planning agents (LLM-SCM), combinatorial optimisation with neural heuristics(OR-Neural), and a hybrid ensemble. Data from 12 European manufacturing companies across six sectors (automotive,pharmaceutical, electronics, food, energy, and logistics) over 2019-2023 -- including the COVID-19 disruption period --was used for evaluation. TFT achieves the lowest demand forecasting MAPE (8.4%) across product categories. DRL-Invreduces inventory holding costs by 18.6% vs. EOQ baseline while maintaining service levels. GNN-Risk predicts supplierdisruptions 14.2 days earlier than human supply chain managers. LLM-SCM reduces disruption response time by 42.4%in simulation but introduces hallucination risks requiring human validation. A sector-specific AI adoption roadmap isproposed.
title: AI in Supply Chain Optimization

abstract: The word robot was first used to describe artificial automata in a Czech play in 1920 and literally meant ‘forced labour’. From the inception of the term and recent progress in the field of AI, society has often panicked society about the effect of robots in terms of job loss, machine takeover and a loss for humanity. However, robots have kept on making inroads in multiple segments of society, from industrial automation to precision surgery. This chapter will discuss human–robot interaction (HRI) for three different applications: collaborative robots (cobots) for industrial applications, social robots and assistive robots. We will briefly discuss the main goals of each application, followed by a case study on developing safe human–robot interaction for persons with severe speech and motor impairments. A second case study will briefly describe the building blocks of a LLM-controlled semi-autonomous rover, where the destination will be given by a human through natural language or even an image, and the robot autonomously navigates to the desired destination, avoiding obstacles. The chapter will emphasize applications of intelligent user interfaces for semi-autonomous control of robotic agents.
title: Human–robot interaction

abstract: Industrial workers face a fundamental interaction design challenge: translating abstract textual instructions into embodied physical actions within complex spatial environments. While mixed reality (MR) technologies promise to bridge this gap through spatially situated guidance, the manual effort required to author MR content from existing documentation limits practical adoption.This paper presents a Research through Design investigation into AI-powered transformation of industrial work instructions. We explore how Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can automatically convert heterogeneous documentation – PDF manuals, technical drawings, and procedural specifications – into context-aware MR experiences. Through collaborative prototyping with two industrial partners, we developed and evaluated proof-of-concept systems addressing distinct operational contexts: procedural assembly guidance in medical technology manufacturing and event-driven maintenance support for distributed automated infrastructure.Our design exploration yields three key insights. First, we identify agentic preprocessing as a critical architectural pattern where LLM agents semantically interpret documents while generating verification context for downstream VLM assessment. Second, we demonstrate the viability of decomposed VLM assessment – using focused single-criterion queries rather than holistic evaluations – for reliable quality verification. Third, we articulate a "two eyes plus AI" paradigm that reframes traditional dual-inspection protocols as human-AI collaboration, positioning VLM verification as a partner that augments rather than replaces human judgment.Our contributions include: (1) a design framework for AI-powered instruction transformation identifying document heterogeneity, spatial-semantic alignment, and verification context generation as critical design challenges; (2) empirical design knowledge for human-AI collaborative quality assurance in safety-critical industrial contexts; and (3) cross-case analysis revealing convergent architectural patterns applicable across procedural and event-driven industrial scenarios. We discuss implications for designing AI-augmented work systems that preserve human agency while leveraging generative AI capabilities
title: From Manuals to Mixed Reality: Designing Generative AI Systems for Context-Aware Industrial Guidance

abstract: Pharmaceutical supply chains are highly complex, global, and tightly regulated systems that are increasingly exposed to disruption from geopolitical instability, pandemics, and demand volatility. This report examines how data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) can optimise pharmaceutical supply chains by improving forecasting accuracy, manufacturing efficiency, inventory management, logistics, quality assurance, and regulatory compliance. It argues that the industry is transitioning from isolated AI pilots toward integrated, intelligent, and potentially autonomous supply chain systems underpinned by data-driven decision-making, digital twins, and agentic AI. The report highlights the foundational role of data, emphasising that its value depends on contextualisation, integration, and governance across fragmented systems. AI applications such as machine learning-based demand forecasting, predictive inventory optimisation, and real-time analytics enable more responsive and efficient supply chain operations. In manufacturing, digital twins and predictive maintenance systems improve yield, reduce downtime, and enhance quality consistency, while AI-enabled logistics and warehouse optimisation strengthen cold-chain integrity and distribution efficiency. The report also explores AI applications in quality management and regulatory compliance, including anomaly detection, computer vision inspection, and automated documentation aligned with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards. Major technology providers such as IBM, SAP, Siemens, Microsoft, and GE Digital are enabling these capabilities through advanced industrial AI platforms. Finally, the report considers the emerging potential of agentic AI to enable autonomous decision-making across end-to-end supply chains, while recognising persistent challenges related to data quality, regulatory constraints, cybersecurity risks, and organisational readiness. Overall, the findings suggest that AI has the potential to transform pharmaceutical supply chains into more resilient, adaptive, and patient-centric systems, provided that technological innovation is matched with robust governance and organisational change.
title: How Data and AI Can Optimise Pharmaceutical Supply Chains
venue: Biology Engineering Medicine and Science Reports

abstract: The emergence of Industry 5.0 emphasizes human-centric smart manufacturing, where human–robot collaboration plays a pivotal role in achieving flexibility, resilience, and sustainability. In this context, natural language serves as a crucial bridge, and recent breakthroughs in large language models that exhibit strong reasoning and generation capabilities have established a solid foundation for generative AI. However, their application in industrial dexterous tasks with force and safety constraints remains limited. This paper explores how integrating advanced AI with embodied agents can overcome these limitations. A set of paradigms are proposed: (i) Generative AI-driven skill learning: Large language models are used to generate and refine reward functions, realizing enhanced reinforcement learning for adaptive policy training in contact-rich tasks. (ii) Human-guided embodied skill transfer: A mixed reality–assisted teleoperation platform is developed for intuitive human demonstration, leveraging generative policies such as action chunk transformer and diffusion policy to learn visuomotor control. Experiments in both simulation and real-world settings demonstrate efficiency and generalization across industrially-inspired tasks such as peg-insertion, gear-meshing, and nut-screwing. It is hoped that this work can establish generative intelligence–driven pathways and provide new insights toward adaptive and human-aligned robotic systems for next-generation intelligent manufacturing.
title: Generative AI-Driven Pathways for Robot Skill Learning and Human-Guided Transfer for Smart Assembly

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly viewed as a general-purpose technology with the potential to reshape production, communication, and governance. At the same time, it is changing the threat landscape facing individuals, societies, and institutions. This chapter outlines future AI threats and risks using a two-by-two framework that distinguishes epistemic versus kinetic harms and misuse versus systemic sources. Epistemic harms destabilize the information environment and the conditions for forming reliable beliefs, while kinetic harms involve physical or cyber-physical damage. Misuse captures intentional, malicious deployment of AI; systemic risks arise from embedding AI in platforms, markets, and institutions even absent malign intent. The chapter then explores two case studies. First, deepfakes illustrate epistemic misuse by lowering the cost of credible deception and enabling the contestation of authentic evidence, thereby weakening public trust. Second, autonomous weapons and AI-enabled targeting pipelines illustrate kinetic risk by distributing lethal decision functions across human–machine ensembles, raising accountability challenges under international humanitarian law and increasing escalation pressures through speed and opacity. The chapter then reviews technical countermeasures, provenance standards, and emerging regulatory approaches, and explains why current responses lag behind rapid capability growth. It concludes by assessing how agentic AI may amplify and recombine these risks across domains.
title: Future Threats and Risks - I: Deepfakes, Autonomous Weapons, and AI Safety

abstract: Abstract This chapter investigates the transformative role of artificial general intelligence (AGI) in advancing lean construction and waste management within the human-centric framework of Industry 5.0. While lean principles effectively minimise inefficiencies, their potential is constrained by manual data handling and the limitations of narrow artificial intelligence (AI). This research posits AGI as a paradigm shift, offering autonomous, cross-domain reasoning and recursive self-optimisation to address these challenges. The analysis explores how AGI enhances lean methodologies by integrating disparate data from building information modelling (BIM), IoT and site telemetry to automate workflows and manage resources. A key focus is its application in construction and demolition waste (CDW) management, where AGI can transcend conventional machine learning models by leveraging generalised learning to predict and classify waste streams with minimal supervision. As illustrated in a projected timeline, the evolution from current narrow AI to agentic AI by 2025, and ultimately to AGI around 2038, is expected to drive waste reduction efficiency towards near-total optimisation. This progression signifies a move towards self-organising, cyber–physical construction systems. The chapter concludes by addressing critical implementation barriers, including data interoperability and the ‘black-box’ nature of AGI, alongside the ethical imperatives of accountability, bias mitigation and fostering a human–machine symbiosis for a resilient and intelligent built environment.
title: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) for Lean and Waste Construction Management
Scene graph enhanced retrieval-augmented generation for unsafe behavior detection in industry

abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transitioning from a technology primarily used for prediction, recommendation, and content generation toward systems capable of reasoning, using external tools, executing multi-step workflows, and interacting with the physical environment. Recent developments in foundation models, multimodal AI, reasoning models, AI agents, robotics, specialized AI infrastructure, and on-device inference indicate that the role of AI within corporations is likely to expand substantially during the next decade. This thesis investigates the potential impact of AI/ML technology on corporate sectors by 2035 using current technological developments and evidence published by organizations including OpenAI, Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, Anthropic, the International Labour Organization (ILO), OECD, and NIST. Current enterprise evidence already indicates a transition from experimental AI usage toward workflow integration. OpenAI reports substantial increases in enterprise usage and reasoning workloads, while Anthropic and other technology companies are developing systems capable of autonomous multi-step task execution. The research examines five major technological trajectories: advanced reasoning, agentic AI, multimodal and embodied AI, AI infrastructure, and AI governance/security. Their potential effects are analyzed across information technology, finance, healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, retail, telecommunications, professional services, and human resources. The thesis argues that the most significant corporate transformation by 2035 is unlikely to be simply the replacement of human employees with AI. Instead, the more plausible transformation is the restructuring of work itself: AI systems will increasingly perform routine cognitive tasks, coordinate workflows, generate and analyze information, operate software systems, and potentially control physical machines. Consequently, organizations are likely to shift toward human-AI collaboration, smaller highly skilled teams, AI-supervised operations, continuous reskilling, and stronger governance mechanisms.
title: The Corporate Impact of Artificial Intelligence by 2035
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: As semiconductor manufacturing advances toward sub-2nm nodes, local place-and-route (P&R) design-rule violation (DRV) fixing is increasingly limited by complex rule interactions, dense multi-layer routing geometries, and foundry-specific constraints. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated strong capabilities in EDA scripting and documentation, their application to visual layout understanding remains largely unexplored: diagnosing DRC violations from layout imagery demands precise geometric reasoning and foundry-specific rule knowledge absent from general-purpose VLM training. We propose SCALE, a framework with a self-supervised layout-generation stage for local DRV fixing at advanced nodes. Multi-layer layout geometry is serialized into structured text, and a fine-tuned language model learns to reconstruct randomly masked polygons from surrounding BEOL context alone without violation labels. At inference, natural-language rule constraints and high-temperature sampling steer generation toward diverse, violation-prone layout variants validated by an industrial signoff DRC checker, producing DRC-annotated layout--violation pairs used to fine-tune a domain-adapted DRC-VLM. This VLM provides rule-aware geometric guidance for local DRV repair, boosting state-of-the-art agents' solve rates by +12--25% (up to 97%) on 100 real sub-2nm cases spanning enclosure, spacing, width, and color-spacing violations.
title: SCALE: Self-Supervised Constraint-Aware Layout GEneration for Local P&R DRV Fixing at Advanced Nodes

abstract: Mechanical product design integrates functional reasoning, geometric modelling, assembly planning, and engineering validation, yet remains highly dependent on human expertise. Existing large language models lack the spatial reasoning and physical constraint awareness required for engineering-grade design, whereas task-specific neural networks perform well in localised geometric recognition but are restricted to narrowly defined and repetitive tasks. Here we show an Intelligent Generative Design framework that enables autonomous mechanical design from natural-language requirements through biologically inspired coordination of task-specific agents. Integrating multimodal engineering knowledge, the framework decomposes design tasks, performs engineering analysis, generates dimensionally accurate three-dimensional models, infers assembly constraints, and validates kinematic behaviour. Across diverse mechanical systems, the framework produces mechanically consistent designs and completes multi-component tasks beyond standalone large language models. Intelligent Generative Design establishes a framework for practical AI-assisted mechanical product development, with implications spanning intelligent manufacturing, rapid prototyping, and design space exploration within diverse industrial domains.
title: Intelligent generative design framework for semantic driven mechanical design

abstract: Enterprise automation is entering a transformative phase as businesses increasingly adopt agentic AI technologies to improve operational efficiency and decision-making. The collaboration between UiPath and OpenAI demonstrates how robotic process automation combined with generative AI can streamline complex enterprise workflows while enhancing productivity across industries. Modern AI-powered automation systems are now capable of handling unstructured documents, automating repetitive processes, and delivering intelligent insights in real time. Sectors including finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and customer support are rapidly embracing these innovations to accelerate digital transformation initiatives. According to a detailed report published by Business Honor, the integration of AI trust layers, governance frameworks, and prompt validation mechanisms is helping enterprises maintain security, compliance, and accuracy while scaling automation capabilities. Read the full article here:UiPath and OpenAI's Agentic Automation Transforms Enterprise Process Intelligence Fundamentally
title: FCA Investigates Competitive Dynamics Across the Digital Payments Industry
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Transformative Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enterprise Resource Planning Systems: A Comprehensive Review

abstract: Drug repurposing is also known as drug repositioning, reprofiling, or redirecting and is the practice of identifying new therapeutic indications for drugs that are already approved, in clinical development, or otherwise characterized in humans. Combination therapy, the deliberate co-administration of two or more therapeutic agents, pursues a related but distinct goal: an effect superior to what any single agent could achieve alone. Both strategies share an underlying logic of building on existing pharmacological, safety, and manufacturing knowledge rather than starting from a blank slate, and both have been transformed over the past decade by the maturation of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), which now support network-based candidate prediction, transcriptomic signature matching, deep-learning synergy scoring, and large language model-assisted literature mining at a scale unattainable by manual curation. This chapter provides a comprehensive, evidence-grounded overview of the scientific rationale, computational and AI-driven methodologies, clinical case studies, combination-design frameworks, regulatory pathways, ethical considerations, and persistent limitations of drug repurposing and combination therapy. It surveys classical case studies (sildenafil, thalidomide, metformin) alongside AI-era examples (baricitinib, AI-optimized tuberculosis regimens, knowledge-graph-driven oncology combinations), reviews the major families of machine learning and deep learning methods applied to drug-disease and drug-drug interaction prediction, and examines how regulatory frameworks such as the FDA's 505(b)(2) pathway and the EMA's Article 10(3) hybrid application route accommodate repurposed and combination products. The chapter closes by considering translational challenges — including a recent, instructive case in which an approved combination therapy was withdrawn after failing a confirmatory trial — and emerging directions including foundation models, digital twins, federated learning, and quantum-assisted computation.
title: DRUG REPURPOSING AND COMBINATION THERAPY

abstract: Artifact for the ACSAC 2026 paper PG-DSL: Physics-Grounded Admission Checking for MCP-Controlled CPS Tools. PG-DSL is an admission-time checker for Model Context Protocol tools that act on a cyber-physical system. It lifts each natural-language tool description into a restricted CPS-grounded formal claim, replays the tool implementation in a SWaT P1+P2 digital twin, and admits the tool only when the claimed effect matches the measured physical trajectory. The repository contains the digital-twin plant, a JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP server exposing the 14 canonical tools, the full admission pipeline (claim grammar, LLM lifter, digital-twin verifier, formal matcher, composition-aware pair verifier), the MCPShield and INVARLLM baselines, a real-agent campaign harness built on the official Python MCP SDK, every campaign script, and every result JSON behind a number in the paper. It also ships the pre-registration registers for all 50 predictions fixed before execution, of which 14 were falsified and reported. See ARTIFACT.md for a claim-to-script-to-JSON mapping and three time-boxed evaluation paths.
title: PG-DSL: Physics-Grounded Admission Checking for MCP-Controlled CPS Tools
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Abstract In this essay, we explore management, language, and artificial intelligence (AI). We highlight how management performs generative AI as magic and argue for the continued crucial role of humans under conditions of AI hype. We view language as an essential part of management to impress, to weave the illusion of expertise, and to manufacture our consent. We argue that performing AI as magic brings this into sharp relief, showing how power and ideology in and around AI operate when its advancement is constructed as inevitable. We encourage discussion on this and propose more research on resistance to management performing AI, on the gendered nature of AI and its consequences, and on AI -powered management clones and their language when agentic AI enters the stage. The magic lens offers a fruitful way forward in studying these fundamentally important topics.
title: Through the Magic Lens: Management, Language, and AI

abstract: Recent advancements in policy learning have enabled impressive results in robotics and cyber-physical systems (CPS), ranging from dexterous manipulation to bipedal locomotion. Despite these successes, learned robot policies still struggle to integrate high-level reasoning and feedback with low-level control, limiting their efficacy in complex, long-horizon tasks. This dissertation introduces methodologies that enable learned policies to leverage the same skills that humans use to reliably achieve complex goals in the real world: devising high-level plans, learning from partial successes, creating cooperative strategies, and dynamically adjusting behavior through trial-and-error.The central insight across the methods contained in this thesis is to use formal, symbolic structure to express both complex tasks and their feedback mechanisms. In doing so, policies can learn high-level behavior from precise, structured plans while maintaining the expressivity of their underlying (deep) parameterization to learn low-level control. We explore this insight across a number of settings. We first demonstrate how exploiting the under- lying structure of tasks specified via formal logic allows reinforcement learning agents to learn complex, long-horizon tasks in both the single and multi-agent setting. The precise, compositional nature of formal logic enables a dense, incremental reward structure in other- wise prohibitively sparse reward signals. We then take a step back and explore how formal task specifications can be learned from data and provide a novel method for learning these specifications from user-provided preferences. Last, we discuss policy learning in the era of foundation models, and resolve the single-shot nature of existing robot foundation models (RFMs) by devising a structured feedback mechanism that allows RFMs to iteratively learn complex tasks through trial-and-error.As a whole, this dissertation advocates for a principled integration of symbolic structure into end-to-end policy learning techniques to enable complex, long-horizon behaviors. We conclude by discussing how a foundation model-centric field can still benefit from structured task specifications, and the role formal logic can play in an increasingly neural landscape.
title: Learning to Solve Long-Horizon Tasks with Formal Logic and Structured Feedback

abstract: Manufacturing environments in Industry 5.0 demand adaptive, human-centric safety systems that can dynamically respond to evolving regulations and operational conditions. Despite technological advances, human error accounts for 70-90% of industrial accidents, highlighting the need for intelligent safety monitoring systems. We present SETTE - Safety Environment using Tracking & ioT for Enterprises - a novel hybrid framework that integrates Large Language Models, Extended Reality, and Internet of Things technologies for comprehensive operator safety monitoring. SETTE operates through two interconnected phases: design time, where multi-agent LLM architectures automatically extract safety rules from heterogeneous regulatory documents (e.g., ISO 45001, company manuals) and encode them in a Domain-Specific Language with embedded Extended Reality simulation metadata; and run time, where validated rules are enforced through real-time monitoring using IoT sensors, computer vision, and wearables integrated with an AI-powered Safety Management System. A key innovation is the human-in-the-loop validation process, where safety experts interact with automatically generated Extended Reality scenarios to assess rule feasibility before deployment, ensuring both regulatory compliance and practical applicability. The framework maintains full traceability between generated rules and source regulations while providing adaptive, context-aware guidance through a conversational Human-Machine Interface. We illustrate the framework’s operational logic through a running example involving machine guarding rules for rotating machinery, showing how regulatory text can be systematically transformed into executable safety rules with complete audit trails. Unlike traditional static safety protocols, SETTE enables continuous adaptation to changing regulations and operational conditions, providing a transparent safety layer that enhances worker understanding and compliance while reducing human error in manufacturing environments.
title: SETTE: A Human-Centric Framework for Operator Safety Monitoring in Industry 5.0

abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a transformative branch of artificial intelligence that enables autonomous systems to learn optimal decision-making strategies through continuous interaction with dynamic environments. Unlike conventional machine learning approaches that depend primarily on labeled datasets or predefined rules, reinforcement learning develops adaptive control policies by maximizing cumulative rewards, making it highly suitable for complex robotic and industrial applications. Recent advances in deep reinforcement learning, computational intelligence, and high-performance computing have significantly expanded the capability of autonomous systems to perform intelligent navigation, robotic manipulation, industrial process optimization, predictive maintenance, production scheduling, warehouse automation, and collaborative human–robot interaction. Simultaneously, the convergence of reinforcement learning with Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), cyber-physical systems, digital twins, edge computing, and Industry 5.0 has accelerated the development of intelligent manufacturing ecosystems capable of autonomous adaptation, real-time optimization, and data-driven decision-making. This chapter presents a comprehensive foundation of reinforcement learning by integrating its theoretical principles, mathematical formulations, core learning components, value functions, policy optimization methods, exploration strategies, and classical reinforcement learning algorithms with modern deep reinforcement learning techniques. The discussion further examines practical implementation frameworks, simulation platforms, and representative applications in autonomous robotics and industrial systems while addressing critical challenges including sample inefficiency, reward engineering, safety-aware learning, computational complexity, explainability, and simulation-to-real-world deployment. Emerging research directions involving hierarchical reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems, federated learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and foundation models are also highlighted to demonstrate the future evolution of intelligent autonomous systems.
title: FOUNDATIONS OF REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR AUTONOMOUS ROBOTICS AND INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS

abstract: Red-and-gold galloping horses for the 2026 Spring Festival kickstarted a disruptive new era of Generative, Agentic and Embodied AI integrations. This chapter discusses how seemingly mundane interactions with technology are now loaded with AI meaning in China. After a quarter of a century of building industrial technology that beguiled the West, 2026 kickstarted China’s “AI+” (artificial intelligence (AI) plus consumption) ambitions to integrate AI across all business sectors – from manufacturing and logistics to healthcare, consumption and tourism. Firms began to commercialise a torrent of agentic AI and embodied AI solutions, from coffee-making humanoid robots to multilingual translation apps and quantum-encrypted phones to passenger-carrying drones. Meanwhile, China’s core AI industry was valued at more than RMB1 trillion for the first time. As more Chinese travellers use homegrown AI models and apps on the move, Chinese tech brands will develop new AI platforms to facilitate cross-border trade and travel across South East Asia and beyond.
title: All Travel Routes Radiate from AI

abstract: Extending earlier work in Physics-informed Meta-instrument for eXperiments (PiMiX) [1], PiMiX~2.0 is an artificial-intelligence (AI)-enhanced data-fusion and analysis framework that integrates multi-experiment multi-modal radiographic imaging and tomography (RadIT) with physics-informed reasoning and agentic AI workflows. The framework supports automated data ingestion, multimodal image processing from one or more experiments, three-dimensional (3D) and time-resolved three-dimensional (4D) reconstruction, and physics-aware interpretation of experimental observations. The PiMiX agents are designed for deployment on desktop and laptop systems commonly used in experimental workflows, while remaining scalable to high-performance computing environments for computationally intensive tasks. By coupling RadIT instrumentation and measurements with geometry, physics, computation, and statistical inference, PiMiX 2.0 aims to accelerate RadIT data processing, knowledge extraction, improve reproducibility, and enable more integrated analysis and workflows in high-temperature plasmas, nuclear fusion, advanced manufacturing, other static and dynamic experiments.
title: PiMiX 2.0: AI-enhanced Data Fusion for Radiographic Imaging and Tomography

abstract: Critical workflows in manufacturing, infrastructure, and logistics rely heavily on business process logic systems, where even minor faults or vulnerabilities can lead to significant operational disruptions or security breaches. For large companies, a typical product recall may cost more than ten million USD, and every hour unplanned downtime of a manufacturing line might incur a million dollars in losses. While typical processes like statistical quality assurance and auditing can help mitigate future occurrences of faults, they time consuming and often lead to downtime as corrective actions are put in place. To address these real-world challenges, we deploy a Large Language Model (LLM) agent capable of detecting vulnerabilities and faults within business systems. Our dual-pipeline framework first extracts rules and specifications, which are efficiently stored for use in the subsequent fault detection pipeline. By integrating advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methodologies, our approach automates the extraction and analysis of process specifications from diverse document formats, including BPMN diagrams, structured PDFs, and JSON files. Once extracted and organized, these rules and their instantiations can be analyzed by the system’s fault detection pipeline or exported to formal languages for evaluation. The first pipeline automates specification generation through advanced text extraction methods. Utilizing optical character recognition (OCR), structured data extraction, named entity recognition (NER) and semantic processing, we identify and map key phrases to form fields using domain-specific lexicons. We employ coreference resolution to establish accurate mappings across documents, allowing us to automatically generate consistent specifications. We convert the extracted data into a vector database (ChromaDB) to facilitate similarity-based retrieval. Building upon this foundation, we implement the second pipeline using a RAG architecture designed for fault detection. When a user submits a query, the system searches the vector database to retrieve the relevant sub-context, which is combined with a business logic-specific prompt derived from the user's query. Dynamically generated fault detection queries enable the LLM to identify discrepancies in workflows and produce detailed fault analyses and corrective recommendations. We evaluate our approach using three metrics: (1) the correctness of the LLM-generated answers (completeness versus hallucination), (2) question-answer accuracy given the context provided to the LLM, and (3) the quality of the RAG process. Our corpus for evaluation is based on artifacts related to typical business processes such as excerpts from regulations (DOT), standards (ISO-9000), and organizational documentation such as Quality Maintenance System and internal business form (travelers, work instructions, bills of material etc.). Our dual-pipeline framework enhances the precision and scalability of fault detection, offering advancements in the automated optimization of business process logic systems. Also, it empowers end users to verify the correctness of processes without extensive technical expertise and mitigate risks associated with faulty business logic. By improving the efficiency of critical workflows, our solution contributes to the overall security and robustness of essential industrial operations.
title: MetaBPL: Fault Detection in Business Logic Systems
Who Controls Physical AI? Orchestration Power in Robotics and Antitrust Law

abstract: Training-time attacks on learning components pose acute risks to robotic and AI-based cyber-physical systems: small amounts of poisoned data can implant backdoors that remain covert under normal operation yet reliably trigger unsafe actions when specific cues appear. This survey focuses on data poisoning and backdoor attacks across the autonomy stack, perception (camera/LiDAR/trajectory prediction), decision-making (deep reinforcement learning controllers), and agentic planners (VLA/LLM-based). We adopt a unified threat model emphasising attacker knowledge/budget and physical realisability, and compare methods using common system-level metrics (attack success rate, performance degradation, latency, time-to-failure). Synthesising nine influential studies, we analyse trigger design, stealth and persistence, transferability to downstream tasks, and failure modes in closed-loop control. We then consolidate defences, dataset governance and provenance, detection/forensics for clean-label and hidden-trigger backdoors, robust training and filtering, and supply-chain controls, and highlight open challenges in physical benchmarking, cross-module backdoors, and certifiable resilience for safety-critical deployments.
title: A Critical Survey of Backdoor and Data-Poisoning Training-Time Attacks in Robotic and AI-CPS

abstract: Modern Artificial Intelligence systems — ranging from large language models to multi-agent architectures and vision classifiers — are fundamentally nondeterministic, opaque, and prone to unpredictable failure modes. These characteristics make them structurally incompatible with safety-critical environments such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, industrial automation, and real-time operational control loops. In this paper, I introduce Lume-V, a deterministic governance layer that validates, explains, certifies, and arbitrates AI decisions before they reach downstream systems. Rather than attempting to force determinism onto the probabilistic models themselves, Lume-V acts as an immutable state machine wrapper. It enforces a strict set of seven non-negotiable safety invariants, generates deterministic explainability traces, issues Ed25519-signed trust certificates anchored to the Lume Trust Certificate (LTC v1.0) architecture, and performs multi-agent consensus-by-safety arbitration. I define a 10-layer architectural specification for Lume-V and demonstrate its effectiveness through a drone control simulation where injected timing and logic faults are safely intercepted, yielding 24 validated decisions, 18 approvals, 6 deterministic overrides, and zero unsafe actuator commands at an average latency of 4ms. Lume-V establishes the foundational mechanism for Deterministic Autonomous Infrastructure Governance Systems (DAIGS), providing a practical, rigorous, and verifiable bridge between nondeterministic AI and real-world systems requiring deterministic safety guarantees.
title: Lume-V: A Deterministic Governance Layer for Nondeterministic AI Systems
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Abstract: Post-quantum cybersecurity is emerging as a defining governance challenge for AI-era digital infrastructure because cryptographic decisions now shape the security of data, machine identities, model supply chains, autonomous agents, public services and cyber-physical systems. This monograph develops an integrated research architecture for understanding and governing that transition. It connects quantum threat horizons and cryptographic assumptions with statistical risk measurement, causal inference, trustworthy machine learning, big-data engineering, reproducible security operations and sector-specific policy design. The argument is that migration must be treated as a continuous socio-technical capability rather than a one-time algorithm replacement. Across five chapters, the manuscript introduces confidentiality-horizon analysis, exposure and readiness models, obsolescence hazards, causal assurance diagrams, Bayesian decisions, systemic-risk simulations, learning-based asset discovery, hybrid-threat detection, federated security analytics, agent authority controls, cryptographic bills of materials, migration digital twins and polycentric governance. The frameworks emphasize explicit assumptions, calibrated uncertainty, human oversight, auditability, continuity and remedy. Comparative application is developed for South Asia, Europe, Africa and the Americas, with attention to uneven capacity, legacy infrastructure, cross-border interoperability and public value. The resulting models, metrics, protocols and governance artefacts support academic research, organizational transformation, regulatory design and multi-year programmes for secure, adaptable and accountable digital infrastructure. Keywords post-quantum cryptography, quantum threat modelling, cryptographic governance, crypto-agility, AI-era infrastructure, harvest-now-decrypt-later, cryptographic bill of materials, causal cybersecurity, Bayesian security decision analysis, systemic cyber risk, trustworthy machine learning, federated security analytics, agentic AI security, model supply-chain security, MLOps, SecOps, Crypto-Ops, migration digital twins, reproducible assurance, digital identity, critical infrastructure, polycentric governance
title: Post-Quantum Cybersecurity and Cryptographic Governance for AI-Era Digital Infrastructure

abstract: Transforming product developmentThe use of artificial intelligence (AI) as part of the food design and development process can offer transformative benefits, but navigating the complexities to successfully leverage the opportunities can be daunting.Here, the focus will be set on key considerations for food and ingredient companies to ensure effective adoption and integration of AI across new product development. The AI moment in food innovationThe food industry's relationship with algorithmic tools and machine learning spans decades: shelf life prediction models, demand and materials planning forecasting systems, and delivery route optimisation have long provided substantial value across manufacturing, logistics, procurement, and sales operations.These established datadriven methodologies remain essential tools, delivering measurable improvements in operational efficiency and cost optimisation.However, today's large language models (LLMs), language reasoning models (LRMs), agentic workflows, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) capabilities represent a qualitative leap that complements and amplifies traditional approaches.Where algorithmic tools excel at pattern recognition and optimisation within defined parameters, modern AI systems integrate and synthesise vast organisational knowledge and data repositories.These work in concert with established statistical models to reason across complex, interconnected variables and help food scientists to reformulate, renew, and reframe existing products and processes.This is especially so with new product development (NPD).Product innovation, one of the industry's most critical yet digitally underserved disciplines, represents the greatest opportunity for AI-driven improvements that build upon, rather than replace existing R&D foundations.Food industry leaders and R&D professionals have long anticipated product development that is faster, moreThe AI shift in food R&D
title: The AI shift in food R&D
Generative Equilibrium for Biomedical IoMT: A CPST-Informed Integrative Review and Conceptual Framework for Security, Privacy, and Clinical Usability

abstract: In the ever-evolving context of the digital twin and Industry 4.0 landscape, it has become increasingly evident that there is a need for a comprehensive framework to maintain the deployed systems that make those cyber–physical systems vital. Deployment management in the cloud-based continuum has become an architecturally complex endeavor to make observable, fault-tolerant, and regulated. Although elaborate Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and sophisticated methodologies define how deployments should be managed in a cloud-based environment, none of them has conclusively determined a framework that ensures minimal human intervention; this is where DepTwin attempts to create a digital replica of systems to handle faults, regulate orchestration and enhance observability. The proposed framework, DepTwin, defines a clear digital twin-based methodology to ensure management of deployed applications in cloud-based environments. It leverages both empirical methods in the form of the proposed Optimal Cloud Resource Identification Algorithm (OCRI) along with ever-evolving large language model-based agents to enhance observability, handle faults, and support resource provider identification in multi-cloud deployment scenarios. DepTwin not only improves application availability and reduces operational overhead but also improves overall resilience to meet Service Level Agreements (SLAs). Evaluated on the iTrust2 health record system across 213 trials with 22 code faults and three resource-degradation scenarios, DepTwin localized faults in 92.4% of trials, repaired 66.7%, and restored SLA compliance in every resolvable resource scenario.
title: DepTwin: A Digital Twin-Based Framework to Manage Deployments in Cloud

abstract: This chapter examines the convergence of quantum computing and artificial intelligence through the emerging field of Quantum Artificial Intelligence (QAI). The discussion explains how quantum principles such as superposition, entanglement, and quantum interference can enhance machine learning, generative AI, optimization, and intelligent systems beyond the limitations of classical computing. The chapter presents concepts of quantum computing, quantum machine learning, quantum neural networks, and hybrid quantum-classical architectures while also discussing applications in healthcare, cybersecurity, finance, manufacturing, and scientific research. In addition, the chapter addresses challenges related to scalability, explainability, cybersecurity, governance, ethics, and unequal access to quantum technologies. The chapter also introduces a conceptual QAI Ecosystem Model and outlines future research directions involving Quantum-enhanced Explainable AI, agentic AI, quantum internet systems, and quantum-safe cybersecurity.
title: Quantum-Enhanced Generative AI
venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series

abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has moved from a peripheral computational curiosity to a central instrument of contemporary engineering design, reshaping how structural forms, materials configurations, and manufacturing strategies are conceived and refined. This paper undertakes an integrative, theory-driven synthesis of the scholarship surrounding generative AI in smart engineering design optimization, with particular attention to generative adversarial networks, variational autoencoders, diffusion-based models, and emerging large language model agents. Rather than cataloguing individual techniques, the study interrogates how these computational paradigms interact with established engineering design theory, including design space exploration, multi-objective optimization, and design for manufacturing. Employing a qualitative, meta-synthetic methodology grounded in a structured review of peer-reviewed literature published primarily between 2014 and 2026, the paper develops an analytical framework that maps generative model classes onto discrete phases of the engineering design lifecycle. The findings indicate a discernible trajectory from narrow, single-objective topology generation toward multimodal, constraint-aware, and increasingly autonomous design agents capable of negotiating competing structural, material, and manufacturability requirements. The analysis further reveals persistent gaps concerning interpretability, manufacturing feasibility validation, and the epistemic role of human designers within increasingly automated pipelines. The paper concludes that generative AI functions most productively not as a replacement for engineering judgment but as a computational collaborator that expands the exploratory reach of the design process while imposing new obligations of verification, accountability, and domain grounding. These insights contribute a consolidated conceptual map for researchers and practitioners seeking to situate emergent generative techniques within a coherent, rigorous engineering design paradigm.
title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Smart Engineering Design Optimization: A Synthesis of Computational Creativity, Structural Performance, and Human-Centered Practice
venue: International Journal of Technology Management and Humanities

abstract: This paper introduces CEOS (Cognitive Enterprise Operating System) and ENACT (Enterprise Cognitive Governance Architecture), a unified meta-framework for designing, governing, and scaling autonomous enterprise systems. CEOS defines the cognitive operating layers required to Sense, Understand, Decide, Act, Govern, and Evolve within complex industrial environments. ENACT provides governance, assurance, semantic alignment, policy enforcement, and responsible autonomy controls that ensure safe and auditable operation of multi-agent AI systems across manufacturing, supply chain, and enterprise functions. The paper proposes the AES (Autonomous Enterprise Stack), an integrated model connecting data platforms, semantics, agents, policies, digital twins, and enterprise workflows. It also introduces the AEMM (Autonomous Enterprise Maturity Model) and a simulation framework for evaluating autonomy readiness. Together, the frameworks provide a structured approach for enterprises aiming to transition from automation to cognitive and autonomous operations. This work is published as an independent research contribution to support practitioners, architects, and researchers building safe, scalable, and governed enterprise autonomy.
title: CEOS & ENACT: A Cognitive Architecture and Governance Framework for Autonomous Enterprises
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Modern discovery is increasingly shaped by an integrated AI–Data–Compute–Governance stack that spans algorithms, software ecosystems, distributed infrastructure, cyber-physical systems, and socio-technical oversight. This review offers a pan-disciplinary synthesis across ten pillars Python/data-science ecosystems; ML/AI foundations including multimodality and RAG/agents; big data and the compute continuum (cloud–edge–HPC/quantum); IoT, robotics, and digital twins; bio/health informatics; geospatial/remote sensing; cybersecurity and privacy; blockchain for provenance; responsible governance; and sustainability/cost. We articulate a unifying lifecycle (design → train → evaluate → deploy → monitor → govern) and map cross-field patterns that consistently determine success: data quality over model size; retrieval-first, knowledge-integrated pipelines; agentic orchestration with strong evaluation; systems-level efficiency (compilers, quantization, distillation); privacy-by-design; and end-to-end assurance for safety, security, and robustness. Methodologically, we consolidate peer-reviewed literature and standards (2015–2025) from major digital libraries, structured via a transparent selection and evidence-grading protocol. The article contributes: (i) a taxonomy aligning methods and systems across scientific domains; (ii) reference blueprints for multimodal RAG/agent pipelines and edge-to-cloud deployment; (iii) comparative tables of tools, datasets, and evaluation suites; (iv) a measurement playbook spanning accuracy, reliability, security, privacy, latency, and energy/carbon; and (v) a 2025–2030 research roadmap prioritizing interpretable multi-agent systems, knowledge-grounded foundation models, privacy-preserving retrieval, green training/serving, and governance-aligned operations. By integrating perspectives from computer science, IT, data/AI engineering, and domain sciences, this review provides a coherent guide for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers seeki
title: Intelligent Science, One World: A Pan-Disciplinary Review of Data Science, Python, Machine Learning & AI Across Big Data, Cloud–Edge & HPC/Quantum, IoT & Robotics, Cybersecurity, Bio/Health Informatics, Geospatial/Remote Sensing, Blockchain, Digital Twins, and Responsible Governance
venue: Scholars Journal of Engineering and Technology

abstract: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks remain a persistent threat to the availability of Internet services, edge networks, and cyber-physical infrastructure. Although recent AI-security work has increasingly focused on foundation models, autonomous agents, and adversarial robustness, many operational defense tasks still require low-latency classification close to the network edge, where cloud-scale analysis may be too slow or expensive. This paper presents a lightweight supervised deep learning approach for DDoS detection using a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on packet-flow representations derived from the CIC-DDoS2019 benchmark dataset. The proposed pipeline extracts packet flows from PCAP traffic, normalizes them to fixed-length representations, and classifies each flow as benign or malicious using a compact CNN architecture with convolution, dropout, pooling, and sigmoid classification layers. On a held-out test set of previously unseen flows, the model achieves 0.9883 accuracy, 0.9864 precision, 0.9784 recall, and 0.9824 F1 score, while processing the evaluated test flows in 0.28 seconds. These results suggest that compact neural models can provide useful early-warning signals for edge-oriented DDoS detection. We further discuss deployment constraints, benchmark limitations, and future directions for cross-dataset evaluation, hardware-aware profiling, and integration with mitigation pipelines.
title: Lightweight CNN-Based DDoS Detection for Resource-Constrained Edge Networks

abstract: This study develops an Agentic AI-driven framework to address critical challenges in digital transformation, including subjectivity. A Dynamic Weight Adjustment algorithm, which is based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DWA-RL), enables adaptive updating of the weights assigned to each evaluation indicator across four capability dimensions: Technology, Organizational, Strategic, and Ecosystem. The empirical validation involved over 8,000 enterprise samples from the World Bank Enterprise Surveys and case studies by MIT. For the training datasets, supplementary synthetic data has been generated by Monte Carlo simulation and Generative Adversarial Networks. The framework achieves 87.3% prediction accuracy, which is 15.8% higher than MIT CISR and 17.5% higher than McKinsey, shows the best dynamic adaptability of 4.6/5.0, and improves the quality of decisions by 28% compared to the traditional experience-based approach. Under volatile environments, the DWA-RL algorithm keeps the decline within 17.6 percentage points, while for fixed-weight methods, the decline is as high as 25.5 points. Manufacturing enterprise transformation trajectories prove balanced four-dimensional capability development over three-year periods. The current study extends dynamic capability theory by introducing mechanisms of autonomous agents and redefining the agent-dominated human-supervised decision paradigm.
title: AI-driven digital transformation: a framework for organizational capability assessment and strategic decision-making in technology management

abstract: IT Service Management (ITSM) has historically been a digitally bounded discipline, limited to data artefacts such as logs, tickets, and network telemetry.This paper introduces Physical-Digital ITSM Integration (PDII) as a new paradigm wherein AI-powered video analytics, deployed on edge computing infrastructure, becomes the primary intelligence layer connecting the physical operational environment to ITSM workflows.Drawing on empirical research, industry case studies, and emerging AI capabilities including Vision Large Language Models (VLLMs), Small Language Models (SLMs) on edge hardware, and agentic orchestration architectures, this paper demonstrates that PDII represents a category-defining evolution of ITSM.The paper contextualises this evolution within India's industrial and regulatory landscape, including DPDP Rules 2025 and Industry 4.0 manufacturing imperatives, and concludes with a practical implementation framework and directions for future research.
title: Physical-Digital ITSM Integration: AI Video Analytics as the Emergent Intelligence Layer

abstract: The average person spends over two hours daily on social media, much of it in passive, low-value doomscrolling that users report as unsatisfying yet find difficult to stop. These feeds are engineered for engagement through mechanisms including algorithmic personalization, social proof, variable reward schedules, and frictionless content delivery. This paper explores repurposing such mechanisms for learning within a synthetic social media platform, a feed where every participant is a large language model agent, tuned to a single real user who is the sole genuine node. While such infrastructure could manufacture an unhelpful echo chamber of synthetic consensus, our focus is on its potential to deliver incidental education through what feels like natural social scrolling. We present a conceptual framework and proof-of-concept prototype grounded in established educational principles including social learning theory, spaced repetition, and stealth education. Where existing agent simulations typically study collective dynamics among agents, we focus on a single user as the sole human on a personalized learning platform. The framework and prototype demonstrate how agents with distinct personas can introduce, scaffold, and reinforce learning objectives through varied feed interactions, suggesting a mechanism for incidental learning utilizing the same mechanics that currently drive doomscrolling.
title: Learnscrolling: Harnessing Attention Economy Mechanics for Incidental Learning via Synthetic Social Media
venue: University of Southern Denmark Research Portal (University of Southern Denmark)

abstract: Episode summary: Explore the unsettling evolution of Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior (CIB 2.0), where AI-driven networks like Matryoshka and tools like Meliorator are transforming the digital landscape into a professionalized factory for disinformation. This episode deconstructs the shift from simple spam to "swarm intelligence," revealing how sophisticated botnets now simulate organic grassroots movements by using fake whistleblowers, laundered news sites, and synchronized amplification to manipulate human psychology and manufacture a false sense of public consensus. As these industrialized operations exploit social divisions and leverage self-coordinating LLM agents, we examine why traditional platform moderation is failing to keep pace with the rise of "cyborg propaganda" and the plummeting cost of creating a fake reality.
