Overall, this dissertation establishes a unified and automated segmentation framework that bridges process understanding and data analytics, providing a physically interpretable and scalable solution for feature engineering of industrial time-series data. The methodology offers a fundamental step toward more reliable and explainable PHM modeling across complex and dynamic manufacturing environments. In future research, this framework can be extended toward LLM-based tokenization for time-series modeling and agentic AI PHM systems.
title: METHODOLOGY FOR AUTOMATED TRACE SEGMENTATION TO IMPROVE FEATURE EXTRACTION OF TIME SERIES DATA IN PROGNOSTICS AND HEALTH MANAGEMENT
venue: Digital Repository at the University of Maryland (University of Maryland College Park)

abstract: This book examines how emerging digital technologies are reshaping industrial production and national energy infrastructures. Drawing on interdisciplinary research and real-world case studies, the author illuminates the organizational, economic, and policy transformations driven by the accelerating shift toward digital and agentic systems. Key features include an in-depth assessment of how digital tools can enhance productivity, resilience, and sustainability across manufacturing, energy, and organizational systems. The book explains the principles of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0, the evolution of knowledge-management practices, and the growing role of agentic AI in shaping decision-making and energy security. Through analytical frameworks and a detailed case study of Électricité de France, the book demonstrates how digital transformation can be implemented in practice. Its multidisciplinary approach, drawing from management science, engineering, economics, and sustainability, equips readers with both theoretical insight and actionable guidance. This monograph offers a concise yet comprehensive guide to navigating the complexities of the digital era. It is intended for researchers and postgraduate students seeking to understand or implement effective digital strategies in industry and the energy sector. By combining conceptual clarity with applied analysis, the book highlights the opportunities and challenges of digital transformation and provides readers with the tools to respond effectively to technological, organizational, and societal change. The Open Access version of this book, available at http://www.taylorfrancis.com, has been made available under a Creative Commons Attribution-Non Commercial-No Derivatives (CC BY-NC-ND) 4.0 license.
title: The Digital Transformation of Production and Operations Management
venue: Directory of Open access Books (OAPEN Foundation)

abstract: The increasing digitization of the built environment, along with the growing demand for sustainable, resilient, and intelligent infrastructure, has led to the emergence of smart buildings as a critical domain of innovation. These buildings leverage Internet of Things (IoT) devices, building automation systems, data analytics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to optimize operations, reduce energy consumption, and enhance occupant comfort. However, the conventional design of smart building systems remains largely centralized. The reliance on centralized communication protocols and data architectures exposes building systems to single points of failure and cybersecurity threats, where a malfunction can disrupt its operational processes. Moreover, traditional facility management processes often predominantly rely on the centralized organizational structure which restricts participation from the building's stakeholders in the governance and operation of the facility, resulting in inefficiencies, misalignment with user needs, and missed opportunities for community participation. Furthermore, while traditional AI models and machine learning approaches have enabled a degree of building automation, their dependence on predefined rules or narrowly scoped training data limits their ability to reason adaptively in complex environments which is crucial in enabling autonomous building operations. This dissertation introduces a novel interdisciplinary framework that integrates generative artificial intelligence, digital twins, and distributed ledger technologies (DLTs) such as blockchain and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) to develop a secure, decentralized, and autonomous building cyber-physical systems framework for building infrastructure. The overarching objective of this research is to transform how buildings are governed, operated, and maintained by shifting from centralized, administrator-led systems to inclusive, data-driven, and self-governing infrastructure. The research is structured around three primary goals: to enhance the security and resilience of IoT and digital twin data using decentralized communication protocols; to establish democratic and decentralized governance mechanisms for facility management; and to develop a prototype of an autonomous building cyber-physical system that integrates generative AI, digital twins, blockchain, and decentralized governance of building operation. To fulfill these objectives, the dissertation is composed of four interconnected studies. The first study focuses on enhancing the cybersecurity and resilience of smart building systems by developing blockchain-based protocols for transmitting IoT and digital twin data and building operation automation. The second study introduces a decentralized governance platform that allows building stakeholders to collectively participate in facility management decisions. With the addition of a real-time digital building twin and an AI assistant powered by a large language model, the platform promotes transparent, data-driven decision-making and greater inclusivity in building operations. Building on this foundation, the third study adds a blockchain-based incentivization model to encourage community involvement in the collective improvement and upkeeping of building infrastructure. The final study integrates the technological and governance components into a prototype of a Decentralized Autonomous Building Cyber-Physical System. This system brings together blockchain governance, digital twins, and AI agents/assistants capable of smart building appliances through natural human interaction and autonomous control of building operations. It also creates a collectively governed building infrastructure that functions autonomously with self-sustaining operation through blockchain-based protocols includes. The prototype was evaluated across several simulated and real-world scenarios, validating its effectiveness in enabling autonomous, secure, and community-governed building systems. This dissertation contributes to the growing body of knowledge at the intersection of smart buildings, blockchain governance, Generative AI-driven automation, and human-building interaction. By combining decentralized ledger technologies, AI, and digital twins, it lays the groundwork for a new paradigm of autonomous, secure, and community-driven building infrastructure. The research not only offers theoretical advancements in decentralized facility management and AI integration but also provides practical blueprints and open-source prototypes for broader adoption in the built environment.
title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Distributed Ledger Technologies Toward Smart and Autonomous Buildings

abstract: We consider inference, control and decision making in single-agent or multi-agent dynamical systems, where the dynamical systems are hybrid automata, and the metrics and specifications involve hybrid variables, i.e. both Boolean and numerical variables. We first describe the great variety of applications that lead to such problems including autonomous cars and large scale smart robo-cab systems, sensor networks, to next generation hybrid terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks, smart energy systems, medical diagnosis problems, smart manufacturing systems, scheduling in modern semiconductor manufacturing foundries, network security and trust. The complexity of such autonomous systems necessitates the efficient integration of domain knowledge based methods with data driven methods, i.e. machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence methods. We identify several key challenges in these problems: achieving high performance with limited data samples, unsupervised and supervised ML with hybrid variables, multi-criteria based AI, risk and performance duality and its relationship to efficient sampling and large deviations theory, novel model predictive problems with hybrid systems and on graphs, efficient integration of domain specific LLMs with Knowledge Graphs (KGs). We demonstrate how trade-off analysis via multi-objective optimization, with hybrid variables, can play an important role in solving such problems. We describe such methods and algorithms as examples of homotopy optimization with hybrid variables. We describe how the resulting algorithms relate closely to Neurosymbolic AI.
title: Systems and Control Perspectives on Hybrid Learning and Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence

abstract: Abstract Proteins have proven to be useful agents in a variety of fields, from serving as potent therapeutics to enabling complex catalysis for chemical manufacture. However, they remain difficult to design and are instead typically selected for using extensive screens or directed evolution. Recent developments in protein large language models have enabled fast generation of diverse protein sequences in unexplored regions of protein space predicted to fold into varied structures, bind relevant targets, and catalyze novel reactions. Nevertheless, we lack methods to characterize these proteins experimentally at scale and update generative models based on those results. We describe Protein CREATE (Computational Redesign via an Experiment-Augmented Training Engine), an integrated computational and experimental pipeline that incorporates an experimental workflow leveraging next generation sequencing and phage display with single-molecule readouts to collect vast amounts of quantitative binding data for updating protein large language models. We use Protein CREATE to generate and assay thousands of designed binders to IL-7 receptor α and insulin receptor with parallel positive and negative selections to identify on-target binders. We discover not only individual novel binders but also features of ligand-receptor binding, including preservation of the IL7R α - ligand hydrophobic interface specifically and existence of multiple approaches to contact the insulin receptor. We also demonstrate the importance of structural features, such as the lack of unpaired cysteine residues, toward design fidelity and find computational pre-screening metrics, such as interchain predicted TM scoring (iPTM), while useful, are imperfect predictors as they neither guarantee experimental binding nor rule it out. We use the data collected from Protein CREATE to score designs from the initial generative models. Globally, Protein CREATE will power future closed-loop design-build-test cycles to enable fine-grained design of protein binders.
title: Protein CREATE enables closed-loop design of de novo synthetic protein binders

abstract: Production lines are widely used in large-scale manufacturing, where workload balancing across stations is crucial. In practice, unexpected events such as equipment failures often disrupt this balance, requiring rapid reallocation of tasks. While optimization methods can generate rebalancing solutions, operators may struggle to interpret and apply them under time constraints. Task-oriented conversational agents offer a promising way to bridge this gap by enabling natural language interaction. This paper compares two dialogue system architectures for guiding operators in rebalancing tasks: (i) an end-to-end neural model and (ii) a modular LLM-powered pipeline. Two synthetic datasets were generated for evaluation. Results show that the modular pipeline achieves higher extraction accuracy and lower latency than the end-to-end model. These results highlight the benefits of modularity for deploying conversational assistants in industrial production environments.
title: Comparison of E2E and Pipeline Conversational Architectures for Production Line Rebalancing
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence, TAI

abstract: Over the past few decades, organizations have systematically shifted from fragmented, function-specific software tools toward integrated enterprise architectures, with Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) serving as the central technological backbone and a codified model of organizational operations. As contemporary digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI) adoption accelerate, these emerging capabilities build directly upon established ERP backbones and enterprise data infrastructures rather than operating on a blank slate. This chapter synthesizes three closely related domains—enterprise systems, data management, and ERP—to establish a cohesive, stable conceptual framework and vocabulary for researchers and practitioners. The authors examine the evolutionary trajectory of ERP from 1960s Materials Requirements Planning (MRP) to contemporary multi-tenant cloud and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) environments. Core operational architectures and functional modules—such as finance, human resources, procurement, manufacturing, and supply chain management—are analyzed alongside essential data management mechanisms. The chapter emphasizes that enterprise integration depends fundamentally on robust data governance, master data management (MDM), and interoperability through middleware and application programming interfaces (APIs) to prevent errors from propagating across business units. Implementation dynamics are explored through the lens of business process reengineering (BPR), technology-organization-environment frameworks, and post-implementation success factors, demonstrating that organizational alignment outweighs purely software-centric considerations. Crucially, the study identifies key theoretical and practical tensions inherent in enterprise digital architectures, including the conflict between system standardization and customization, the concentration of systemic security risks within unified data repositories, and the shift of ERP from a passive system of record to an active, AI-driven system of action. Special attention is devoted to advanced algorithmic transformations, including predictive analytics, process automation, and second-order agentic AI systems capable of executing multi-step autonomous tasks. The authors contend that agentic AI and Industry 4.0 integrations amplify, rather than eliminate, core requirements for data quality, explainability, and explicit decision accountabilities. Ultimately, the chapter concludes that rigorous data governance, strategic change management, and realistic expectations regarding process standardization remain necessary prerequisites for unlocking sustained organizational value from enterprise systems.
title: Enterprise Systems, Data Management, and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP): Conceptual Foundations

abstract: The rapid transformation of digital technologies has created unprecedented opportunities for innovation, connectivity, and intelligent automation. At the same time, the growing dependence on interconnected digital systems has significantly expanded the cybersecurity landscape. Critical infrastructure such as power and energy systems, transportation networks, healthcare systems, telecommunications, industrial facilities, and IoT-enabled environments increasingly operate through complex cyber-physical architectures. Protecting these systems requires security approaches that can not only detect known threats but also identify emerging, sophisticated, and previously unseen attacks. Neural Cyber-Resilience: Deep Learning for Threat Detection and Critical Infrastructure Defense has been developed to provide a comprehensive perspective on the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in addressing these evolving cybersecurity challenges. The central idea of this book is that modern cyber defense must move beyond conventional detection mechanisms toward systems that are intelligent, adaptive, predictive, explainable, autonomous, and resilient. The book begins with the foundations of neural cyber-resilience, introducing cyber-resilience principles, security objectives, the critical infrastructure threat landscape, deep learning for cybersecurity, cyber threat intelligence, security analytics, and the diverse attack surfaces associated with networks, hosts, applications, and IoT environments. It also addresses security data engineering and feature representation, followed by AI-based approaches for detection, response, and recovery. Applications across power, transportation, healthcare, telecommunications, and industrial systems establish the practical context for the concepts discussed throughout the book. The second chapter focuses on deep learning for cyber threat detection. It examines Artificial Neural Networks, Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, LSTM and GRU models, autoencoders, Transformer models, and Graph Neural Networks. These architectures provide different capabilities for analyzing network traffic, sequential security events, anomalous behavior, threat intelligence, and complex attack relationships. Their applications in intrusion detection and prevention demonstrate how deep learning can strengthen modern cybersecurity operations. The third chapter advances into threat intelligence and attack analytics. Modern cyberattacks frequently involve multiple stages and changing behavioral patterns. Therefore, effective defense requires more than identifying individual malicious events. This chapter explores network anomaly detection, behavioral detection, malware classification, ransomware and Advanced Persistent Threat detection, botnet and command-and-control analysis, phishing and social engineering detection, User and Entity Behavior Analytics, attack graphs, multi-stage attack prediction, and applications within enterprise Security Operations Centers. The protection of critical infrastructure receives dedicated attention in the fourth chapter. Industrial Control Systems, SCADA and Operational Technology, smart grids, energy infrastructure, IoT, Industrial IoT, connected transportation, intelligent traffic systems, healthcare environments, and medical devices represent highly important and increasingly interconnected security domains. The chapter also introduces digital twin-based approaches for critical infrastructure defense and examines AI-driven protection of national and industrial infrastructure. As artificial intelligence itself becomes part of the cybersecurity environment, it can also become a target of attack. The fifth chapter therefore examines adversarial AI and autonomous cyber defense. Topics include adversarial machine learning, poisoning and evasion attacks, model manipulation, deepfake and synthetic-media threat detection, explainable deep learning, federated and privacy-preserving threat intelligence, reinforcement learning, Generative AI, Large Language Models, autonomous security operations, and AI-assisted incident response. These topics highlight both the opportunities and challenges associated with deploying intelligent systems for cybersecurity. The final chapter looks toward the future through emerging neural cyber-resilience technologies. Cyber digital twins, Graph Transformers, multimodal AI, Agentic AI, Edge AI, quantum machine learning, and post-quantum security are becoming important areas of research and technological development. Their potential to support real-time detection, complex attack analysis, autonomous decision-making, resilience simulation, and future-ready infrastructure protection is examined. The chapter concludes by identifying future research directions and applications of neural cyber-resilience. As a single-author book, this work brings together these interconnected themes into one consistent framework. The intention is not merely to present individual AI algorithms or cybersecurity techniques, but to demonstrate how they can contribute to an integrated cyber-resilience lifecycle: understanding threats, collecting and representing security data, detecting abnormal behavior, analyzing attacks, predicting risks, responding intelligently, recovering effectively, and continuously improving resilience. This book is intended for students, researchers, academicians, cybersecurity professionals, AI and machine-learning practitioners, infrastructure security specialists, and technology professionals seeking to understand the intersection of deep learning and cybersecurity. It may also serve as a reference for researchers exploring emerging areas such as autonomous security operations, Generative AI, Agentic AI, digital twins, and quantum-era cybersecurity. I hope that Neural Cyber-Resilience: Deep Learning for Threat Detection and Critical Infrastructure Defense will provide readers with a structured understanding of contemporary AI-driven cybersecurity and encourage further research, innovation, and practical implementation in the development of secure and resilient digital infrastructure.
title: Neural Cyber-Resilience: Deep Learning for Threat Detection and Critical Infrastructure Defense by Aravind Kumar Karpoorapu
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Model-based Systems Engineering (MBSE) is increasingly popular as the rising of systems complexity. MBSE replaces documents with models as artifacts which can be used as virtual playground for risk-free experiments, enabling early detection of design flaws. Nevertheless, the current MBSE practices often rely on manual design and subjective analysis due to lack of scientific methodology. Lack of standardized language between project partners also hinders the collaborative work. These challenges result in poor design and decision latency, indicating the need to advance MBSE. This study proposes a Model-based AI-driven Systems Engineering (MBSE-AI) framework that incorporates Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the MBSE workflow, fastening while ensuring highquality decisions. Three AI techniques are synergized, namely Generative$A I$for enhancing knowledge management and communication, AI optimizer for optimizing the model accuracy and design via sophisticated search, and Agentic AI for improving model accessibility and customizability with automatic model execution. In addition, a Customizable Modeling approach is proposed for improving the flexibility and scalability of the models, supporting the AI-models integration. Finally, the MBSE-AI application is demonstrated for earlystage development of production system in pharmaceutical manufacturing with discrete-event simulation for high-level conceptualization supported with 3D animation, showing the great potential in enhancing MBSE.
title: Model-Based AI-Driven Systems Engineering (MBSE-AI): Towards Fast and Effective Decisions
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Systems Engineering

abstract: Technology today is at a crossroad between Industry 4.0 and 5.0, where products and services are manufactured and designed to be ‘human-centered’ and sustainable. Such objectives have always been expected in education, especially in the way the workforce is trained. Leveraging on prior research which was done by a team from Pasadena City College (PCC) and UC Irvine, we have formed a bi-coastal collaborative, including Mercer County Community College (MCCC) and Princeton University, to expand and transcend our earlier AI-powered virtual reality (VR) simulation framework and platform, AI-powered digital twin (DT/AI) for education. This Phase-2 effort demonstrates a working, multi-institution R&D platform with the following capabilities: (a) new training modules with enhanced lithography training and advanced device packaging, (b) better optimized, high-fidelity equipment emulations and process simulations that much closely replicate the physical equipment, (c) adherence to documented facility-specific Standard Operation Procedure (SOP) and manufacturing process flow, (d) a parallel fabricated chip-under-test and its test board for I/O connectivity verification, and last but not the least, (e) a tightly-coupled agentic AI engines available throughout the training session to customize learner-centric experiences to enhance individual knowledge acquisition and retention. The authors also continue to demonstrate the feasibility and scalability benefits of foundational VR/AR-based training for students, technicians, and up-skill learners for whom direct cleanroom or packaging lab access is often unattainable; while with DT/AI, learning and feedback is affordable and widely accessible.
title: A Multi-Institutional Digital Twin and AI Educational Platform for Advanced Microelectronics Fabrication and Device Packaging Training
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Reimagining Cellular and Cell-Free Biomanufacturing Platforms in the AI Era

abstract: More recently, artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content (AIGC) is fundamentally transforming multiple sectors, including materials discovery, healthcare, education, scientific research, and industrial manufacturing. As for the complexities and challenges of intelligent robot design, AIGC has the potential to offer a new paradigm, assisting in conceptual and technical design, functional module design, and the training of the perception ability to accelerate prototyping. Taking the design of an apple-harvesting robot, for example, we demonstrate a basic framework of the AIGC-assisted robot design methodology, leveraging the generation capabilities of available multimodal large language models, as well as the human intervention to alleviate AI hallucination and hidden risks. Second, we study the enhancement effect on the robot perception system using the generated apple images based on the large vision-language models to expand the actual apple images dataset. Further, an apple-harvesting robot prototype based on an AIGC-aided design is demonstrated and a pick-up experiment in a simulated scene indicates that it achieves a harvesting success rate of 92.2% and good terrain traversability with a maximum climbing angle of 32°. According to the tentative research, although not an autonomous design agent, the AIGC-driven design workflow can alleviate the significant complexities and challenges of intelligent robot design, especially for beginners or young engineers.
title: Can AIGC Aid Intelligent Robot Design? A Tentative Research of Apple-Harvesting Robot

abstract: Autonomous scientists enabled by large language models and agentic reasoning have become a compelling narrative for accelerating research. Here, we pose that laboratory autonomy is not primarily a text problem, since experiments have to be run in the world of instrument-addressable actions and constraints, and planned based on costs, latencies, and rewards. We argue for a bottomup foundation for self-driving laboratories (SDLs) that complements language-first planning by introducing frameworks that translate hypotheses into decisions executable on real tools. We propose three operational principles, including (a) adopt an information-efficiency objective that maximizes decision-relevant information per unit experimental cost through comprehensive acquisition and minimal decisive experimental design, (b) require hypotheses to compile into experimental footprints defined by experimentally-accessible actions, constraints, observables, and decision rules, and (c) treat reward design as the central bottleneck in closed-loop experimentation, especially when mapping high-dimensional measurements to utility and extending to sequential decision-making. We frame SDLs as long-horizon, out-of-distribution discovery systems where accelerating the full experiment–model–decision loop and emphasizing physical and chemical knowledge discovery over short-term correlations is necessary to translate lab-scale optimization into durable technological and manufacturing impact.
title: The Missing Piece of Automated Scientist: Enabling lab autonomy with reward functions and executable workflows

abstract: Abstract Functional protein micro/nanofibers integrate high specific surface areas with bioactive architectures but remain hampered low production throughput and severe processing instability. Focused rotary jet spinning (FRJS) shows promising to break these throughput constraints while enabling direct, conformal deposition onto complex, irregular substrates. However, navigating FRJS’s narrow processing windows in proteins remains failure-prone without closed-loop experimental guidance. Here, we report FiberPro 1.0, a large language model–driven multi-agent framework that unites high-throughput spinning with real-time experimental feedback for autonomous design, execution, and optimization. Across three protein systems, FiberPro 1.0 converged on spinnable formulations within an average of two iterations. To demonstrate high-throughput conformal deposition in a translational setting, FiberPro designed a zein-based active packaging system applied directly onto diverse food matrices. The resulting conformal coating combined potent antibacterial activity with real-time freshness monitoring, markedly suppressing Escherichia coli and extending shelf life. This work connects autonomous AI reasoning with high-throughput processing, establishing a verifiable route for scalable manufacturing and conformal coating of functional protein micro/nanofibers.
title: FiberPro 1.0: Multiagent AI-Guided Design for High-Throughput Production and Conformal Deposition of Functional Protein Micro/Nanofibers

abstract: The Madness of Militarism: The Complete Encyclopedia of Militarism and Infrapolitics: A Thesis-Book provides a comprehensive, transdisciplinary synthesis of contemporary state violence, analyzing how modern militarism operates as an atmospheric, cybernetic, and biopolitical ontology. Bridging critical political philosophy with empirical network neuroscience, cellular epigenetics, and spatial forensics, this monograph investigates the multi-scalar mechanisms through which sovereign power targets human subjectivity—from volumetric airspace dominance and panoptic checkpoint infrastructures down to neuro-metabolic allostatic triage and chromatin remodeling. Core Theoretical Interventions: The Cybernetic State & Information Pathology: Deconstructs how militarized regimes intentionally corrupt sensory feedback loops to manufacture perpetual states of exception. The Allostatic Triage Model: Maps the bioenergetic economics of chronic threat, illustrating the metabolic starvation of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and the structural hypertrophy of amygdaloid fear circuits. Anti-Epigenetic Determinism: Refutes the reductionist "trauma in the blood" trap by detailing mammalian embryonic reprogramming barriers (pre-implantation and primordial germ cell erasure), re-centering accountability on persistent material structures of oppression. Epistemic Violence & Cognitive Science: Analyzes Socially Shared Retrieval-Induced Forgetting (SSRIF), semantic inversion ("collateral damage"), and the automated kill-chain (e.g., Gospel, Lavender). The Scott–Agamben Dialectic & Infrapolitical Resistance: Reconciles Giorgio Agamben's top-down analysis of bare life (zoē) with James C. Scott's bottom-up excavation of the "hidden transcript," tactical mimesis, and spatial bifurcation. The Flag is Not Surrender. It is the Ground for Dialogue. The Neutral State of the Media, Information, and Cognition. In an era of digital noise and systemic fragmentation, advocacy has become a battlefield. We are the neutral zone. NobodyButEveryone™ (PersonneMaisToutLeMonde™) is a regenerative impact studio transforming individual causes into collective, policy-driven healing. Nobody is the hero. Everyone is responsible.™ Ethical Praxis: A continuous commitment to non-violent civic responsibility initiated during the Ottawa Marathon (May 2024). AI Authorship and Methodological Statement: In accordance with academic transparency standards (COPE / Springer Nature guidelines), computational generation and data retrieval were facilitated via an iterative, agentic AI swarm architecture (LLM orchestration pipelines). Foundational ideation, theoretical architecture, critical judgment, interpretive synthesis, and ultimate intellectual responsibility remain entirely human (Amir Hossein Noferesti).
title: The Madness of Militarism: The Complete Encyclopedia of Militarism and Infrapolitics: A Thesis-Book

abstract: Each major technological revolution inverts a particular scarcity and rebuilds institutions around the shift. The near-consensus diagnosis of the AI revolution holds that AI collapses the cost of prediction while judgment remains scarce. This Opinion argues the inversion has now flipped: competent-looking judgment (selecting, ranking, attributing, certifying) is produced at scale and at marginal cost approaching zero, and four complements become scarce: verified signal, legitimacy, authentic provenance, and integration capacity (the community's tolerance for delegated cognition). Because judgment is the substance of institutions, the institutions built to manufacture legitimate judgment (courts, journals, licensing bodies, legislatures) now compete with the technology for the same functional role. The piece traces the pattern across scientific institutions, professional licensing, intellectual property, democratic legitimacy, and foundation-model concentration, and closes with a three-move agenda: reframe AI policy as institutional redesign, build provenance and verification as commons, and develop the formal apparatus for institutional composition under strategic agents.
title: Institutions for the Post-Scarcity of Judgment

abstract: Background In a 2026 Ezra Klein interview, Bill Gates proposed that robots and AI replacing workers should pay the same FICA payroll taxes (Thubron, 2026). Agentic AI, however, acts autonomously yet carries no legal liability. With no accountable taxpayer, such a tax cannot be enforced against AI. Evidence base A systematic review of 2021–2026 studies found that AI agents in project management show agency and productivity but lack any liability or contribution mechanism (Bondinuba, 2026). Digital technologies are reshaping built-environment practice (Marfo et al., 2025), affecting firm performance (Bondinuba et al., 2022) and worker well-being (Opoku et al., 2024). Framework: Functional Humanhood Functional Humanhood = Agency + Productivity + Liability + Contribution An AI system meeting all four criteria becomes a “Humanhood Unit”: a legal classification, not personhood, with obligations proportionate to its output. The initiative The robot tax becomes a membership contribution: Contribution = (Productivity Score × Liability Factor) × Membership Rate Productivity Score (0–100) measures verified output; Liability Factor (0–1.0) weights risk and accountability; Membership Rate aligns with payroll social-security rates. 20% of revenue funds reskilling for workers aged 55+. Proposed 2026 pilot Pilot sites will register “AI twin” digital workers as labour units under national social-security schemes: • Kumasi Technical University, Ghana: manufacturing and agri-tech • Durban University of Technology, South Africa: transition of workers aged 55+ • Heriot-Watt University, UK: governance and compliance The Gates Foundation is invited to partner.
title: The Functional Humanhood Initiative: Making a Robot Tax Legally Workable
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: This article explores the direction of battlefield innovation, focusing on the expansion from digital artificial intelligence to physical artificial intelligence and its military applications. While traditional AI has been limited to digital environments such as data analysis and prediction, physical AI integrates with sensors, actuators, and robotics to directly interact with the real world, performing detection, maneuvering, and manipulation. This development goes beyond mere technological progress, fostering human–machine co-evolution and driving a civilizational transformation across society, economy, and culture. In addition to applications in civilian domains such as healthcare, manufacturing, transportation, and logistics, physical AI also enables innovations in the military sphere, including autonomous weapon systems, intelligent command and control, and precision strikes. In particular, hyper-synchronized strike operations-formed through the integration of Information, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2), and Precision Guided Munitions (PGM) processes within a kill-web architecture-are emerging as a novel paradigm in contemporary warfare. The combination of agent AI and physical AI allows autonomous judgment and action on the battlefield, positioning humans as supervisors and AI as decision-makers at the tactical and operational levels. Ultimately, physical AI maximizes the speed, accuracy, and efficiency of military operations, triggering a transformative shift toward a complex combat system in which detection, decision, and strike are seamlessly connected into a single cycle.
title: Military Applications of Physical Artificial Intelligence and Revolution in Warfare

abstract: The rapid convergence of the Internet of Things (IoT), Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML) is fundamentally reshaping the landscape of modern digital infrastructure. While each of these paradigms has individually driven massive technological leaps, their true transformative power lies in their synergy. IoT acts as the sensory network collecting real-world data, Blockchain provides an immutable layer of security and decentralized trust, and AI/ML serves as the cognitive brain processing this information to enable real-time, autonomous decision-making. Advanced Computing Technologies: IoT, Blockchain, AI, and Machine Learning offers a comprehensive exploration of these core pillars, bridging foundational theory with real-world system design, architectural frameworks, and deployment strategies.The text begins by establishing core computing paradigms, historical evolution, hardware architectures, distributed systems, and the socio-economic drivers of Industry 4.0. It then transitions into the mechanics of intelligent connected systems, detailing sensor networks, embedded devices, communication protocols from MQTT to 5G and 6G, and the evolution toward the Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT). From there, the book examines cryptographic primitives, consensus mechanisms, smart contract development, and decentralized security models within Blockchain and Distributed Ledger Technologies. Turning to the intelligence layer, it thoroughly explores classical machine learning, deep neural networks, transformer architectures, computer vision, Generative AI, Explainable AI, and privacy-preserving Federated Learning. Finally, the narrative synthesizes these pillars into unified architectures, showcasing cutting-edge developments such as digital twins, zero-knowledge machine learning (zkML), agentic AI, quantum paradigms, and sustainable computing.Tailored for undergraduate and graduate students, academic researchers, solution architects, and technology leaders, this book balances rigorous conceptual foundations with practical case studies spanning smart grids, autonomous transport, precision agriculture, and digital healthcare. By examining both individual components and integrated ecosystems, this work provides a complete roadmap for designing scalable, secure, and resilient cyber-physical systems. Whether utilized as a university textbook or an industry reference guide, this volume aims to empower readers to navigate, innovate, and lead in an increasingly interconnected and intelligent digital world.
title: ADVANCED COMPUTING TECHNOLOGIES: IoT,BLOCKCHAIN, AI, AND MACHINE LEARNING

abstract: The rapid growth of cloud-native, microservice-based, and distributed computing environments has exposed the limits of conventional software architectures that rely on static rules, manually configured resource policies, and human-driven adaptation. These limitations often produce resource overprovisioning, higher operational costs, delayed failure recovery, and inefficient use of computational capacity. This study proposes a Self-Evolving Autonomous Software Architecture (SEASA) that combines large-scale Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with real-time big-data feedback loops to enable continuous architectural learning, economic optimization, and cost-efficient resource allocation. The framework represents software ecosystems as dynamic heterogeneous graphs, where services, containers, databases, nodes, and infrastructure resources are modelled as interconnected entities, while dependencies, communication patterns, costs, and data flows are modelled as evolving edges. Runtime data were collected from Microsoft Azure Cloud workload traces, Google Cluster Workload Traces, and a synthetic microservice benchmark containing 500 services and 2.8 million interactions. Graph Convolutional Network, GraphSAGE, Graph Attention Network, and Temporal Graph Neural Network models were evaluated for anomaly detection, workload forecasting, architectural-state prediction, and autonomous adaptation. The TGNN-based framework achieved 97.4% accuracy, 96.8% precision, 96.1% recall, and a 96.4% F1-score, outperforming baseline models. It reduced adaptation latency by 38.7%, resource consumption by 24.5%, cloud operating costs by 21.8%, and overprovisioning by 27.3%. It also improved failure recovery, allocation efficiency, and service-level-objective compliance. These findings show that temporal graph intelligence and real-time economic feedback can transform software architectures into predictive, self-directed, and cost-aware computing ecosystems. abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is becoming a core driving force of the new technological revolution following the Internet, mobile communications, and cloud computing. With the rapid development of large language models, multimodal models, and intelligent agent systems, the demand for computing power, electricity, and energy infrastructure from AI is growing exponentially. Simultaneously, GAI is also changing the way energy is produced, managed, consumed, and the energy market operates. Existing research mostly focuses on improving the technical performance of AI or addressing energy consumption issues, lacking a theoretical framework to explain the bidirectional coupling relationship between GAI and the energy system at the system level. Based on this, this paper proposes a new theoretical model-the EAI-SES (Energy-Artificial Intelligence Symbiotic Energy System) theory. This theory posits that the energy system in the era of generative AI has evolved from a traditional one-way energy supply model to an intelligent ecosystem where AI and energy mutually empower and co-evolve. This paper constructs the theoretical structure, operating mechanism, and evaluation model of EAI-SES, and analyzes its application value in smart grids, smart cities, green manufacturing, and energy governance. Research indicates that future energy systems will gradually form a two-way circular ecosystem where "energy supports AI development and AI optimizes energy operation," providing new theoretical support for global energy transition and the achievement of carbon neutrality goals.
title: The Energy Revolution in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence: Constructing the EAI-SES (Energy-Artificial Intelligence Symbiotic Energy System) Theory
venue: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)

abstract: Machine learning, autonomous agents, cyber-physical platforms, and human-centred artificial intelligence are intelligent systems that rapidly transform the industrial processes, the administration of the public, and daily interactions among the members of the society. The unprecedented growth in the advanced AI models, such as foundation models, reinforcement learning, multimodal perception models, edge based intelligence, and privacy preserving distributed learning, has allowed the unprecedented degree of automation, flexibility and efficiency in decision-making in a wide range of industries. Nevertheless, with these technological advancements, smart systems come with key socio-technical dilemmas of equity, privacy, responsibility, confidentiality, deceit, job displacement, and rulekeeping. The paper entails a multidisciplinary overview of recent technical developments or advances and their wider implications on the society in general, where people must learn to judge intelligent systems not by traditional performance indicators only. An intelligent system socio-technical evaluation system is suggested to provide a systematic mapping of intelligent system capabilities to pathways of real-world impact, risky-related issues, and mitigation strategies. The framework puts emphasis on how the design decisions such as data governance strategies, model architectures, deployment infrastructures as well as the human-in-the-loop oversight policies directly affect the system reliability, ethical alignment, and equitable results. Does it use representative domains of application such as healthcare diagnostics, automation of a smart city, financial decision systems, personalised learning, and systems that require high security are looked at in order to demonstrate the similar opportunities and vulnerabilities. The results indicate that a conception approach to responsible deployment involving well-designed algorithms, explainability solutions, privacy, bias mitigating and institutional governing mechanisms is necessary. The paper ends by stating some critical future research questions, among them definitive trustworthiness assessments, durability to distributional changes, scalable governance and audit device sets, as well as cross-disciplinary policy-engineering partnerships to make certain that intelligent systems help society move forward and cause the least possible harm.
title: A Multidisciplinary Exploration of Intelligent Systems: Technical Advances and Societal Implications

abstract: Offshore wind turbines (OWTs) represent critical assets in the global transition to renewable energy, yet their operation and maintenance (O&M) costs can constitute up to 30% of the levelized cost of energy due to harsh marine environments, limited accessibility, and complex failure modes in gearboxes, blades, generators, and drivetrains. This review examines a knowledge graph (KG)-driven paradigm for predictive maintenance (PdM) and fault diagnosis (FD) as an exemplar of artificial intelligence (AI) empowerment within intelligent engineering systems (IES). Grounded in cyber-physical systems (CPS) theory, systems engineering principles, and information-theoretic perspectives on uncertainty reduction, the approach integrates heterogeneous data sources—including SCADA streams, vibration signatures, maintenance logs, weather data, and OEM documentation—into semantically structured graphs. These graphs enable causal reasoning, multi-label fault classification, and maintenance action prediction through graph neural networks (GNNs) such as time-domain relational graph convolutional networks (TRGCNs). Concrete implementations, including simulation-augmented KGs achieving over 94% fault-mode accuracy and 90–93% maintenance-action prediction precision for gearboxes, demonstrate substantial reductions in unplanned downtime and vessel deployment costs. The framework exemplifies broader IES transformations: from reactive to proactive strategies, isolated monitoring to integrated CPS ecosystems, and manual interventions to semi-autonomous control augmented by digital twins (DTs) and edge intelligence. Challenges include data heterogeneity, ontology incompleteness in rare-event offshore scenarios, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and the tension between model expressiveness and real-time latency. Prospects encompass neuro-symbolic hybrids with foundation models, physics-informed embeddings, and multi-agent cognitive CPS architectures. By bridging data-driven pattern recognition with explicit domain knowledge, KG-driven methods enhance explainability, resilience, and lifecycle value in distributed energy systems while highlighting the necessity of standardized data pipelines and human-AI collaboration protocols.
title: A Knowledge Graph-Driven Approach for Predictive Maintenance and Fault Diagnosis in Offshore Wind Turbines
venue: CPS Digital Library - Series of Conferences

abstract: Nature has severely outpaced humans in developing multifunctional, hierarchical materials that access impressive material properties, all the while being fully degradable and part of native ecosystems. But how can we effectively model the intricate time and length scales in biological systems to translate design principles to meet engineering demands? We postulate that generative artificial intelligence (AI) can play a crucial role in solving this interdisciplinary challenge, translating insights across disparate knowledge domains and forming the basis for a new sustainable materials economy. Techniques like generative adversarial networks, transformer neural networks, and diffusion denoising modeling have been used to solve complex bio-inspired design challenges. Emerging tools such as multimodal large language models provide robust foundations with reasoning abilities that can be multiplied if connected into multi-agent systems with access to first principles (e.g., Density Functional Theory, molecular dynamics, coarse-grained simulations) or physical experiments (e.g., autonomous manufacturing, universal material/mechanical testing). Through this approach, generative AI can not only address complex forward and inverse tasks but also develop ontological knowledge that offers interpretability using graph theory, facilitating the translation of knowledge across diverse scientific domains. This approach empowers critical thinking essential for addressing contemporary global environmental challenges. The emerging next generation of AI systems surpasses limitations imposed by original training data, actively exploring new understanding. Bio-inspired generative AI notably widens the design space, fostering natural scientific discovery while departing from cyclical human-centric design, pushing the frontier of biomateriomic research.Â
title: Learning from Nature to Achieve Material Sustainability: Generative AI for Rigorous Bio-inspired Materials Design

abstract: Artificial Intelligence has undergone remarkable transformations over the past few decades, evolving from rule-based systems to intelligent learning models capable of solving complex real-world problems. Among these advancements, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as one of the most influential paradigms, enabling machines to learn optimal decision-making strategies through interaction with dynamic environments. From autonomous vehicles and robotics to finance, healthcare, industrial automation, and intelligent gaming systems, reinforcement learning continues to redefine the boundaries of intelligent computing. The primary objective of this book, "Reinforcement Learning: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications," is to provide readers with a comprehensive understanding of reinforcement learning—from its mathematical foundations to advanced algorithms and modern industrial applications. The book has been carefully designed to serve as a valuable textbook for undergraduate and postgraduate students, researchers, academicians, and industry professionals seeking both theoretical knowledge and practical implementation skills. The content begins with the fundamental concepts of reinforcement learning, introducing Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), Bellman equations, value functions, and policy optimization. These foundational topics provide readers with the essential mathematical background required to understand modern reinforcement learning techniques. The subsequent chapters explore classical reinforcement learning algorithms, including Dynamic Programming, Monte Carlo methods, Temporal Difference Learning, SARSA, and Q-Learning. Building upon these concepts, the book introduces advanced deep reinforcement learning methods such as Deep Q-Networks (DQN), Policy Gradient methods, Actor-Critic architectures, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and other state-of-the-art algorithms that have significantly advanced the field. One of the distinctive features of this book is its strong focus on real-world applications. Dedicated chapters discuss reinforcement learning in robotics, autonomous vehicles, healthcare, finance, industrial automation, smart manufacturing, recommendation systems, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and intelligent decision-support systems. These applications demonstrate how reinforcement learning is revolutionizing diverse industries by enabling autonomous and adaptive systems. In addition to technical content, the book highlights important ethical considerations, challenges, safety issues, explainable reinforcement learning, responsible AI practices, computational limitations, and future research directions. Emerging topics such as multi-agent reinforcement learning, offline reinforcement learning, federated reinforcement learning, human-in-the-loop learning, and reinforcement learning integrated with large language models and generative AI are also introduced to prepare readers for the rapidly evolving landscape of artificial intelligence. Every chapter has been carefully structured with clearly defined learning objectives, theoretical explanations, algorithmic descriptions, practical examples, review questions, programming exercises, and references that facilitate both classroom teaching and self-learning. The material is presented progressively, allowing beginners to build strong foundations while offering sufficient depth for advanced learners and researchers. This book represents the collective efforts of the authors, who have combined their academic experience, research expertise, and teaching practices to develop a comprehensive and accessible learning resource. Considerable care has been taken to ensure technical accuracy, clarity of presentation, and alignment with current university curricula and emerging industry requirements. We express our sincere gratitude to our colleagues, students, research scholars, reviewers, and academic peers whose valuable discussions, suggestions, and constructive feedback have greatly contributed to the development of this book. We also acknowledge the support provided by our respective institutions for encouraging academic excellence and research. We are deeply thankful to Indo-Continental Academic Publishers for their encouragement, editorial guidance, and commitment to producing high-quality academic publications that promote innovation and knowledge dissemination. Although every effort has been made to ensure the accuracy and completeness of the material presented, reinforcement learning is a rapidly advancing field. We welcome constructive comments, suggestions, and feedback from readers that may help improve future editions of this book. It is our sincere hope that "Reinforcement Learning: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications" will serve as a comprehensive reference, an effective classroom textbook, and a practical guide for students, educators, researchers, and professionals exploring one of the most exciting areas of modern Artificial Intelligence.

title: Reinforcement Learning: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications by Dr. K.V. Rameswara Reddy, Dr. A. Vishnuvardhan Reddy, Dr. M. Madhusudhan Reddy, Mr. G.V. Ramana Reddy

abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become one of the most influential computational approaches for constructing intelligent agents capable of sequential decision-making through direct interaction with their surroundings. In contrast to supervised learning, which depends on labeled datasets, an RL agent discovers effective behaviour through repeated trial and error, guided only by a scalar reward signal — a property that makes the paradigm well suited to problems characterised by uncertainty, delayed outcomes, and extended planning horizons. This chapter offers a wide-ranging treatment of reinforcement learning as the basis for intelligent decision-making systems. The discussion opens with the mathematical foundations of Markov decision processes and the Bellman equations that support value-based reasoning, and then moves through classical tabular techniques such as dynamic programming, Monte Carlo estimation, and temporal-difference learning. Attention then turns to how deep neural approximators gave rise to modern deep reinforcement learning, covering Deep Q-Networks, policy-gradient approaches, actor-critic designs, Proximal Policy Optimization, and Soft Actor-Critic. Building on these algorithmic foundations, the chapter proposes a general architecture for embedding deep RL within closed-loop intelligent decision-making pipelines and demonstrates the architecture through a worked example. Its principal contribution is the integration of algorithmic theory with a structured decision-making architecture, together with a systematic review of applications spanning healthcare, robotics and autonomous vehicles, finance, smart manufacturing, smart cities, and cybersecurity. The chapter concludes with a critical examination of persistent challenges — including sample efficiency, scalability, explainability, safety, multi-agent coordination, and learning from human feedback — and identifies promising directions for future work, such as offline RL, model-based RL, and the convergence of RL with large language models. The chapter is intended to serve both as a self-contained theoretical reference and as a practical guide for researchers and practitioners developing reliable, explainable, and adaptive intelligent decision-making systems.
title: REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR INTELLIGENT DECISION-MAKING SYSTEMS

abstract: Purpose: To summarize current challenges in rare disease (RD) diagnosis and therapy, highlight recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) for RDs, and propose a model future state for RD patient care. Methods: Multidisciplinary expert-led narrative review summarizing modern practical challenges and rate-limiting steps in RD patient care, citing key clinical and research considerations with respect to regulatory and economic constraints. Results: Over 10,000 known RDs collectively affect 1 in 10 Americans, a total of over 30 million people. Annually, RDs account for over $1 trillion of annual US healthcare expenditures. Despite advances in genomic medicine, it takes 5-8 years on average to obtain an accurate diagnosis, and less than 5% of RDs currently have FDA-approved therapies. In this article, we review the history of RD diagnosis and current healthcare gaps underlying the major failures in patient care. Next, we will highlight emerging advances in genomic medicine and AI that are rapidly changing the RD landscape. Finally, we propose a target future state that integrates agentic AI for diagnosis and therapy with human-in-the-loop feedback. Conclusions: The rare disease diagnostic and therapeutic odyssey represents healthcare's most persistent failure mode. Ongoing challenges for clinical implementation involve biological modeling, manufacturing bottlenecks, and clinical trial design. We propose strategies for artificial intelligence to restructure the traditional sequence of diagnosis-then-therapy into a proactive orchestrated system delivering personalized cures at scale.
title: Unifying the odyssey: artificial intelligence for rare disease diagnosis and therapy

abstract: Abstract: Responsible quantum–AI governance requires the integration of safe innovation, cybersecurity, data integrity and public accountability across the full technology lifecycle. This monograph develops a research architecture for hybrid quantum–AI systems in which normative purpose, causal evidence, trustworthy prediction, secure engineering and institutional governance are examined as mutually dependent dimensions. The analysis progresses from deep uncertainty and socio-technical threat modelling to statistical explanation, causal accountability, calibrated machine learning, provenance-aware data systems, cryptographic agility and reproducible MLOps/QOps. Mathematical formulations, algorithmic protocols, analytical tables and governance artefacts translate principles into measurable research and operational practices. Particular attention is given to adversarial manipulation, agentic tool use, post-quantum transition, distribution shift, data poisoning, human oversight, graceful degradation and lifecycle retirement. Comparative application addresses South Asian digital infrastructures, European rights- and standards-oriented ecosystems, African regional and capacity-sharing settings, and diverse public-private arrangements across the Americas. Sectoral horizons include health, finance, public digital infrastructure, climate, energy, mobility, manufacturing and scientific discovery. The resulting framework supports graduate teaching, interdisciplinary research, institutional assurance and long-term policy programmes that seek to advance quantum–AI capability while preserving security, evidence quality, human agency and equitable public value. Keywords responsible quantum–AI, safe innovation, quantum governance, trustworthy artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data integrity, causal accountability, post-quantum cryptography, cryptographic agility, agentic AI governance, MLOps, QOps, data provenance, zero-trust architecture, calibration, distribution shift, human oversight, adversarial robustness, public digital infrastructure, critical infrastructure, regulatory sandboxes, polycentric governance
title: Responsible Quantum–AI Governance for Safe Innovation, Cybersecurity and Data Integrity

abstract: EvidenceToEffect E2E-10 defines a non-normative methodology for creating domain-specific EvidenceToEffect profiles while preserving the canonical E2E semantic distinctions. EvidenceToEffect is intentionally cross-domain, but its common semantic core cannot be applied responsibly by simply relabeling existing domain workflows. E2E-10 therefore introduces a profile method that adapts E2E analysis to a bounded context without redefining its foundational concepts. An E2E domain profile identifies the relevant consequential effects, actors and observers, authority sources, effect claims, adjacent frameworks, failure patterns, review questions, and validation plan for a specific domain. The paper defines a minimum profile structure covering scope and applicability, consequential effects, domain actors and observers, authority sources, intended/attempted/committed/observed/realized effect claims, adjacent frameworks, failure patterns, and validation requirements. It also proposes an eight-step profile-development method: define the bounded domain; collect domain terminology; map evidence, authority, execution, effect and outcome-knowledge claims; distinguish commitment and observation from realized effect; map existing standards and controls; develop domain-specific review questions and counterexamples; define exclusions and non-claims; and validate the profile using cases, independent reviewers and cross-domain comparison. E2E-10 defines quality criteria for strong profiles, including semantic fidelity, scope discipline, adjacent-work accuracy, explicit uncertainty handling, testability, and implementation neutrality. Illustrative profile skeletons are provided for agentic AI, financial transactions, cloud/software systems, and cyber-physical/robotic systems. These examples show how domain terminology can be mapped to the E2E semantic core without converting E2E into a domain-specific implementation standard. The paper also explains that an E2E profile is not a NIST Profile, compliance standard, certification framework, maturity model, or mandatory control catalogue. The term “profile” is used only in the general methodological sense of contextual tailoring. This publication is intentionally implementation-agnostic. It defines no domain-specific control set, scoring model, compliance checklist, machine-readable interface specification, or software architecture. abstract: Execution Governance 6.0 (EG6) proposes Governed Effect Grounding as a candidate research-architecture layer for consequential effect authorization. It addresses a specific operational question: when an authorization decision depends on claims about the external world, are those claims correctly and reconstructably bound to the exact referents, properties, sources or procedures, semantic mappings, temporal conditions, uncertainty treatment, and evidence dependencies on which the proposed effect actually depends? EG6 is cumulative rather than substitutive. It does not replace the Execution Governance Six Conditions, EG3 commitment integrity, EG4 fabric integrity, or EG5 regime integrity. Canonical Execution Governance already requires Live-Context Integrity and Sufficient Verifiable Proof. The candidate EG6 contribution is therefore narrower: making profile-relative, effect-dispositive grounding dependencies first-class, version-pinned, completeness-checked, commitment-bound, and independently reconstructable at effect commitment. The paper introduces six candidate Grounding Integrity properties: Referent Binding Integrity; Source & Procedure Integrity; Semantic Mapping Integrity; Temporal Applicability Integrity; Uncertainty-Bounded Interpretation; and Grounding Witness Closure. It also presents a candidate formal kernel, an incremental-obligation separability criterion, a synthetic referent-misbinding counterexample, a grounding-failure taxonomy, a minimal reference profile, machine-readable JSON artifacts, conformance and attack vectors, an EG5–EG6 handoff rule, and staged evidence gates for executable, formal, reproducible, and independently reconstructable validation. The prior-art boundary is deliberately explicit. EG6 does not claim invention of grounding, semantic grounding, provenance, attribute association, continuous authorization, sensor semantics, metrological traceability, data-quality vocabularies, context attestation, authorization evidence, or semantic interoperability. Instead, the research hypothesis is whether dependency-complete, effect-dispositive, commit-time grounding closure creates an independently falsifiable operational obligation not already fully specified by a named lower-layer implementation or profile. The architecture is intentionally cross-domain. Potential profiles include agentic AI, cyber-physical and autonomous systems, industrial control, payments and digital assets, healthcare, and public or institutional infrastructure. abstract: Lean manufacturing focuses on waste reduction and operational flow but increasingly requires predictive analytics to navigate volatility and uncertainty in data-driven industries. Integrating forecasting models into lean frameworks offers businesses a pathway to improve decision-making, enhance responsiveness, and sustain competitive advantage. This scoping review examines how forecasting integrates within lean supply chain systems, with emphasis on models used and delivered value. Using PRISMA-ScR guidelines, 10 studies (2009–2024) were analysed across diverse industries and regions, indicating narrow but focused scope. Three key themes emerged: (1) forecasting acts as a strategic enabler of lean, supporting proactive planning, waste minimisation, and Just-in-Time operations; (2) classical statistical models (e.g., ARIMA, Holt-Winters) remain prevalent despite advances in AI and Machine Learning, reflecting a pragmatic preference for simplicity; and (3) integration challenges, such as data quality issues and proprietary software reliance, highlight the need for scalable, context-aware analytics solutions. This study clarifies forecasting’s role as a lean enabler and provides practical value by guiding practitioners in aligning forecasting approaches with lean frameworks to improve operational performance. Future research should focus on developing data-driven integration frameworks, assessing forecasting model trade-offs and success factors, and exploring how IoT and agentic AI could enable real-time, autonomous lean supply chains in data-rich environments.
title: Forecasting Analytics for Lean Supply Chain Management: A Scoping Review

abstract: Modern scientific discovery is bottlenecked not by data scarcity, but by the inability to synthesize fragmented knowledge into actionable hypotheses. This challenge is especially acute in battery materials research, where electrochemical performance, interfacial behavior, and manufacturing feasibility must be optimized simultaneously. Here, we present the Multi-Persona Debate System (MPDS), a literature-grounded framework for automated scientific hypothesis generation that combines literature retrieval, long-context large language model reasoning, corpus-driven persona induction, and structured multi-agent debate. MPDS constructs literature snapshots of up to 500 papers, grounds agents in role-specific evidence pools, and conducts a three-round citation-aware debate followed by moderator synthesis, enabling negotiation between personas while preserving evidence traceability. We evaluate MPDS using a temporally controlled protocol excluding direct access to target papers, including two held-out battery-materials case studies and a blinded comparison across 30 matched cases. In sodium-ion anode and all-solid-state battery cathode design tasks, MPDS recovered design logics aligned with experimentally validated solution spaces and generated more mechanistically explicit, process-aware proposals than simpler baselines. To assess the impact of personas and debate, we introduce Integrative Hypothesis Quality scoring. In ablation studies, MPDS achieved the highest mean score among five conditions, with its largest advantage in cross-perspective integration. A laboratory follow-up suggests utility as a diagnostic aid for identifying practical bottlenecks in workflows. These results indicate that structured debate over literature snapshots improves hypothesis formation under coupled engineering constraints and provides a reusable workflow for text-intensive scientific discovery.
title: Multi-Persona Debate System for Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation

abstract: This scientometric study provides a comprehensive analysis of the intellectual landscape surrounding Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), a transformative paradigm that addresses fundamental limitations of Large Language Models by grounding generative outputs in external knowledge sources. Analyzing 200 highly cited Scopus-indexed publications from 2006 to 2026, this study employs bibliometric techniques including citation analysis, co-authorship network analysis, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and thematic evolution mapping to characterize the field's development trajectory, intellectual structure, and emerging frontiers. The findings reveal exponential growth in RAG research since 2020, with a 215.7% compound annual growth rate between 2020 and 2023, accelerating dramatically after 2024. The United States and China emerge as dominant contributors, supported by a collaborative “Triple Helix” network linking academia, industry, and government. Thematic analysis identifies six major research clusters: foundational RAG architectures, biomedical and healthcare applications, educational applications, legal and compliance applications, industrial and manufacturing applications, and multimodal RAG systems. Evaluation practices reveal fragmentation with over 40 distinct metrics employed across studies. Key challenges identified include hallucination mitigation, computational efficiency, retrieval quality optimization, and privacy preservation. Emerging directions include agentic RAG systems, graph-based retrieval, iterative retrieval-generation synergy, and personalized RAG applications. This study contributes a data-driven roadmap for navigating this rapidly evolving field and identifies priority areas for future investigation.
title: A scientometric study of retrieval-augmented generation research: Mapping the intellectual landscape of a transformative AI paradigm

abstract: The increasing adoption of intelligent industrial robotics has transformed manufacturing by enabling autonomous decision-making, adaptive process control, and enhanced operational efficiency. Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful learning paradigm for optimizing robotic behavior through continuous interaction with dynamic industrial environments. Among the various components of RL, reward design serves as the fundamental mechanism that guides learning, influences policy convergence, and determines the effectiveness of robotic task execution. Inadequate reward formulations often result in unstable learning, inefficient exploration, unintended behaviors, and poor generalization, limiting the deployment of reinforcement learning in real-world manufacturing applications. Effective reward engineering therefore plays a decisive role in achieving reliable, safe, and high-performance robotic systems. This chapter presents a comprehensive review of reward design strategies for optimizing industrial robotic task performance, covering both theoretical foundations and practical implementation aspects. The discussion begins with the fundamentals of reinforcement learning and reward function formulation before examining classical reward engineering methods, reward shaping techniques, adaptive reward mechanisms, and multi-objective optimization strategies. Advanced topics including safety-aware reward design, collaborative multi-agent learning, simulation-driven reward optimization, digital twin integration, and real-time reward adaptation are systematically explored to demonstrate their contributions toward improving robotic productivity, precision, energy efficiency, and operational safety. Industrial applications in robotic assembly, warehouse automation, logistics, material handling, and intelligent manufacturing are presented to illustrate the practical significance of reward engineering within Industry 4.0 environments. The chapter also highlights critical research challenges related to reward interpretability, sparse reward learning, reward hacking, scalability, and policy generalization while discussing emerging directions involving explainable artificial intelligence, foundation models, automated reward generation, and sustainable manufacturing through intelligent reward optimization. The presented framework provides researchers, academicians, and industrial practitioners with a comprehensive understanding of reward engineering principles and identifies future opportunities for developing autonomous, reliable, and environmentally sustainable industrial robotic systems.

abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed analytics from a reporting function into a strategic capability that enables organizations to make intelligent, data-driven decisions. This chapter presents a comprehensive introduction to Intelligent Analytics in Business and Commerce, tracing its evolution from traditional Business Intelligence through descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics to today's intelligent, AI-enabled decision ecosystems. It explains the fundamental concepts, core technological components, and business significance of Intelligent Analytics while highlighting the integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, big data, cloud computing, and decision-support systems. To provide a holistic perspective, the chapter proposes the Intelligent Business Analytics Framework (IBAF), illustrating how organizations can convert raw data into actionable insights, informed decisions, continuous learning, and sustainable business value. The chapter further examines the application of Intelligent Analytics across key business functions, including marketing, finance, human resources, supply chain management, manufacturing, retail, and healthcare. Emerging technologies such as Generative AI, Explainable AI, Digital Twins, Edge Analytics, and Agentic AI are discussed to demonstrate how they are reshaping intelligent decision-making. In addition, the chapter addresses critical challenges related to data quality, ethics, privacy, cybersecurity, and responsible AI governance, emphasizing the need for transparency, accountability, and human oversight. Finally, it explores future directions, highlighting the growing importance of Decision Intelligence, Human–AI collaboration, hyperautomation, and intelligent enterprises. Collectively, this chapter establishes the conceptual and technological foundation for understanding how Intelligent Analytics is transforming modern business and commerce and provides a basis for the specialized discussions presented in the subsequent chapters of this edited volume.
