abstract: This two-part work introduces the AI Structured Output Governance Layer (ASOGL): an architecture for making large language models reliable for high-stakes decision-making. The first paper makes the strategic case for business and organizational leaders, grounding the problem in real enterprise AI failures and positioning ASOGL as a lightweight alternative to full-scale data ontologies. The second is an engineering blueprint for practitioners, translating that framework into a concrete pipeline, code patterns, and a worked case study. They make one argument from two directions: an AI system's value lies not in the fluency of its generation, but in the rigor of the verification built around it.
title: AI Structured Output Governance Layer (ASOGL)
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Competency Questions (CQs) are the central component of CQ-verification, an established process in which an ontology is evaluated against a set of natural language questions to determine whether the intended purpose of the ontology has been properly modelled. However, CQ-verification is often time-consuming and error-prone, as it requires careful interpretation of linguistic nuances and precise alignment with formal ontology constructs. Ambiguities and complexity in CQs can further complicate this process, leading to inconsistent modelling decisions and verification outcomes. In this paper, we investigate what makes a CQ challenging and possible solutions to enhance the users' performance in the CQ-verification process. We experimented with the data of 19 participants who performed CQ-verification on 20 tasks using an LLM assistant to support ontology evaluation. The results show the necessity of a tool to refine CQs before publishing them to avoid ambiguity or excessive complexity in later phases of the ontology engineering process.
title: When CQs Go Wrong: Challenges in CQ Verification with OE-Assist

abstract: With the advent of large AI models empowering Chinese higher education and the development of new engineering disciplines, this paper explores a course reform pathway leveraging AI large models to address common challenges in university-level Data Structures courses. These include abstract and difficult-to-grasp content, disconnect between theory and practice, significant student variation, and limited assessment methods. Guided by Outcome-Based Education (OBE) and student-centered principles, this approach integrates large language models like DeepSeek with knowledge graph technology to establish a closed-loop teaching process spanning pre-class, in-class, and post-class activities. This forms a pedagogical model featuring “intelligent resource generation, tiered progressive instruction, human-machine collaborative classrooms, and data-driven assessment.” Concurrently, an industry-academia integration platform is introduced to deepen the connection between data structures knowledge and AI engineering applications. Teaching practices involving 300 students over two academic years demonstrate that this reform significantly enhances students’ academic performance, engineering practice capabilities, and innovative outcomes. This validates the effectiveness and scalability of leveraging AI large models to empower teaching reform in the Data Structures course.
title: Large AI Models based Learning Reform in Data Structures Courses for Chinese Higher Education
venue: International Conference on Big Data and Informatization Education (ICBDIE)

abstract: To address the problems of insufficient extraction accuracy and inadequate utilization of contextual conditions for structured knowledge extraction from vertical domain documents, this paper proposes a dynamic prompt scheduling and context co-optimization knowledge graph extraction (DyPOKE) method. By adopting semantic chunking, dynamic prompt template scheduling and context-injection mechanisms, this method enables collaborative modeling of prompt strategies and semantic condition. Experiments are conducted based on texts of manufacturing-processing and antenna-design domains, with comparisons against the baseline methods such as one-stage joint neural information extraction with global features (OneIE), relation extraction by end-to-end language generation (REBEL), and extract-define-canonicalize (EDC), as well as against various prompting configurations. The experimental results show that DyPOKE method achieves favorable performance on both entity recognition and relation extraction tasks, with F1 scores of 0.90 and 0.86, respectively. Ablation experimental results further indicate that for the relation-extraction task, DyPOKE method improves the F1 score by 7.5% compared with the second-best prompt configuration. Cross-model transfer experiments further demonstrate that DyPOKE method maintains stable output performance over different underlying large language models. These results indicate that the collaborative design of dynamic prompt scheduling and contextual constraints contributes to improving the reliability of structured knowledge extraction in vertical domains, providing a reusable framework for the automatic construction of specialized domain knowledge graphs.
title: Dynamic prompt scheduling and context co-optimization for domain-oriented knowledge extraction
venue: JOURNAL OF SHENZHEN UNIVERSITY SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING

abstract: Purpose A persistent gap exists between abundant safety documentation and its effective conversion into actionable knowledge in bridge construction safety. While knowledge modeling offers a promising solution, unresolved issues remain regarding knowledge granularity and the boundaries of model advantage. This study develops a Bridge Engineering Construction Safety Knowledge Model (BECS-KM) to narrow this gap and to investigate these challenges. Design/methodology/approach BECS-KM is built using ontology and knowledge graph techniques grounded in codes and standards. A multilayered representation structure is incorporated to balance knowledge granularity, and a comparative experiment is conducted to evaluate the strengths boundaries of BECS-KM versus ChatGPT-5. Findings In terms of knowledge modeling, the multilayered structure effectively balances knowledge granularity within BECS-KM. Regarding knowledge application, the comparative experiment demonstrates the superiority of BECS-KM (F1 = 0.97) over ChatGPT-5 (F1 = 0.83) of domain knowledge queries. Originality/value This study makes three contributions: (1) transforms fragmented and heterogeneous safety documentation into a structured and operational knowledge resource, (2) provides a multilayered representation structure to balance knowledge granularity and (3) empirically delineates the performance boundary of domain knowledge models against general LLMs. Together, these contributions establish BECS-KM as a robust foundation for future intelligent safety knowledge services.
title: BECS-KM: a multilayered domain knowledge model for bridge construction safety with experimental validation
From perception to governance: Knowledge-enhanced intelligence for smart sustainable buildings

abstract: Abstract & Description:Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) frameworks rely primarily on dense vector databases to retrieve unstructured text snippets for Large Language Model (LLM) grounding. However, real-world enterprise environments process highly heterogeneous data formats, including knowledge graphs, relational tables, and unstructured documents. Single-modality vector retrieval struggles with multi-hop logical reasoning, structured relational constraints, prompt security, and context hallucination. To address these systemic limitations, this research manuscript proposes a novel, closed-loop Advanced RAG architecture incorporating adaptive multi-database routing, hierarchical rank fusion, and end-to-end security guardrails. The proposed pipeline introduces an input query guardrail for adversarial prompt mitigation, followed by query decomposition into atomic sub-queries. Each sub-query is routed dynamically across Graph, Vector, and Relational databases via an intelligent routing layer with caching. Retrieved candidates are aggregated using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and refined using a neural Cross-Encoder re-ranker. Finally, output guardrails assess answer relevance and factual grounding before committing verified key-value pairs back to the semantic cache. This preprint formulates the mathematical rigor of the pipeline, presents algorithmic execution flow, and outlines a qualitative capability comparison establishing the theoretical superiority of the proposed framework over existing RAG paradigms. Keywords: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Query Decomposition, Adaptive Routing, GraphRAG, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, Cross-Encoder, Guardrails, Semantic Caching.Category: Computer Science / Artificial Intelligence / Information RetrievalType: Preprint / Research ManuscriptAuthor: Snehil Yadav (Department of Computer Applications, Institute of Engineering and Technology, Lucknow, India)
title: A Multi-Database Adaptive Routing and Dual-Guardrail Hierarchical Architecture for Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Realizing the full potential of digital twins in facility management requires prescriptive modeling that does more than describe current states — it must anticipate operational needs, recommend actions, and adapt as conditions evolve. However, this remains difficult due to fragmented data silos and the lack of flexible mechanisms to connect diverse information sources. Most existing methods rely on rigid schemas or predefined ontologies which constrain adaptability. This dissertation proposes a no-model, dynamic linkage framework that connects structured and unstructured datasets without enforcing strict predefined standards. The resulting framework supports prescriptive digital twins (PDTs) that evolve in parallel with the built environment. Built on this foundation is a system that leverages knowledge graphs and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) to bridge fragmented data sources and drive prescriptive analytics in facility management. The work begins by identifying conceptual and practical limitations in current prescriptive analytics within the built environment. A review of over 600 studies reveals that prescriptive modeling in Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) is often underdeveloped and rarely connected to operational data. In response, the dissertation proposes a graph-based digital twin architecture that integrates structured and unstructured datasets using adaptive, schema-agnostic representations. One instantiation of the system takes the form of a multi-agent platform powered by large language models and equipped with a user-facing interface for natural language querying. Through extensive evaluation across BIM models and facility work orders, the system demonstrates high query accuracy, semantic alignment with Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) standards, and significant improvement in retrieving actionable insights from unstructured maintenance data. In addition, by combining domain-specific fine-tuning with agentic reasoning, the research shows how GenAI-equipped knowledge graphs can support both interpretive and prescriptive tasks in facility operations. The result is a blueprint for constructing intelligent, user-centric digital twins capable of adapting to dynamic facility environments, and a methodological foundation for future work at the intersection of AI, construction informatics, and operational decision support.
authors: Amirhossein Babaei Ravandi Amirhossein Babaei Ravandi
title: A Platform for Prescriptive Digital Twins in AEC

abstract: Sahayak AI is an advanced AI-powered educational assistant system designed to enhance learning through an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline. The system integrates query rewriting, semantic retrieval, re-ranking, conversational memory, and prompt engineering to deliver accurate and context-aware responses. The platform supports multi-modal learning, including document-based Q&A, summarization, AI-generated notes, and personalized recommendations. Additional features include multilingual support, voice interaction, knowledge graphs, and real-time progress tracking. This work presents the system architecture, pipeline design, and implementation details, demonstrating how modern LLM-based systems can transform digital education.
title: Sahayak AI: An Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Intelligent Educational Assistance
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

abstract: Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines are foundational to modern software delivery, yet remain reliant on rigid, pre-defined scripts that lack the flexibility to handle unforeseen anomalies. While prior surveys have examined Large Language Model (LLM) agents for general software engineering tasks, none have focused specifically on CI/CD orchestration and the transition from automation to autonomy. Through a structured review of 72 papers published between 2023 and 2025 and sourced from IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and arXiv, this survey addresses that gap. The 72 studies are distributed across three primary application domains: autonomous code generation and repair (28 papers), intelligent verification and environment setup (23 papers), and incident management with root cause analysis (21 papers). We propose the PARA (Perception, Action, Reasoning, Reflection) framework as an operational lens for analyzing agentic CI/CD systems. Comparative analysis of five representative systems yields concrete performance figures: SWE-agent resolves 12.5% of issues against a 3.8% scripted baseline; the DEI multi-agent committee reaches 34.3% versus 27.3% for single-agent baselines; CXXCrafter achieves 71.2% success on C/C++ builds compared with 45% for general-purpose agents; MACOG reaches 74.02% on Terraform synthesis, dropping to 61.45% when its Security Prover is ablated; and Flow reports a 67% reduction in Mean Time to Resolution for incident triage. Reported task success across the 72 studies ranges from 15% to 75% as a function of task complexity, and self-correction loops add a further 4–5% per iteration at exponential token cost. Challenges spanning economic viability, security risks, and reliability concerns are systematically analyzed. We conclude that the shift from scripted automation to autonomous agents represents a significant evolution in DevOps practices toward intent-driven orchestration, and outline future directions, including Knowledge Graph-augmented LLMs and standardized Agent-Tool Protocols.
title: From Automation to Autonomy: A Survey of Agentic Workflows in CI/CD Orchestration
venue: International Journal of Innovations in Science and Technology

abstract: The article presents the initial stages of developing an intelligent information retrieval system on the website of the FRC KSC RAS, based on the use of large language models, ontological and prompt-engineering, and RAG-technology. The system is aimed at increasing the relevance of responses to user queries formulated in the dialogue process in natural language and related to the website content, as well as to the electronic repository of documents of the FRC KSC RAS. The system architecture has been designed, and a prototype has been developed that implements some of the proposed features of intelligent retrieval. The use of RAG-technology allows for analysis of current context without the need to retrain a large language model, which is especially important in situations where information on a website can be added and modified ad hoc. For some query types, specialized prompts have been developed to allow you to formulate an answer that corresponds to the specific of the query. In order to prevent the transfer of confidential information to external services, it was decided to deploy the software system locally on the server of the IIMM KSC RAS. The experiments carried out demonstrated the feasibility of the proposed solutions for the considered tasks of intelligent retrieval.
title: OPPORTUNITIES FOR INTELLIGENTIZATION OF THE FRC KSC RAS WEBSITE
