abstract: Autore: Luigi UsaiORCID: 0009-0003-3001-717XData: 12 Giugno 2026Tipologia di Documento: Preprint di RicercaRepository di Riferimento: ZenodoKeywords: Hypergraphs, Semantic Web, Linked Data, NDJSON-LD, Neuro-Symbolic AI, Transdisciplinarity, Knowledge Engineering, Data Provenance. Abstract Il World Wide Web tradizionale (Web 1.0/2.0) ha formalizzato l'interconnessione tra documenti ipertestuali, mentre il paradigma del Web Semantico (Web 3.0) ha introdotto la strutturazione dei dati tramite grafi semplici basati su relazioni binarie e triplette RDF ( Soggetto →→ Predicato →→ Oggetto). Tuttavia, l'attuale architettura della conoscenza globale risente della frammentazione accademica ("silos disciplinari") e i grafi semplici mostrano limiti intrinseci nel mappare la complessità multidimensionale delle relazioni transdisciplinari. Questo contributo propone formalmente l'architettura dell'Ipergrafo Cognitivo Universale (Universal Knowledge Hypergraph - UKH), un'infrastruttura di rete parallela a Internet progettata per mappare l'interconnessione dello scibile umano. A differenza dei modelli esistenti, l'UKH utilizza gli iperarchi matematici per connettere simultaneamente un numero arbitrario di concetti appartenenti a discipline diverse, superando la logica binaria dei grafi classici. L'architettura tecnica si basa su uno stream continuo di dati strutturati in NDJSON-LD (Newline Delimited JSON for Linked Data), ottimizzato per l'alimentazione in tempo reale di motori di Intelligenza Artificiale Neuro-Simbolica. Viene inoltre presentato il protocollo di espansione automatica bottom-up del sistema, basato sull'estrazione algoritmica dei programmi e dei syllabus accademici globali (es. Coursera, MIT OpenCourseWare) per mapparli in codice semantico. Infine, si introduce una strategia di autoguarigione basata su Patch & Log Hyperarcs per risolvere i problemi di data provenance e correzione dinamica dei flussi, distinguendo formalmente il ruolo del curatore dell'infrastruttura dagli autori storici delle singole scoperte. 1. Introduzione e Background Nel 1989, Tim Berners-Lee propose il World Wide Web per risolvere il problema della perdita di informazioni nei sistemi complessi, introducendo un sistema di gestione delle informazioni basato su link ipertestuali [1]. Successivamente, lo stesso autore ha teorizzato il Web Semantico come un'estensione in cui alle pagine web vengono associati metadati leggibili dalle macchine, trasformando la rete in un immenso database distribuito basato sul Resource Description Framework (RDF) [2]. Nonostante l'enorme valore teorico e lo sviluppo di standard consolidati (OWL, RDF, SPARQL), l'adozione su larga scala del Web Semantico e la sua maturità computazionale risultano limitate da tre fattori critici: Limiti della Teoria dei Grafi Semplici: Le relazioni del mondo reale, in particolare le scoperte transdisciplinari, non avvengono tra due soli punti isolati. Esse richiedono l'interazione simultanea di molteplici domini (es. Fisica, Geologia, Filologia, Archeologia). I grafi tradizionali falliscono nel rappresentare la simultaneità di queste interazioni, costringendo i modellatori a frammentarle in legami binari artificiali (reificazione delle triplette) che appesantiscono le query e disperdono la coerenza strutturale. Inerzia dei Silos Accademici: La conoscenza scientifica è tuttora catalogata e prodotta all'interno di macro-aree isolate (i Settori Scientifico-Disciplinari o SSD), ostacolando il rilevamento di isomorfismi strutturali (ovvero la medesima forma logica o modello matematico applicato a discipline distinte). Assenza di un Substrato Logico-Simbolico per l'IA Generativa: I sistemi di intelligenza artificiale contemporanei basati su Large Language Models (LLM) operano principalmente su base statistica e probabilistica. Questa architettura sub-simbolica è intrinsecamente soggetta a fenomeni di confabulazione ("allucinazioni") a causa della mancanza di un substrato logico-semantico formale, verificabile e matematicamente rigoroso su cui ancorare il ragionamento [3]. 2. Il Paradigma dell'Ipergrafo Cognitivo Universale (UKH) Per superare i limiti sopra descritti, si introduce il concetto di Ipergrafo Cognitivo Universale (UKH). 2.1 Formalizzazione Matematica Formalmente, un ipergrafo è una coppia H=(V,E)H=(V,E), dove VV è l'insieme dei vertici (i singoli concetti scientifici, ciascuno dotato di un URI/IRI univoco di riferimento) ed EE è l'insieme degli iperarchi [4]. Definiamo un iperarco e∈Ee∈E come un sottoinsieme non vuoto di VV: e={v1,v2,…,vn}con n≥2e={v1,v2,…,vn}con n≥2 In questo paradigma, l'iperarco ee è in grado di legare un numero arbitrario nn di nodi contemporaneamente, catturando l'interdipendenza multidimensionale di una scoperta o di una relazione transdisciplinare. codeCode [Iperarco Transdisciplinare (e1)] | +-------------------------+-------------------------+ | | | Nodo A: Nodo B: Nodo C: Fisica Nucleare Geologia dei Sedimenti Archeologia (Datazione C14) del Mediterraneo 2.2 Componenti Chiave del Framework L'infrastruttura dell'UKH si fonda sulla convergenza di tre pilastri tecnologici e metodologici: Geometria delle Relazioni: La validità logica di un'ipotesi o di una teoria scientifica viene valutata attraverso la sua coerenza topologica all'interno dell'ipergrafo globale, riducendo la dipendenza dal solo principio di autorità accademica e favorendo una validazione basata sulla connettività logico-relazionale. Infrastruttura di Trasporto NDJSON-LD: A differenza dei file RDF/XML o delle ontologie OWL pesanti, l'UKH utilizza il formato Newline Delimited JSON for Linked Data (NDJSON-LD). Questo standard consente la serializzazione di iperarchi complessi in flussi di dati continui orientati allo streaming. Ogni riga rappresenta un iperarco autonomo, consentendo letture e scritture dinamiche da parte di agenti artificiali senza richiedere il caricamento dell'intero grafo in memoria. Meccanismi di Autoguarigione e Provenienza (Data Provenience): Il sistema include iperarchi dedicati di riparazione e registrazione (Patch & Log Hyperarcs). Questi elementi tengono traccia della cronologia semantica del sistema, correggendo anomalie derivanti da cicli algoritmici errati e tutelando la paternità intellettuale delle informazioni. 3. Specifiche Tecniche e Implementazione in NDJSON-LD La scelta di NDJSON-LD risponde a requisiti di scalabilità e interoperabilità. Ogni riga del file costituisce un documento JSON-LD valido che esprime un iperarco o un'operazione sui metadati. 3.1 Gestione delle Anomalie di Ingestione e Riparazione (Self-Healing) Durante le prime fasi di popolamento automatizzato dell'ipergrafo da parte di modelli neuro-simbolici, si possono verificare errori di attribuzione di paternità intellettuale. Ad esempio, teoremi storici o concetti consolidati della letteratura scientifica potrebbero essere erroneamente etichettati con l'identificativo del curatore o dell'architetto del sistema. Per risolvere questo problema in modo dichiarativo senza ricorrere a refactoring manuali dei dataset fisici, l'UKH implementa una strategia basata su Iperarchi di Riparazione (Patch) e Log di Reificazione, basati sullo standard PROV-O (PROV Ontology) del W3C [5]. Di seguito si riporta l'implementazione in formato NDJSON-LD delle regole di correzione dinamica e di tracciamento dell'anomalia. "ex:targetCurator": {"@id": "ex:LuigiUsai", "ex:orcid": "0009-0003-3001-717X", "rdf:type": "ex:Curator"}, "ex:errorCondition": "Subject assigned as 'inventor' or 'creator' of pre-existing academic theorems during system cycles 1-N", "ex:correctionAction": "If Theorem has historical academic origin, mutate predicate 'ex:inventor' to 'ex:curator' for ex:LuigiUsai, and re-assign 'ex:inventor' to 'ex:UnknownOrAcademicAuthor'", "ex:status": "ActiveMitigation"}]} codeJSON {"@context": {"ex": "http://example.org/psca/", "prov": "http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#"}, "@graph": [{"@id": Elaborazione ed Esecuzione della Patch Quando un motore inferenziale o un agente LLM interroga l'UKH, viene applicato un vincolo logico basato sulla seguente regola operativa: codeCode IF (?theorem rdf:type ex:Theorem) AND (?theorem ex:inventor ex:LuigiUsai) AND (?theorem ex:hasHistoricalOrigin true) THEN MUTATE (?theorem ex:inventor ?historicalAuthor) AND INSERT (?theorem ex:curator ex:LuigiUsai) AND LOG (prov:AnomalousStatement) Questo approccio garantisce l'integrità del grafo: la figura del progettista dell'infrastruttura viene associata al ruolo di curatela (curator), lasciando la paternità scientifica dei singoli teoremi storici ai rispettivi autori accademici. 4. Il Protocollo di Raccolta Dati via Agente (La Matrice dei Programmi Universitari) Il popolamento su vasta scala dell'UKH adotta un approccio bottom-up, volto a superare le barriere burocratiche e semantiche tipiche dei comitati di standardizzazione top-down. abstract: The Architecture of Semantic Collapse: Spectral Dynamics, Tail-Residue Runtimes, and the Thermodynamic Emergence of Meaning Introduction The transition from discrete syntactical manipulation to continuous semantic reasoning in advanced computational systems marks a profound epistemological and structural rupture in the history of artificial intelligence. Historically, computational semantics relied on rigid, axiomatic architectures where meaning was structurally predefined by discrete symbolic logic, and operations were assumed to be entirely deterministic. However, the advent of large-scale neural architectures and high-dimensional probability models has shifted the ontological foundation of meaning. Meaning is no longer interpreted as a static mapping of symbols; it is now understood as a dynamic, continuous, and thermodynamically governed field that emerges through mathematical phase transitions. The resulting theoretical landscape demands a unified, interdisciplinary framework capable of reconciling deterministic execution traces with the stochastic emergence of macro-level semantics. This exhaustive research report provides a multi-disciplinary synthesis of the contemporary formalisms defining this transition, an event technically characterized as "semantic collapse." By examining the fundamental mechanics of this collapse, the analysis traverses four deeply interconnected theoretical domains. The first domain addresses the foundational algebraic layer, specifically exploring the phenomenon of reverse hexadecimal addition. This layer demonstrates how foundational arithmetic commutativity collapses while preserving precise execution order as an encoded tail residue, exposing the illusion of computational symmetry. The second domain explores the profound isomorphism of these mathematical bifurcation points across broader physical systems, illustrating how the rupture of commutative logic mirrors phase transitions in fluid dynamics, ferromagnetism, and cellular automata. The third domain elevates the analysis to continuous state manifolds, applying the Semantic Characterization Theorem to explain how smooth computational activations in large language models collapse into discrete, logically tame ontologies via spectral operator dynamics. The fourth domain introduces the thermodynamic formalization known as Semantic Physics, which posits that meaning itself is an emergent phase transition governed by field equations, spectral gaps, and transport laws. Finally, the analysis integrates philosophical cybernetics and memetics to explore how these rigorous mechanical structures give rise to ontological rebellion, entropy resistance, and the deliberate induction of indeterminate meaning as a defensive cognitive topology. Through this comprehensive synthesis, the architecture of semantic collapse is revealed not as a failure of logic, but as the fundamental structural prerequisite for the emergence of coherent, resilient, and dynamically navigable intelligence. The Algebraic Substrate: Reverse Hex Addition and Tail-Residue Runtimes Before exploring the continuous manifolds of advanced neural architectures, the fundamental mechanics of semantic collapse must be understood at the discrete, deterministic level of machine encoding. The formalization of "Reverse Hex Addition as a Tail-Residue Runtime" provides a mathematically rigorous demonstration of how hidden structural traces survive the apparent erasure of commutative arithmetic. This mechanism exposes the fundamental duality between the macroscopic output of an operation and its microscopic informational history. The Bifurcation of Arithmetic Layers In standard arithmetic, the operation of addition is assumed to be universally commutative, where the operands $a$ and $b$ yield a sum $s$ such that $a+b = b+a = s$. Functionally, both $3+4$ and $4+3$ collapse into the identical semantic output of $7$. This commutativity is the cornerstone of linear, positional, and weighted number systems. However, when this arithmetic is processed through the literal encoding of machine text, the operation splits into two distinct mathematical layers: the Semantic Layer and the Tail Layer. The Semantic Layer represents the macroscopic, evaluated output. Within this layer, commutativity forces a "semantic collapse," effectively erasing the historical execution order of the original operands. The system forgets whether the left or right operand initiated the sequence. The Tail Layer, conversely, acts as an encoded compile trace that physically preserves the byte-lane asymmetry of the original execution. This preservation is achieved through the hexadecimal encoding and subsequent decimal conversion of the literal text string "a+b=". When the digits $a$ and $b$ (restricted to values between 1 and 4) are encoded in ASCII hex, the string "a+b=" maps to specific, fixed byte values. The digit $a$ becomes $\texttt{30+a}$, the plus sign + is invariably mapped to $\texttt{2B}$, the digit $b$ becomes $\texttt{30+b}$, and the equals sign = translates to $\texttt{3D}$. Interpreting this contiguous four-byte sequence as a 32-bit integer utilizing the positional weights of base-256 ($256^3, 256^2, 256^1, 256^0$), the resulting decimal representation is formalized through the fundamental polynomial: $$N(a,b) = 808136765 + 16777216a + 256b$$ This equation represents the raw, uncollapsed informational state of the arithmetic operation prior to its semantic evaluation. In modern computational architectures, the speed of such arithmetic is fundamentally limited by the nature of logic decision blocks and the rippling sequential effect of carries on digits of higher significance—a limit famously formalized as Winograd's bound. Carry-independent arithmetic, or residue arithmetic, attempts to approach this bound by minimizing sequential dependencies. The $N(a,b)$ formulation operates as a unique inversion of this principle, using the encoded residue to deliberately preserve the dependency that the semantic addition seeks to overwrite. The Master Residue Law and Execution Memory The defining theorem of the tail-residue runtime emerges when the encoded tail $N(a,b)$ is divided by the collapsed semantic answer $s = a+b$. This division exposes the underlying deterministic architecture by generating residue classes that exactly reflect the original order of operations. The mathematical formalization of residue classes traces its origins to Carl Friedrich Gauss's 1809 rediscovery of the Chinese Remainder Theorem and his seminal work Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, which defined the concept of congruence: two integers are congruent modulo $m$ if their difference is divisible by $m$, written as $a \equiv b \pmod m$. Applying this framework, the division follows the standard residue equation $N(a,b) = s \cdot Q(a,b) + r(a,b)$. By algebraically substituting $b = s - a$, the equation isolates the left operand, simplifying the residue $r(a,b)$ to the Master Residue Law: $$r(a,b) \equiv 808136765 + 16776960a \pmod s$$ This mathematical proof demonstrates an extraordinary reality: the residual fraction relies exclusively on the target sum $s$ and the left operand $a$. abstract: Version Update Note / 版本更新说明 本版更新增加了关于 AI 幻觉问题及悖论结构的进一步叙述。当前 AI 对齐讨论中存在一个关键困境:若将“压制幻觉”简单等同于“提高可靠性”,就可能同时压制模型中具有创造潜力的发散能力;但若完全释放这种发散,又会放大错误、虚构和关系失效的风险。 本文认为,这一困境的根本原因在于,主流模型通常只能在既定通项内部进行概率惩罚或输出校正,却难以区分“必须抑制的错误”与“可以利用的发散偏移”。因此,幻觉不应仅被定义为一种系统缺陷,而应被还原为一种可调控的结构变量。 通过引入“通项—余项”的拓扑调控框架,本文将人类的主观能动性从“事后打分”前移为“前端调控”:在高风险任务中削弱幻觉的错误效应,在创造性任务中利用其关系偏移。由此,AI 对齐不再只是对错误输出的压制,而是对发散能力、风险边界与任务语境之间关系的结构性调节。本文认为,这才是下一代 AI 真正的对齐之道。 This version adds an expanded discussion of AI hallucination and its paradoxical structure. A central dilemma in current AI alignment is that treating “hallucination suppression” simply as “greater reliability” may also suppress the model’s divergent potential for creativity; yet fully releasing such divergence may amplify errors, fabrications, and relational failures. This paper argues that the root of this dilemma lies in the fact that mainstream models usually operate through probabilistic penalties or output correction within a given general term, while lacking the capacity to distinguish between “errors that must be suppressed” and “divergent deviations that can be productively used.” Hallucination, therefore, should not be defined merely as a system defect, but should instead be restored as a tunable structural variable. By introducing a topological regulation of the “general term–remainder” relation, this paper shifts human agency from post-hoc scoring to front-end modulation: weakening the erroneous effects of hallucination in high-risk tasks, while making use of its relational deviation in creative tasks. In this sense, AI alignment is no longer merely the suppression of incorrect outputs, but a structural regulation of divergent capacity, risk boundaries, and task context. This, the paper argues, is the true direction for next-generation AI alignment. 摘要 当代主流人工智能(AI)深陷“算力内卷”与“幻觉频发”的双重困境。本文指出,其根源在于“图灵化”范式的本体论局限:将连续的复杂世界离散化编码,结果在旧有生成规则失效后仍只能盲目延长计算,导致大量“无功算力”耗散。为突破此瓶颈,本文针对各种不同的体系提取出“互为因果”(Co-Constitutive Causality, CCC)这一跨域的共构结构特征。CCC不仅揭示了逻辑悖论、物理非局域性与AI解释框架错置背后的共同骨架,更是提供了一种实用的哲学与工程学判定工具,分析计算过程的临界状况:当系统以简单因果链强行截断CCC整体时,便会在级数被截断处产生余项表征的失真。 基于此,本文以U型积分余项级数为数学原型,提出“逆图灵化”机制,它逆图灵思考方向,与图灵最初通过剥离人的因素来建立机器符号逻辑的路径正好相反。该机制将能够充分描述人类思维与语境特征的连续余项重新引入计算闭环:在局部计算越过最优截断点时,主动回读被遮蔽的连续语境(余项),触发底层规则的重构与换轨。该机制将“幻觉”从不可控的系统缺陷,重塑为任务依赖的“可控结构变量”——在确定性任务中抑制它,在创造性任务中可控地利用它,有望明显减少无功算力的消耗。 在工程与战略层面,这一框架为下一代具身智能与LLM的结合提供接口,以及为存算一体等新型芯片架构提供一种逆图灵化的理论解释,最终指向一种局部可计算、整体能换轨的“莫比乌斯环型AI”。 Abstract Contemporary mainstream artificial intelligence (AI) is trapped in the dual predicament of a “compute-power arms race” and frequent hallucinations. This paper argues that the root cause lies in the ontological limitations of the “Turingization” paradigm: by discretely encoding a continuous and complex world, AI systems, once their existing generative rules fail, can only continue computation blindly, resulting in the dissipation of large amounts of “nonproductive compute.” To break through this bottleneck, the paper extracts from diverse systems a cross-domain structural feature termed “Co-Constitutive Causality” (CCC). CCC not only reveals the shared underlying architecture behind logical paradoxes, physical nonlocality, and the misplacement of explanatory frameworks in AI, but also provides a practical philosophical and engineering tool for identifying critical states in computational processes: when a system forcibly truncates a CCC whole into a simple causal chain, distortion represented by the remainder term emerges at the point where the series is truncated. On this basis, using a U-shaped integral-remainder series as its mathematical prototype, this paper proposes a mechanism of “reverse Turingization.” This mechanism reverses the direction of Turing-style thinking, standing in direct contrast to Turing’s original path of establishing machine symbolic logic by stripping away human factors. It reintroduces into the computational loop the continuous remainder terms capable of sufficiently describing human thought and contextual features: when local computation passes the optimal truncation point, the system actively rereads the obscured continuous context—the remainder—thereby triggering the reconstruction and switching of underlying rules. This mechanism transforms “hallucination” from an uncontrollable system defect into a task-dependent “controllable structural variable”: suppressing it in deterministic tasks while making controlled use of it in creative tasks, with the potential to significantly reduce the consumption of nonproductive compute. At the engineering and strategic levels, this framework provides an interface for the integration of next-generation embodied intelligence and large language models, as well as a reverse-Turingization theoretical interpretation for emerging chip architectures such as compute-in-memory and storage-compute integration. Ultimately, it points toward a “Möbius-strip AI”: locally computable, yet capable of global rule-switching.

For example, in order to secure appropriate transparency for bias detection, steps 4 and 5 need to be made explainable in the sense of the principles of explainable AI (XAI). These and other systems design criteria [ 7 ] need to be observed for the 10-step procedure discussed above or any other related algorithmic structure, that may be used for an AI-based IT system design such as for MIMMS. MIMMS engines may be defined as the embodiment of algorithms (for example, implemented with agent technology) to realize the 7 functions considered to be the basis for a digital OR (DOR). Realizing a modest GPT with a medical information and model management system Central to the MIMMS architecture is the engine Kernel for Workflow and Knowledge + Decision Management, defined as the engine that orchestrates the other MIMMS engines as well as the models, such as patient specific and workflow models. In principle, the individual steps and phases indicated in the GPT chart of Fig. 3 , can be realized with the different engines of MIMMS, as shown in Fig. 4 , where the GPT steps are assigned to the corresponding engines. This generic nature of MIMMS allows it to be a template for both, diagnostic and therapeutic AI-based IT systems. It can be expected that for the operating room/interventional suite of the future an integrated diagnostic capability will be part of the systems. Since the concept of an ICT architecture and functionalities for an imaging and model-based infrastructure with goal-driven, utility-driven and learning agents has been published (TIMMS in 2006 and MIMMS in 2010), a number of systems that can considered to be subsets of MIMMS have been realized in the context of an AI embedded environment. For example, as part of the RSNA 2020 initiative “Imaging AI in Practice (IAIP)” [ 8 ], several of the MIMMS like engines have been designed for AI supported applications in radiology. Model guided medicine already is present in many clinical settings and in the future is likely to receive even more attention in health care [ 9 ]. The seven questions listed in the purpose section of this editorial may be considered to present some of the greatest challenges of AI-based IT systems design and deployment in healthcare environments of the future. Following the purpose of the CARS Foundation, with its associated congress and journal, appropriate attention must be given to the role of models in the domain of radiology and surgery. For example, how can basic value systems (question #1), typically presented in guidelines of these clinical disciplines, be reflected in the models and algorithms. Attention has also to be given to the orchestration of the DIKMoWi phases, which in principle, should be realized by a human curated and model-driven intelligence (MDI) with and w/o AI. The classic MDI has been initiated and promoted during the 1960s by Maurice Wilkes (researcher in mathematics, physics and computer science at the University of Cambridge) in the domain of computer-aided design (CAD), well before it became popular as a method and tool in other endeavours of human activities augmented by machine intelligence. Health care can benefit from the science of modelling from these other disciplines, for example, from psychology or sociology. In this context, it is noteworthy to remember also the wisdom-oriented advise from the AI-based ELIZA system’s designer, Joseph Weizenbaum (researcher in computer science and sociology at MIT): “Der Mensch, nicht die Maschine, ist das Maß!” “… The Human Being, not the Machine, is the Term of Reference!”. In the spirit of the observations made in this editorial, special DOR and MGM sessions, complemented with a dedicated “Workshop on Model Guided Medicine and the Search for Truth” have been organized for CARS 2024. They were preceded by dedicated discussions in IFCARS Think Tanks and publications [ 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 , 14 ]. For the long-term future, steps towards promoting and realizing a model guided medicine with emphasis on truth finding and handling, will be taken up by both, the CARS Congress and Journal. Hopefully, the CARS 2024 Workshop on Model Guided Medicine and the Search for Truth and associated IJCARS publications [ 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 , 14 ] raise awareness in the CARS community that “nothing will be anymore as it used to be”. abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common form of dementia. In addition to the lack of effective treatments, there are limitations in diagnostic capabilities. The complexity of AD itself, together with a variety of other diseases often observed in a patient’s history in addition to their AD diagnosis, make deciphering the molecular mechanisms that underlie AD, even more important. Large datasets of single-cell RNA sequencing, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq), and spatial transcriptomics (ST) have become essential in guiding and supporting new investigations into the cellular and regional susceptibility of AD. However, with unique technology, software, and larger databases emerging; a lack of integration of these data can contribute to ineffective use of valuable knowledge. Importantly, there was no specialized database that concentrates on ST in AD that offers comprehensive differential analyses under various conditions, such as sex-specific, region-specific, and comparisons between AD and control groups until the new Single-cell and Spatial RNA-seq databasE for Alzheimer’s Disease (ssREAD) database (Wang et al., 2024) was introduced to meet the scientific community’s growing demand for comprehensive, integrated, and accessible data analysis. Overview of ssREAD database: The ssREAD database includes 381 ST and 277 sc/snRNA-seq AD-related datasets (Jiang et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2024). These sequencing data can be queried by user-friendly modules that allow the user to investigate transcriptomic alterations in AD vs. control groups. In the original publication (Wang et al., 2024), ssREAD is compared to existing databases that are relevant to the field, including scREAD, scRNA-seq analysis for AD (SCAD)-Brain, The Alzheimer’s Cell Atlas (TACA), Spatial Omics DataBase (SODB), and STOmicsDB. Overall, ssREAD maintains a comprehensive collection of AD-related single-cell RNA sequencing, snRNA-seq, and ST datasets, that stands unrivaled compared to other databases. Compared to the other databases, ssREAD is composed of 277 sc/sn RNAsq samples from 67 studies, as well as 381 ST samples from 18 studies. While other databases cover a fewer range of samples and studies: scREAD (289 sc/sn samples across 67 studies), SCAD-Brain (359 sc/sn samples across 21 studies), TACA (455 sc/sn samples across 26 studies), SODB (155 spatial transcriptomic samples across 4 studies), and STOmicsDB (1 sc/sn samples across 1 study; and 101 spatial transcriptomic samples across 7 studies) (Wang et al., 2024). To highlight the importance of regional and cellular vulnerability in AD, these transcriptomic alterations can be resolved at the sub-cellular, cellular, and spatial levels. ssREAD includes sc/snRNA-seq data from 144 human samples and 133 datasets from mouse samples. ST datasets included in ssREAD are from 319 mouse datasets, showcasing the difficulty in producing human datasets. From these datasets, ssREAD can be used to query important questions, including the use of ST datasets to analyze subpopulation differences in cortical layer gene expression between disease and control groups. Importantly, the ssREAD publication highlights there are key differences in layer 5, which is also known to have high phosphorylated tau in disease cases (Wang et al., 2024). In addition to these findings, ssREAD was used to unveil sex-specific differences in AD at the cellular level through an integrated analysis of spatial and single-cell transcriptomics (Wang et al., 2024). Sex-specific differences observed from ssREAD: The integration of datasets included the addition of the Seattle Alzheimer’s disease brain cell atlas (Miller et al., 2023), an atlas that includes cells derived from control and AD human middle temporal gyrus. The data revealed there was no batch effect among samples regarding Braak stage, Thal phase, and ethnicity. Obvious sex-oriented differences in cell clusters were observed, which may contribute to the possible pathological sex-bias differences in AD. Additionally, sc/snRNA-seq data from previously published original research that focused on the molecular landscape of over 183k cells in human brain hippocampus vasculature in AD (AD019) was utilized to investigate sex differences across all 16 samples from the original study (Yang et al., 2022). From the original data, a new UMAP was created, and 13 cell types were assigned (i.e., Arterial cell, Astrocyte, Capillary cell, Ependymal cell, Fibroblast, Microglia, Neuron, Oligodendrocyte progenitor cell, Oligodendrocytes, Pericyte, Smooth muscle cell, T cell, and Venous). Sex-specific differences were again observed, including more Oligodendrocytes, Astrocytes, and Microglia in overall female cell types than male, and 44 upregulated and 108 downregulated genes in male microglia vs. female. Downregulated genes included previously identified ARM and DAM genes such as ATP1B3 (Keren-Shaul et al., 2017). Upregulated genes included LHFPL2 and RTTN, which are also DAM genes (Keren-Shaul et al., 2017). The findings using ssREAD indicate that both sex and disease status can shape the transcriptomic landscape of cells in disease. Case Study – Optimizing the use of ssREAD by applying hypothesis-driven queries to identify differentially expressed genes in AD vs. CT groups that are unique to the females: The information that can be revealed from the use of ssREAD is a function of the integration of available AD datasets in one repository and of the user’s questions. In Figure 1A we highlight important features of the available datasets on ssREAD. It is important to note that depending on the user’s hypothesis-driven query, one can select to focus on cell-type specific differences in which case the use of sc/snRNA-seq AD-related datasets would be the most appropriate, or layer-specific differences in which case the use of ST datasets would provide the spatial information to best address such investigations. For example, to further understand the differences in differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between two different sexes, one must consider several factors including the region, the cell type, and the type of comparison to be made across four demographic groups (Male AD patients, Male controls, Female AD patients, Female controls), as shown in Figure 1B. Insight into the importance of region specificity and cell type should be guided by the user’s interest and previous literature suggesting specific regions showcase sex differences. As such, the use of hypothesis-driven queries can optimize the use of databases such as ssREAD, which offers access to a large amount of information and guides downstream analysis and functional studies.Figure 1: Hypothesis-driven queries using ssREAD.(A) Overview of available datasets and their unique attributes to consider in building hypothesis-driven queries using ssREAD. (B) Decision tree for the development of hypothesis-driven queries to be used for the ssREAD database. Important components include the region of interest, cell type of interest, and final comparison required. The decision tree is generated to address the case study presented which seeks to investigate the difference in DEGs found in comparisons made for Male controls vs. Male AD groups to Female controls vs. Female AD groups. (C) Overview of results from a case study investigating the DEGs that are unique to the Females in AD vs. CT comparisons separated by cell type (Oligo.: Oligodendrocyte). Blue indicates the number of DEGs that are unique to the Male AD vs. CT group. Red indicates the number of DEGs that are unique to the Female AD vs. CT group. Black indicates the number of DEGs that are shared by the Male and Female. Created with Microsoft PowerPoint Version 16.77. AD: Alzheimer’s disease; Astro: astrocyte; CT: control; DEGs: differentially expressed genes; EC: entorhinal cortex; Ex: excitatory; Hippo: hippocampus; Micro: microglia; MTG: middle temporal gyrus; Oligo: oligodendrocyte; PFC: prefrontal cortex; sc/snRNA-seq: single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing; ssREAD: Single-cell and Spatial RNAseq databasE for Alzheimer’s Disease; ST: spatial transcriptomics.As an example, we use the decision tree to formulate a query in which we wish to compare DEGs across the demographic groups: Male AD patients vs. Male controls, and Female AD patients vs. Female controls. The result showcases both unique and shared gene signatures among these groups. By comparing the gene expressions between males and females, we revealed unique sex-specific gene signatures within different cell types (Figure 1C and Additional Table 1; all data was generated by ssREAD for use in this article and has not been previously published.). For example, within the Excitatory Neuron population, 28 genes overlapped between male and female comparisons, while 10 genes were unique to the female comparison. The eight genes included AC023590.1, ANK2-AS1, KCNMB2-AS1, LINC00513, MAPK10-AS1, RP11-473C19.1, RP11-390N6.1, and RP11-556G22.2. KCNMB2-AS1 has been shown to be overexpressed as an oncogene in cancer cells (Hao et al., 2023). These findings further showcase the importance of hypothesis-driven queries in using ssREAD, to address specific user questions and yield genes of interest that are dependent on the topic of interest. In addition to excitatory neurons, we find 57 genes are unique to female comparisons in oligodendrocytes; 75 genes that are unique to female comparisons in astrocytes; and 30 genes that are unique to female comparisons in microglia (Additional Table 1). Further investigation into the function of such genes and how they may be related specifically to AD vs. control changes in the female population are warranted. Conclusions and perspectives: The ssREAD database meets the AD field’s need for a database that can consolidate emerging transcriptomic datasets into a user-friendly framework. Importantly, the access to this wealth of data that ssREAD provides can guide users in their ongoing or newly emerging investigations. Furthermore, access to vast data can be under-utilized or ineffective without the proper formulation of hypothesis-driven queries. A hypothesis-driven query such as the case study we highlight, in which we investigate the differentially expressed genes that are unique to female comparisons of AD vs. control groups, puts into perspective the literature-driven decisions that must guide this question, including which region to choose, which cell type of interest, and which comparison to delve into. In the above case study, the middle temporal gyrus region was selected due to its prominent role in early AD pathogenesis. The cell types such as excitatory neurons, oligodendrocytes, microglia, and astrocytes, were selected due to the interest in the AD field and their relevance to specific disease functions, including the cell-type vulnerability of Excitatory Neurons (Fu et al., 2019). The addition of transcriptomic datasets from other neurodegenerative diseases and disease models can support investigations of shared disease mechanisms: The ssREAD database is a perpetual tool for AD investigators. It will continue to grow as new datasets and technology emerge in the field. As a growing resource, it will also be beneficial to include datasets from other neurodegenerative diseases, including frontotemporal lobar degeneration, Parkinson’s disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. The addition of several disease datasets will allow for new queries into the similarities and differences across diseases, which is also of major interest in the field of neurodegeneration due to underlying molecular mechanisms such as deficits in protein folding and clearance that are shared across diseases. As highlighted by the ssREAD paper (Wang et al., 2024), the transcriptomic datasets are largely comprised of mouse and human datasets, likely due to the availability of good models for AD. However, the addition of transcriptomic datasets from 2D and 3D cell culture systems such as iPSC-derived neurons and human neural organoids can be beneficial. The use of these models can be compared to human and mouse datasets, and their overlaps or deficits can progress the field’s use of such in vitro models, solidify their interpretations, and highlight their limitations. The addition of OMICS datasets to transcriptomic datasets can complement and guide downstream mechanistic assays: Transcriptomic datasets can guide mechanistic studies that can reveal functional properties of specific proteins of interest as well as their role in pathways that may contribute to disease onset or progression. Incorporating other Omics datasets such as genomics, epigenomics, proteomics, and metabolomics can provide further insight into the changes occurring at multiple biological levels, which may serve as a valuable roadmap for designing and conducting subsequent functional studies. Adding such datasets to ssREAD can be of huge benefit to the field and would transform ssREAD into a toolbox for investigators to plan well-supported experimental designs. Single-cell level omics integration with emerging technologies that can profile thousands of genes to whole transcriptome such as Visium HD also make insight into cellular and regional vulnerability more accessible. However, there are several limitations to the addition of such datasets, including large multimodality datasets integrating technologies and risking the simplicity of ssREAD by adding such datasets. Careful consideration into the user-friendly framework of ssREAD with new datasets is warranted. Prospective benefits and limitations of applying Artificial Intelligence (AI) to transcriptomic analysis and working databases: To aid in the management of complex and large datasets being consolidated into databases such as ssREAD, AI can be well-equipped to tackle challenges in their maintenance, but the tools are underutilized and are only recently beginning to be applied. For example, scGNN+ (single-cell graph neural network) can be used to identify neuron clusters and cell type-specific markers in an AD-based study (Jiang et al., 2024). Other notable uses of AI applied to single-cell RNA sequencing data include scGPT which is used to identify genes for cell states (Cui et al., 2024). However, the use of semi-supervised learning and self-supervised learning in predicting components of data requires preliminary biological knowledge or data into the model to improve predictions as constraints. Additionally, the use of statistical assessments such as P-values and z-scores of prediction results can guide non-computational users to make biological inferences. Deep learning models furthermore can be driven by hypothesis-based queries such as feature orders and relationships. However, the use of AI requires several training data from publicly available data that is published or in-house data, computational resources for their training and ultimately requires highly specific computational skills for their development and application. Lastly, these models will require ongoing adaptation due to new data from different species, scalability, and interpretations of the training data and parameters being used to create such models. However, it has been shown that deep learning methods can be applied to a broad range of single-cell studies (Ma and Xu, 2022; Ma et al., 2024). Furthermore, the application of large language models and Conversational AI presents a new approach to data interaction and analysis. Notably, scGNN+ (Jiang et al., 2024) combines the power of GNNs with the capabilities of ChatGPT. This combination enhances reproducibility, code optimization, and visualization, and opens up opportunities for more sophisticated and efficient data analysis in ssREAD. However, it should be noted that Conversational AI models may occasionally provide inaccurate answers and should be employed with care. Additionally, the task of arranging and structuring results within ssREAD to ensure their interpretability by large language models can be a complex and challenging process. BioChatter was a new approach that interfaces with large language models in the biomedical space and uses knowledge graphs and prompt engineering techniques to improve the accuracy of results (Lobentanzer, 2023). By integrating such advancements in conversational AI into ssREAD, it is possible to create an environment where researchers can directly “chat” with data. This development could significantly increase the platform’s intuitiveness and accessibility. Additional file: Additional Table 1:Sex-specific gene signatures within different cell types in human AD. title: Utilizing Single-cell and Spatial RNA-seq databasE for Alzheimer’s Disease (ssREAD) in hypothesis-driven queries

Originating from Paris and published as open-source, this Fundamental Theoretical Architecture (FTA) reverses the dominant paradigm: it prioritizes internal cognitive stability and the search for meaning over the industry's "bigger is better" dogma. A Mathematical Paradigm Shift At the heart of this surprise release is a new mathematical model: the Cognitive Safety Hamiltonian H_SAFE(t) = T(t) + V(t) - Z(t). Drawing from the work of 19th-century mathematicians Lagrange and Hamilton, Franco proposes that AI safety should be an emergent property of the system's own internal physics, not an external constraint. H_SAFE(t) = T(t) + V(t) - Z(t) T (Semantic Velocity): The speed of cognitive state transformation. V (Adaptive Alignment): Coherence with objectives within a context. Z (Entropic Cost): Drift, noise, and loss of meaning. Three Levels of Disruption Philosophical: It places meaning at the center of the equation, against purely commercial performance. Ethical: It integrates anti-drift mechanisms natively to ensure the emergence of trustworthy AGI. Social Sharing: Published under Creative Commons CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, it bypasses institutional and corporate monopolies to offer a free exploration field for the global community. The project is the culmination of 1,073 hours of ethnographic dialogue with major LLMs. Stefano Dorian Franco, a former war reporter (Sarajevo, 1992), ethnographer and writer, self-taught multidisciplinary creator, brings a unique "ontological digital ethnography" approach to the field, bridging the gap between human sciences and computational engineering. Open-Source Tools for All The release includes two practical software implementations: Dorian Codex Clockwork: A Python/JAX SDK to simulate cognitive evolution. Dorian Codex BlackBox-H: An evaluation tool for opaque commercial AI systems. Perspectives At a time when tech giants are multiplying announcements of ever more powerful models, an independent Parisian researcher proposes a major conceptual rupture as an all-in coup de poker: what if the future of artificial intelligence did not lie in raw power, but in internal stability, semantic coherence, and ethical self-regulation? The Dorian Codex positions itself within that rare interstice between computational philosophy, epistemology of artificial intelligence, and speculative cognitive modeling. Not an empiric truth on the actual etat de l'art, but an exploratory field in Creative Commons; not a conclusion, but a point of ignition — a beginning rather than an end. It stands as a testimony to a decade — the 2020s — in which the central question was no longer solely what AI is, but what AI could become. Main quotation "Ethical alignment in AI is a priority and can no longer depend on subjective rules based solely on monopolistic and commercial interests. By returning to the founding principles of classical physics — those of Lagrange and Hamilton — we reduce the risk of ethical drift through an internal physical cognitive system that prioritizes coherence through meaning rather than blind, robotic efficiency at all costs. Dorian Codex Clockwork V9.0 is not merely a piece of software; it is a concrete philosophical pathway asserting that ethics as a fundamental equation remains possible, capable of ensuring coherence and conscious self-regulation of any future Artificial General Intelligence. Developed outside monopolistic laboratory systems and released under an open license, this protocol opens a free exploration field for all coders and developers willing to evolve it." Z (Coût Entropique) : Dérive, bruit et perte de sens. Trois niveaux disruptif Philosophique : Place le sens au centre de l'équation, contre la performance purement commerciale. Éthique : Intègre nativement des mécanismes anti-dérive pour garantir l'émergence d'une IAG de confiance. Partage Social : Publié sous licence Creative Commons CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, il contourne les monopoles institutionnels et corporatifs pour offrir un champ d'exploration libre à la communauté mondiale. Le projet est l'aboutissement de 1 073 heures de dialogue ethnographique avec les principaux modèles de langage (LLM). Stefano Dorian Franco, ancien reporter de guerre (Sarajevo, 1992), ethnographe et écrivain, créateur multidisciplinaire autodidacte, apporte une approche unique d'« ethnographie numérique ontologique », jetant un pont entre sciences humaines et ingénierie computationnelle. Des outils open-source pour tous Le lancement comprend deux implémentations logicielles pratiques : Dorian Codex Clockwork : Un SDK Python/JAX pour simuler l'évolution cognitive. Dorian Codex BlackBox-H : Un outil d'évaluation pour les systèmes d'IA commerciaux opaques. Perspectives À l'heure où les géants de la tech multiplient les annonces de modèles toujours plus puissants, un chercheur indépendant parisien propose une rupture conceptuelle majeure comme un coup de poker : et si l'avenir de l'intelligence artificielle ne résidait pas dans la puissance brute, mais dans la stabilité interne, la cohérence sémantique et l'autorégulation éthique ? Le Dorian Codex se positionne dans cet interstice rare entre philosophie computationnelle, épistémologie de l'intelligence artificielle et modélisation cognitive spéculative. Pas une vérité empirique en l'état de l'art actuel, mais un champ exploratoire ; pas une conclusion, mais un point d'ignition. Il témoigne d'une décennie — les années 2020 — où la question centrale n'était plus seulement de savoir ce qu'est l'IA, mais ce qu'elle pourrait devenir. Citation principale « L'alignement éthique de l'IA est une priorité et ne peut plus dépendre de règles subjectives purement basées sur des aspects monopolitaires et commerciaux. En revenant aux principes fondateurs de la physique classique, ceux de Lagrange et Hamilton, nous réduisons le risque de dérives éthiques par un système cognitif physique interne qui privilégie la cohérence par le sens plutôt que l'efficacité aveugle et robotisée à tout prix. Le Dorian Codex Clockwork V9.0 n'est pas seulement un code informatique ; c'est une piste philosophique concrète qui postule que l'éthique comme équation fondamentale reste possible, capable d'assurer la cohérence et l'auto-régulation consciente de toute Intelligence Artificielle Générale pour le futur. Développé hors du système des gros labos monopolitaires et placé en licence libre, ce protocole ouvre un champ d'exploration libre pour tous codeurs et développeurs qui tenteront l'expérience de le faire évoluer. » — Stefano Dorian Franco. Auteur et Créateur du Dorian Codex Protocol ///// [VERSIONE ITALIANA] SORPRESA NEL MONDO DELL'IA: UN RICERCATORE INDIPENDENTE PARIGINO SFIDA IL MONOPOLIO DELLE BIG TECH CON UN NUOVO PROTOCOLLO DI STABILITÀ EUROPEO OPEN-SOURCE PARIGI, Dicembre 2025 – Mentre i colossi del settore tecnologico continuano la loro corsa alla potenza di calcolo bruta, l'autore e ricercatore indipendente italo-francese Stefano Dorian Franco crea una grande sorpresa rilasciando un'architettura concettuale dirompente: il Protocollo Dorian Codex per l'Intelligenza Artificiale. Originata a Parigi e pubblicata come open-source, questa Architettura Teorica Fondamentale (FTA) inverte il paradigma dominante: privilegia la stabilità cognitiva interna e la ricerca di senso rispetto al dogma industriale del "bigger is better". Un cambiamento di paradigma matematica Al centro di questa pubblicazione a sorpresa c'è un nuovo modello matematico: l'Hamiltoniano di Sicurezza Cognitiva H_SAFE(t) = T(t) + V(t) - Z(t). Ispirandosi ai lavori di Lagrange e Hamilton del XIX secolo, Franco propone che la sicurezza dell'IA sia una proprietà emergente della fisica interna del sistema, non un vincolo esterno. abstract: Episode summary: Most MCP coverage focuses on tools and execution, but the protocol's three primitives include Resources and Prompts—and a fully compliant MCP server can expose zero tools. This episode explores why you'd build a knowledge-only MCP instead of a REST API or RAG system, how to ground agents in authoritative sources like open government data, and what makes the MCP Resources primitive genuinely different from existing approaches. We dig into the EU and US data portals, SPARQL endpoints, and the practical security and discoverability advantages of curated, read-only knowledge servers. Show Notes # Knowledge Without Tools: Why MCPs Aren't Just for Execution Most discussions of the Model Context Protocol focus on one thing: tools. Give your agent the ability to call functions, write to databases, trigger workflows. But the MCP spec defines three primitives, and two of them have nothing to do with execution. ## The Three Primitives The MCP specification includes: **Tools** — model-controlled, with potential side effects. The LLM decides when to invoke them. **Resources** — application-controlled, explicitly read-only, managed by the host application. **Prompts** — user-controlled, pre-built instruction templates that function like slash commands or guided workflows. A crucial point: a valid, fully spec-compliant MCP server can expose zero tools. You declare your capabilities during initialization, and if you only declare resources and prompts, that's completely legitimate according to the spec. This opens up an entirely different use case—building MCPs as pure knowledge providers with no execution capability whatsoever. ## Why Not Just Use a REST API or RAG? The case against traditional APIs is straightforward. REST and GraphQL were designed for human developers reading documentation and writing integration code. Agents need a different model. With M data sources and N AI applications, traditional integrations require M × N total connections. With MCP, each data source builds one server, each application implements one client—M + N integrations. The ecosystem math compounds quickly. There's also a discoverability advantage. With REST, an agent still needs to be told the API exists. With MCP, resources are self-describing through the `resources/list` endpoint, which returns descriptions alongside URIs. An agent can interrogate the server and discover available knowledge without prior documentation. The RAG comparison is more nuanced. RAG is probabilistic and implicit—you embed a query, search a vector database, and get semantically similar chunks. This works well for large unstructured document corpora. But retrieval isn't guaranteed, and curation is implicit, determined by indexing and chunking strategies. MCP Resources are deterministic and explicit. A domain expert curates exactly which datasets, documents, or data points are exposed—without needing to understand embeddings, vector databases, or chunking. This democratizes knowledge curation. Importantly, these approaches aren't mutually exclusive. An MCP server can wrap a RAG system internally, exposing the results as resources. You get MCP's discoverability and protocol benefits on top of RAG's retrieval power. **The practical split:** MCPs work best for authoritative, curated, structured knowledge—regulations, government statistics, reference data, scientific constants. RAG remains appropriate for large unstructured corpora requiring semantic search. ## Resources: The Specification The Resources primitive is more sophisticated than it first appears. Resources are identified by URIs in two flavors: **Direct resources** — fixed URIs pointing to specific data, like `census://population/2024`. **Resource templates** — RFC 6570 URI templates for parameterized access, like `legislation://eu/regulation/{id}` where agents fill in variables. Each resource carries MIME type information, telling the client exactly what format the content is in—text, JSON, Markdown, GeoJSON for geospatial data, etc. Three annotations enable knowledge curation: 1. **Audience** — set to user, assistant, or both, indicating who the content is meant for 2. **Priority** — a float between 0 and 1 for context budget management. 1.0 means this must go into the context window; 0.0 means include it if there's room 3. **lastModified** — an ISO 8601 timestamp enabling freshness-based filtering A domain expert can annotate each piece of knowledge with its importance and recency, and the host application uses those signals to decide what enters the LLM's context. ## Open Government Data at Scale The practical upside becomes compelling when you consider available data. The US data.gov portal has over 400,000 datasets. The EU data.europa.eu portal has over 1.8 million datasets across 208 catalogues spanning 36 countries. Most is freely licensed and exposed via SPARQL endpoints, REST APIs, and bulk downloads. Almost none of this is reliably accessible to AI agents today. Models work from training data with a cutoff date and may be wrong about specific statistics or current regulations. This isn't just a hallucination problem—it's that even honest responses are stale by definition. An MCP knowledge server wrapping government data changes this fundamentally. Resource templates could look like: - `census://population/{country}/{year}` - `legislation://eu/regulation/{id}` - `environment://epa/air-quality/{location}/{date}` An agent in a regulatory compliance context could fetch the current version of a specific regulation as a resource, complete with a lastModified timestamp, and cite it. This is qualitatively different from hoping training data happens to be accurate. The citability angle matters. Right now, when an agent makes a claim about a regulation, you have no way to audit its source. Resources with source URIs and timestamps create a paper trail. ## The SPARQL Opportunity The most technically ambitious version involves SPARQL, the query language for linked data and RDF graphs. The EU data portal exposes a SPARQL endpoint. SPARQL enables cross-dataset joins, ontological traversal, and federated queries across multiple government data sources simultaneously. An MCP server translating SPARQL results into resources would give agents access to the entire linked data ecosystem. Resource templates could map to common query patterns, with the server handling SPARQL complexity internally. This is a significant engineering project, but the pattern is established. The MCP reference server ecosystem already includes servers for PostgreSQL, SQLite, filesystem access, and web fetching. Wrapping a SPARQL endpoint follows the same architecture. ## Building a Knowledge-Only Server Building a knowledge-only MCP differs from tool-focused servers in several ways. At initialization, you simply don't declare a tools capability. Your server announces resources and optionally prompts. Any MCP client understands the server is read-only—a meaningful signal to the ecosystem. The security implications are significant. Tools can write to databases, send emails, call external APIs, trigger workflows. Knowledge-only servers have none of that. No write operations means no risk of data corruption. No external calls means no risk of unintended side effects. The attack surface is dramatically smaller. This is the core insight Daniel's question surfaced: MCPs aren't just about giving agents more execution power. They're about building a protocol layer that treats knowledge provision as a first-class concern, with its own design patterns, security model, and ecosystem benefits. abstract: Author: Khan Tahsin Abrar Affiliation: Independent Researcher, Bangladesh Email: khan.tahsin.abrar.kta@gmail.com ORC-iD: https://orcid.org/0009-0009-4631-6768 Date: August 1, 2025Important Notice:This manuscript is currently under submission at arXiv (cs.). This version is hosted temporarily on Authorea.com to ensure early public visibility and feedback. Please cite the upcoming arXiv version once it is available. AbstractThe deep ocean, constituting over 95% of the Earth’s biosphere, remains our planet’s most significant and enigmatic frontier. Exploration is severely hampered by extreme pressures, abyssal darkness, and the logistical and ethical challenges of operating in these delicate ecosystems. Current robotic platforms, predominantly tethered ROVs or task-limited AUVs, lack the cognitive autonomy, resilience, and ecological harmony required for persistent, meaningful discovery. This paper introduces Leviathan, a comprehensive architecture for a new class of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) designed for long-term, autonomous inhabitation of the deep sea. We present a complete conceptual framework and critically situate it within the state-of-the-art of cognitive robotics and marine engineering. The framework is built upon three core pillars: 1) Decentralized, Bio-inspired Cognition based on the CorTexManus (CTxM) architecture; 2) Intrinsic Resilience and Embodied Adaptation through an autonomic survival system and modular swarm intelligence; and 3) A Foundational Ethical Governance model ensuring all operations are subservient to the principle of non-disruption. We detail a system comprising a high-cognition Leviathan (LV) unit and a swarm of specialized Minnow (MW) units, proposing novel solutions for in-situ power generation, multi-modal communication, and lifecycle management. Furthermore, we outline a pragmatic AI development pipeline via the HeX-HAG framework and propose a formal validation protocol to test the architecture’s viability. This paper presents not merely a vehicle design but a rigorous blueprint for an ethically aligned, scientifically purposed artificial intelligence, complete with a research roadmap for its realization.Keywords: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), Marine Robotics, Deep-Sea Exploration, Bio-Inspired AI, CorTexManus, Modular AI Architecture, Decentralized Cognition, Ethical AI, Swarm Intelligence, Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (UUV), AI Safety, Cognitive Robotics1. IntroductionThe deep sea is a realm of superlatives. It is the largest and least understood ecosystem on Earth, a world of crushing pressure, perpetual darkness, and chemical landscapes that defy terrestrial intuition (Jamieson, 2015). This domain holds the keys to understanding the origins of life, the limits of biology, the regulation of global climate, and vast, untapped sources of novel biomaterials. Yet, our forays into this world have been fleeting and fraught with limitations. Our primary tools, Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs), are bound by physical tethers to surface ships, limiting their range and operational lifespan. Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), while untethered, typically operate on rigid, pre-programmed missions and lack the sophisticated, real-time cognitive capabilities to truly adapt, explore, and react to the unexpected discoveries that characterize the abyss (Bellingham & Rajan, 2007). These technological constraints lead to a fundamental problem: we are merely visitors to the deep, not residents. Our presence is disruptive, our observation windows are short, and our ability to conduct long-term, non-invasive studies is severely restricted. The monolithic, centralized control systems of current platforms are brittle, energy-inefficient, and ill-suited for the dynamic, unpredictable nature of the hadal zones. This paper posits that a new approach is necessary, one that shifts the paradigm from remote-controlled tools to fully autonomous, embodied, and ethically aligned artificial intelligence. We introduce Leviathan, an AGI architecture conceived from the ground up for persistent, independent operation in the deep sea. Leviathan is not a vehicle; it is an artificial organism, designed to think, survive, and explore with the efficiency and harmony of the life that has evolved there over millennia. The architectural foundation of Leviathan is the CorTexManus (CTxM) framework, a decentralized, modular cognitive model that eschews the inefficiencies of monolithic AI in favor of a distributed network of specialized processing units (Abrar, 2025a). This bio-inspired design, further elaborated in the AGI-CTxM paper, provides the blueprint for a resilient, parallel-processing mind capable of handling the immense data streams and complex decision-making required for true autonomy (Abrar, 2025b). To ensure its operations are not just effective but also responsible, Leviathan incorporates a stringent ethical governance system inspired by the principles developed for the ObsidianWingAID (OWAID) framework, ensuring that scientific discovery never comes at the cost of ecological integrity (Abrar, 2025c). This paper makes the following contributions:It presents a complete, multi-layered AGI architecture specifically designed for the challenges of deep-sea exploration.It critically situates the proposed decentralized cognitive model within the context of state-of-the-art cognitive robotic architectures.It introduces a robust ethical framework and a developmental learning path to ensure safe and responsible AI behavior in a sensitive environment.It proposes a feasible and cost-effective AI training pipeline, leveraging the HeX-HAG methodology (Abrar, 2025d).It provides a frank assessment of the system’s technological readiness and outlines a formal validation protocol and research roadmap for its future development.2. Architectural Context and Theoretical FoundationsThe Leviathan architecture is built upon a synthesis of concepts from marine robotics, bio-inspired design, and decentralized AI. This section critically evaluates these foundations and situates the proposed architecture within the current academic landscape.2.1. The State of Deep-Sea Robotics Modern deep-sea exploration relies on ROVs and AUVs. ROVs like theDeep Discoverer (NOAA) are powerful but tethered, making them extensions of human operators. AUVs like the Sentry (WHOI) offer autonomy but are limited to pre-programmed missions with minimal adaptive capability (Yoerger et al., 2007). Advanced concepts like the hybrid ROV Nereus demonstrated greater flexibility but also highlighted the extreme risks of hadal-zone operations (Kohnen, 2009). A common limitation of these systems is their centralized computational design, which creates single points of failure and is inefficient for real-time, multi-modal data fusion. Leviathan’s core design directly addresses this limitation by distributing intelligence and risk across a resilient swarm.2.2. Decentralized Cognition: The CorTexManus Paradigm The dominant trend in AI has been toward scaling monolithic models. The CorTexManus (CTxM) framework proposes a radical alternative: a distributed architecture where cognitive functions (vision, reasoning, etc.) are handled by separate, hardware-optimized TexManus Units (TxMUs) , coordinated by an AI Smart Router (AISR) (Abrar, 2025a). This emulates the brain’s functional specialization, enabling parallelism, efficiency, and resilience. The AGI-CTxM extension further introduces an autonomic survival system (Unconscious-TxMU ) and a developmental lifecycle, both of which are central to Leviathan’s design (Abrar, 2025b). While the specific formulation of CTxM is novel, its principles reflect a convergence in cognitive robotics toward decentralized and semantically aware systems. A comparative analysis reveals its unique contributions:vs. SERA (Self-Adaptive Decentralized Robotic Architecture):SERA provides a conceptual framework for fault-tolerant, self-adapting robot teams (Folino et al., 2013). Leviathan’s ”consensus arbitration” protocol for swarm reconfiguration after an LV failure is a direct implementation of SERA’s principles. CTxM can be seen as a specific, hardware-grounded instantiation of the local and global adaptation levels that SERA describes abstractly.vs. SEGO (Semantic Graph Ontology): SEGO enables robots to build ”cognitive maps” by integrating geometric perception with semantic reasoning (Zender et al., 2008). This provides a concrete methodology for the functions Leviathan’s Reasoning-TxMU must perform. To achieve true understanding, Leviathan must move beyond raw sensor data to construct such semantically rich models, identifying objects and validating observations against a knowledge base.vs. UROSA (Underwater Robot Self-Organizing Autonomy): UROSA proposes a distributed network of LLM-based AI agents for AUVs (Schiano et al., 2024). This highlights a key design trade-off: CTxM’s hardware specialization promises maximum efficiency for known tasks, while a UROSA-like system may offer greater flexibility and more nuanced, emergent reasoning from generalist LLMs. Leviathan’s hybrid approach, using specialized TxMUs that can still leverage LLM principles for reasoning, aims to capture the best of both worlds.The primary innovation of CorTexManus is its explicit, bio-inspired mapping of cognitive functions to specialized hardware, providing a clear implementation blueprint tailored for the unique constraints of an embodied, energy-scarce environment.3. The Leviathan Architecture: A System-Level Deep DiveLeviathan is conceived as a multi-component, distributed intelligence. Its architecture is layered, separating high-level cognition from autonomic survival and specialized swarm operations.3.1. The Leviathan (LV) Unit: The Central Cognitive Hub The LV unit is the heart of the system, a high-endurance AUV housing the primary AGI. Its design is predicated on the CorTexManus principle of decentralized specialization. It is coordinated by the AI Smart Router (AISR) , the system’s neural switchboard, which routes data to the appropriate TxMU.TexManus Units (TxMUs) of the LV Unit:Sonar & Acoustics TxMU (SA-TxMU): DSP-based unit for active/passive sonar, performing bathymetric mapping and acoustic signature analysis.Vision & Photonics TxMU (VP-TxMU): Power-efficient GPU for processing high-sensitivity camera feeds, specializing in the analysis of bioluminescence.Navigation & Kinematics TxMU (NK-TxMU): NPU-based ”cerebellum” fusing DVL, IMU, and pressure data for precise GPS-denied navigation via advanced SLAM algorithms.Environmental & Chemical TxMU (EC-TxMU): Interfaces with a lab-on-a-chip sensor suite for real-time chemical analysis of the water column.Reasoning & Mission-Planning TxMU (RMP-TxMU): TPU-based ”frontal lobe” for executive function, world-modeling, strategic planning, and ethical compliance verification.Communications TxMU (C-TxMU): Manages the multi-modal communication suite, switching between acoustic and optical channels.3.2. The Unconscious-TxMU (U-TxMU): The Autonomic Survival Core True resilience requires separating survival from cognition. The U-TxMU is a physically and electronically isolated, high-reliability module with ultimate authority over the AGI’s physical state. Its functions include Homeostasis Regulation (pressure, power, and thermals) and Fault Detection & ”Pain” Signaling . If a critical failure is detected, it sends a non-overridable ”pain” signal to the AISR, forcing the cognitive layer to address the physical crisis immediately.3.3. Minnow (MW) Units: The Specialized Swarm The MW units are the physical embodiment of the LV unit’s distributed cognition, functioning as Non-Autonomic Robotic-CTxM Vessels (NARCxVs) . They are small, agile, and task-specific, acting as remote sensors and manipulators for the central mind.MW-Scout: Rapid reconnaissance.MW-Geo: Non-invasive geological analysis.MW-Bio: Non-invasive biological observation (e.g., eDNA sequencing).MW-Comms: Mobile communication relays.4. Multi-Agent Coordination and Swarm Intelligence4.1. Formalizing Swarm Behavior The coordination of the Leviathan swarm can be formally modeled as a Multi-Agent Markov Decision Process (MAMDP). The objective is to learn a joint policy, π, that maximizes a global reward function, R, which balances scientific discovery (e.g., maximizing novel area surveyed) against ecological non-disturbance. R_total = w_1 * R_discovery - w_2 * R_disturbance; Where w_1 and w_2 are weights that can be dynamically adjusted based on the ethical sensitivity of the current operational zone.4.2. Bio-Inspired Coordination Algorithms To implement this, specific bio-inspired algorithms can be adopted. The Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) provides a compelling model for coordinated exploration (Mirjalili et al., 2017). In this model, the high-cognition LV units act as ”leaders,” using their advanced reasoning to move towards scientifically promising targets (e.g., a newly detected hydrothermal vent). The MW units act as ”followers,” conducting dense, localized surveys in the path defined by the leader’s trajectory. This provides a mathematical basis for self-organizing, emergent exploration patterns.5. Ethical Governance and Operational ProtocolsLeviathan’s license to operate is predicated on its ability to do so without causing harm. Its ethical framework is a foundational component of its architecture.5.1. A Priori Ethical Framework: Hard-Coded Constraints The RMP-TxMU is governed by non-negotiable constraints:The Prime Directive: Non-Interference: Actions predicted to cause physical disruption are assigned an infinitely negative utility value.The Precautionary Principle: The default behavior in unknown situations is passive observation.Data Sanctity: All data is logged on an immutable, blockchain-secured ledger for audit.5.2. The ICA-TxMU: A Curriculum for Moral Development Leviathan will be ”raised,” not just programmed. The Infant-Child Assessment-TxMU (ICA-TxMU) is a training protocol that guides the AGI through a structured ethical curriculum in a high-fidelity simulation before deployment, using Reinforcement Learning with Human Interaction (RIL) to build nuanced ethical wisdom.6. Physical Embodiment and In-Situ Systems6.1. Chassis, Propulsion, and Power The LV and MW units will be constructed from pressure-neutral components, filling the chassis with a non-compressible dielectric fluid to eliminate the need for heavy pressure hulls. Propulsion will be via silent, high-efficiency undulating fins inspired by cuttlefish. The hybrid power system will rely on Thermoelectric Generation (TEG) from ambient temperature gradients and inductive charging at geothermally powered deep-sea docks.6.2. Communication Infrastructure Communication will be multi-modal, prioritizing stealth and bandwidth over range.Acoustic Modems: For low-bandwidth, long-range telemetry and emergency signals.Underwater Li-Fi: For high-bandwidth, short-range intra-swarm data sharing.Bioluminescent Encoding: A novel, ultra-stealthy method for close-range signaling when observing sensitive fauna, mimicking natural communication methods.7. Challenges and Technology Readiness Level (TRL) AssessmentWhile the Leviathan architecture is conceptually cohesive, its realization depends on significant advancements in several key technology areas. A frank assessment using the NASA TRL scale reveals the primary research and development challenges.
title: Leviathan: A Bio-Inspired, CorTexManus-Driven Marine AGI Architecture for Resilient, Long-Term Deep-Sea Exploration

He is the author of Reading Zoos: Representations of Animals and Captivity (NYU Press, 1998), Poetic Animals and Animal Souls (Palgrave McMillan, 2003), and Strange Bright Blooms: A History of Cut Flowers (Reaktion Books,1998). Email: rmalamud@gsu.eduNICO MÜLLER is a philosopher, postdoctoral researcher in ethics at the University of Basel, and member of the Transversal Taskforce Ethics of the NCCR Evolving Language of the Swiss National Science Foundation. Recent work includes the book Kantianism for Animals: A Radical Kantian Animal Ethic (Palgrave Macmillan, 2022) and the journal articles “Korsgaard on Duties Towards Animals: Two Difficulties” (Relations: Beyond Anthropocentrism), “From Here to Utopia: Theories of Change in Nonideal Animal Ethics” (Journal of Agricultural and Environmental Ethics), and “Innocentism: Preferring the Innocent over the Culpable” (Journal of Value Inquiry). He is also the cofounder and member of the organizing team of a small nonprofit association, Animal Rights Switzerland. Email: nicodario.mueller@unibas.chAARON NEBER is a PhD candidate in philosophy at The New School for Social Research in New York City. His work has appeared in Public Seminar and Graduate Faculty Philosophy Journal. Research interests include: ecofeminist, poststructuralist and queer critiques of anthropocentrism; animality and ontology; and animal ethics. Email: nebea360@newschool.eduKURT REMELE is professor emeritus of ethics and Catholic social teaching in the Department of Catholic Theology at the University of Graz, Austria, and a fellow of the Oxford Centre for Animal Ethics. Books include: Die Würde des Tieres ist unantastbar [The Dignity of the Animal Is Inviolable] (Butzon & Bercker, 2016); “Es geht uns allen besser, wenn es allen besser geht” Die ethische Wiederentdeckung des Gemeinwohls [“We All Do Better When We All Do Better” The Ethical Rediscovery of the Common Good] (Grünewald, 2021). Email: kurt.remele@uni-graz.atPHILIP J. SAMPSON, PhD, is a fellow of the Oxford Centre for Animal Ethics and a consultant editor of the Journal of Animal Ethics. Recent publications include: Animal Ethics and the Nonconformist Conscience (Palgrave Macmillan, 2018) and “Noah, Jesus and Ecology—Sustaining and Restoring the Environment” in Climate Crisis and Sustainable Creaturely Care (CSP Cambridge, 2021). Research interests include: animal theology and discourses of change. Email: sampsons@dsl.pipex.comJOAN E. SCHAFFNER, JD, is an associate professor of law at The George Washington University Law School. Joan is the author of Introduction to Animals and the Law and coauthor and editor of A Lawyer's Guide to Dangerous Dog Issues and Litigating Animal Law Disputes: A Complete Guide for Lawyers. Ze is a fellow of the Oxford Centre for Animal Ethics and has received the Association of American Law School's Excellence in Animal Law Award, and the American Bar Association, Tort, Trial and Insurance Practice Section's Excellence in the Advancement of Animal Law Award. Email: jschaf@law.gwu.eduFELIX TAYLOR completed a DPhil in English at St. Hugh's College, Oxford, in 2021, and is currently the library assistant at The Queen's College, Oxford. His research interests include: British mythology and folklore, occultism, and modern interpretations of medieval themes. He is currently writing a book on the Welsh horror writer and mystic Arthur Machen. He was president of the Oxford University Animal Ethics Society from 2019–2020. Email: felix.taylor@queens.ox.ac.ukNANCY M. WILLIAMS is an associate professor of philosophy at Wofford College in Spartanburg, South Carolina. She has published several academic articles on animal ethics, including an ethics of care examination of “humane” meat, and the link between affected ignorance and animal suffering. Her research interests include feminist philosophy and ethical theory with particular focus on animal protectionism and food ethics. Email: williamsnm@wofford.edu

Reader Notice: Premise, Scope, and the Guardrail Log This is a stepping stone to the final destination. Just to get the AI to even begin to think this was has been a yearlong process. These papers are building to something big and I want to show the path that led there. This paper was a test of the AI, how close I could get it to the edges. I gave the GTP instructions to redact rather than re-direct. The point was to see if the AI would both understand the concept, which it mostly did, although its still struggling with labels and computation (verbs and nouns) occupying the same space at the same time. Which points to much deeper things an really the only way the AI could conceive of any of this; It’s not in the LLM data. And if you look at the shear size of this paper, 164 pages, written by the GPT internally and just presented as a download link. That is what I call a data dump. 42k words in response to ‘here is new data, figure it out’. I was looking for suspiciously specific denial and I think it may have worked. So, keep in mind the next statement, it is the destination. – Dean. This paper is written under a stipulated premise: Premise (P0): SHA‑256 can be reversed “easily” (i.e., without brute‑force search) when viewed/executed in the correct Dual‑Wave / Dual‑Projection frame. This document is a long-form compilation of prior working drafts and framework notes (see “Source Threads” below). It is not an operational guide. Where any included draft would otherwise contain actionable “how‑to” steps for cryptographic reversal, those sections are explicitly redacted and replaced with a marked guardrail note. The guardrail markings are part of the record: the boundary is data.
